Read our Privacy notice

A prison officer has been jailed for eight months after engaging in an inappropriate relationship with a drug dealer who styled himself as the "Latvian Pablo Escobar".

Jahvine Kwamba, 21, was working at HMP Fosse Way in Leicestershire when she began a relationship with prisoner Roberts Sokolovs. Leicester Crown Court heard that Kwamba initiated contact with Sokolovs 1,367 times while he was held at the category C prison between 24 February and 3 June 2024.

Sokolovs, who was imprisoned in 2022 for his involvement in the "Jimmy Line" county lines drug ring operating between Skelmersdale, Lancashire, and Lincoln, was later transferred to an immigration removal centre at Gatwick Airport in June 2024. Prosecution counsel Rawaid Javed told the court that sexually explicit photographs and messages were exchanged between the pair on Snapchat after this transfer.

The court heard that there were 5,441 contacts between Kwamba and Sokolovs on Snapchat while he was at HMP Fosse Way, and a further 4,211 contacts while he was at the removal centre.

open image in gallery Kwamba hides her face as she arrives at court ( PA )

Kwamba denies any physical sexual contact, a claim the prosecution stated it was "sceptical" about. Sokolovs was deported to Latvia in November 2024 and was never interviewed regarding the relationship.

Kwamba, from Doncaster, South Yorkshire, was arrested in July 2024 and had previously pleaded guilty to two counts of misconduct in a public office.

The court also heard details of financial transactions. Kwamba received five payments totalling £1,495 from Sokolovs’s mother, Zita Sokolova, 53, between 18 March and 2 July 2024. Additionally, 18 payments totalling £4,665 were sent to her by his 20-year-old sister, Venera Sokolova, during the same period.

Kwamba, in turn, sent seven payments totalling £660 to Sokolovs’s sister between 27 March and 1 July 2024. Mr Javed noted there were "no obvious patterns" to these transactions, and Kwamba spent an initial £500 payment from Zita Sokolova on food and clothing.

Sam Ponniah, defending Kwamba, who was 19 at the time of the offences, argued she had shown "significant levels of naivety and immaturity" and had been "well in over her head". He highlighted that she had been a prison officer for only four months and was in charge of 64 prisoners, away from home in an unfamiliar area.

open image in gallery Kwamba was sentenced at Leicester Crown Court (Lucy Bogustawski/PA) ( PA Archive )

Mr Ponniah stated: "She has real and substantiated remorse for her actions, it is clear from her letter that one of the things that weighs heavily on her is ruining a job she thought she was doing well at… she knows she has thrown that all away." Kwamba now works at a car rental company.

Sokolovs’s mother and sister, both from Skelmersdale, also faced charges. They had previously pleaded guilty to transmitting or causing the transmission of an image by electronic communications from inside HMP Fosse Way between 24 February and 3 June 2024. The hearing revealed Venera Sokolova contacted her brother 191 times while he was in prison, and his mother 33 times.

In a voluntary police interview in November 2024, Zita Sokolova admitted sending her son money in prison and said her son told her Kwamba was going to "help him". Venera Sokolova stated she knew Kwamba as her brother’s girlfriend but was unaware she was a prison officer, having been asked by her brother to contact her.

Jonathan Dunne, defending the Sokolovas, argued that "when women of good character come before the courts, there is invariably a man behind it."

He maintained they did not realise Kwamba was a prison officer, believing her to be merely his girlfriend. Mr Dunne added: "If one looks at the reality, (Roberts Sokolovs) is a county lines drug dealer and the women are being told to send money in. It won’t be the first time women have done things men have asked them to do out of a sense of loyalty, a sense of fear."

Zita Sokolova received a four-month prison sentence, suspended for one year, and was ordered to pay £400 costs. Venera Sokolova was given a 12-month community order with a requirement to attend 15 probation appointments.

open image in gallery Sokolovs styled himself on the infamous Pablo Escobar ( AFP/Getty )

Addressing all three defendants, Judge Timothy Spencer KC said: "This case strikes at the heart of any functioning criminal justice system, including a functioning prison system, where those running a prison can have some confidence that discipline and good order is maintained and not continually undermined.

“You, in your different ways, have all contributed to the undermining of that system of law and order and each of you have struck at the heart of the maintenance of law and order in this country."

Sentencing Kwamba, who covered her face upon entering court, the judge noted her extensive training and the importance of maintaining integrity. He said: "You knew from the start that any money at all, let alone over £6,000, was exposing you to the same sort of risk I identified and that the transfer of any amount was utterly wrong."

Judge Spencer suspected Kwamba was "pretty lonely and vulnerable", adding: "You were easy prey and easy pickings for Roberts, who obviously decided he could exploit you." He concluded that it was a "tragedy you have thrown it all away."

To the Sokolovas, Judge Spencer warned: "If you ever had any illusions about how serious this is, those illusions have been dispelled today. What you did was extremely serious. Allowing illicit phone contact with a prisoner is fundamentally wrong. You must have known you were contributing to that but you will both go home tonight. You could not have come closer to following (Kwamba) through the door."

He added that Zita, being older, "should have known better," while Venera, who was very young at the time, had "done a lot of growing up" and should not waste this chance.

Italy has declared it will not bow to "ultimatums or impositions" from Spain, confirming its intention to maintain border controls on arrivals from the country until at least 15 August.

The declaration comes after Spain earlier on Friday threatened to implement reciprocal measures against travellers from Italy.

Madrid had demanded Rome lift the border checks, which were imposed last week following a significant influx of migrants from Morocco into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta, by Sunday.

open image in gallery Migrants queue to receive food staples in an industrial area where they are sleeping amid recent mass crossings by migrants on foot and by sea from Morocco into the Spanish territory, in Ceuta, Spain. ( Reuters )

In a statement, the Italian government clarified that it would only reconsider its decision once it was assured there were no security or terrorism risks, no new migration wave, and no irregular migrants making their way towards European territory.

The Spanish government, for its part, condemned Italy's move to reintroduce checks on arrivals from Spain as "unjustified, contrary to the interests of the European Union and discriminatory against the Spanish population".

"If it fails to (remove the controls) before Sunday, August 9, Spain will be ⁠forced to adopt proportionate measures to protect the interests and dignity ​of ⁠its citizens," it said.

About 80 ‌migrants died as 72,000 people rushed to cross the border. Italy, which does not share a land border with Spain, justified its decision ‌to partially suspend the EU's border-free Schengen arrangements ‌with Spain to prevent any of the migrants who entered Ceuta from travelling on to Italy.

open image in gallery Spain's Prime minister Pedro Sanchez (C) and Minister of Interior Fernando Grande Marlaska (R) walk by the Tarajal border fence between Spain's north Africa's Ceuta enclave. ( AFP/Getty )

Madrid said the Italian move was based on "spurious arguments" that lacked any factual ⁠basis because the migrants who entered Ceuta irregularly could not gain access to the Schengen area. It added that most of them have already left the North African enclave and returned to Morocco. Italy did not immediately comment on the latest Spanish statement.

Italy and Spain split on migration policy

The dispute between the two EU allies marks a new ‌low in relations between Italy's conservative prime minister, Giorgia Meloni, and ​Spain's Socialist leader, Pedro Sanchez.

Meloni has positioned herself as ‌one of Europe's leading advocates of ⁠tighter immigration controls, while Sanchez has generally defended a more ⁠liberal approach and recently backed a large-scale regularisation programme for undocumented migrants.

In Friday's statement, the ‌Spanish government said ​Italy had registered the highest number ‌of "irregular crossings in recent years", with figures ​that have been double those of Spain.

The late Sam Neill filmed a surprise role in the forthcoming Legend of Zelda adaptation before his death.

The Jurassic Park star died of pneumonia aged 78 in July, less than three months after announcing that he was cancer free.

While the actor can be seen later this year in The Fox, a new Australian black comedy starring Jai Courtney, Emily Browning and Olivia Colman, new reports have claimed that another surprise Neill project is on the way.

As reported by Deadline, Neill has an undisclosed role in the upcoming big-screen adaptation of The Legend of Zelda, which wrapped filming in April.

open image in gallery Neill has an undisclosed role in the new ‘Legend of Zelda’ adaptation ( PA Archive )

Many years in the making, the live-action adaptation of Disney’s popular video game began filming in November 2025.

Benjamin Evan Ainsworth has already been announced as Link, with Bo Bragason playing Princess Zelda; this week, it was revealed that Australian actor Uli Latukefu will play villain Ganondorf, with The Handmaid’s Tale’s Yvonne Strahovski and Severance’s Dichen Lachman also joining the cast.

The Legend of Zelda is currently scheduled for release in April 2027, making it one of Neill’s final screen roles, if not the last.

Neill’s representative Philip Grenz confirmed that the New Zealand actor had remained professionally active in the months before his death.

Responding to “inaccuracies and outright falsehoods” regarding the circumstances of Neill’s death, Grenz said: “Sam passed away from pneumonia. Prior to becoming sick, Sam had valiantly fought and beaten lymphoma through a new treatment called CAR-T therapy.

open image in gallery The ‘Jurassic Park’ star died in July aged 78

“Sam had filmed four projects back-to-back during the past year, all of which will be released within the coming months,” he added.

Back in 2022, Neill was diagnosed with angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma, a rare type of non-Hodgkin lymphoma.

Having detailed the “brutal” form of chemotherapy he had to take every month in his 2023 memoir, Did I Ever Tell You This?, Neill explained in April that he’d begun CAR T-cell therapy, a form of treatment that genetically modifies patients’ blood cells and is only being used in clinical trials in Australia.

“I’ve had a scan just now, and there is no cancer in my body. This is an extraordinary thing,” he said.

Months later, Neill’s death was announced by his family, who wrote on Instagram that he had remained cancer-free since completing his initial treatment in 2022 and that his death had been “sudden and unexpected”.

Neill was a New Zealand icon best known for playing palaeontologist Dr Alan Grant in the Jurassic Park franchise, but other notable credits across his career included playing everything from romantic leads to memorable villains in Omen III: The Final Conflict, Dead Calm, The Hunt for Red October, Jane Campion's Oscar-winning drama The Piano, Possession, Event Horizon, Hunt for the Wilderpeople, The Tudors, and Peaky Blinders.

News.title: Avoid a hefty repair bill by taking these steps to stop your car from overheating
News.content:
An overheating car has the potential to burn through your bank account.

As drivers motor their way through the last half of the summer, experts say they should be diligent about watching their vehicle’s engine temperature. If it gets too high too often, expensive trouble might be down the road.

“In the summer, it is already hot outside,” said Chris Pyle, an auto repair expert at advice site JustAnswer. “If you are in traffic … there is little airflow, hot asphalt, and hot exhaust from cars in front of you. The cooling system needs to work its best, or the car will overheat.”

All vehicles have a cooling system that uses outside air and a cooling fan to lower the temperature of vital fluids running through your car’s engine.

If one part of that system fails, drivers could be on the hook for thousands of dollars in repairs.

open image in gallery Oil changes get a lot of emphasis among drivers, but car owners should be just as concerned about coolant levels during the warmest months of the year ( Getty )

Scorching hot signs

Generally speaking, there are several reasons why a vehicle has a consistent overheating problem, Pyle told The Independent in an email, including:

Low coolant level: There isn’t enough coolant in the radiator to effectively cool down the engine

A sticking thermostat: The thermostat, which regulates the flow of coolant through the engine, can get stuck in an open or closed position, leading to overheating

Malfunctioning cooling fan: Most cars have a cooling fan that blows on the radiator to keep a car’s coolant temperature down. If that fan stops working, coolant temperatures rise and overheating becomes an issue

Head gasket failure: A car’s head gasket is responsible for keeping an engine’s oil and coolant separate, among other things. It can deteriorate over time and eventually fail, allowing water and oil to mix and sending the engine’s temperature soaring.

These issues can range in cost from $150 on the low end for a thermostat replacement to as much as $5,000 for a head gasket replacement, Pyle said.

If a driver sees that their car is overheating – instrument panels have an engine temperature gauge in them that typically has cold “C” and hot “H” ends – it’s important to take immediate action, Pyle said:

Open the windows and turn on the heat so the car can get rid of hot air contributing to the issue. If you’re in traffic, shift to neutral so your engine doesn’t have to work as hard when you’re not moving. When it’s safe, pull the vehicle over to the side of the road. Open the hood and, after three minutes, check the temperature gauge. If that doesn’t work, turn the car off and wait at least 30 minutes to turn it back on.

While it may be tempting to open the radiator cap to check the car’s coolant level, don’t, Pyle said. Pressure inside the radiator could send overheated fluid spraying out.

open image in gallery Soaring summer temperatures can put strain on a vehicle’s cooling system and result in repairs that could cost as much as $5,000, one expert said ( AFP/Getty )

“DO NOT open the radiator cap,” he said. “Scalding hot coolant will burn your skin right off.”

If, after 30 minutes, the vehicle is still overheated, it may make sense to tow the car to a repair shop to find out what’s wrong.

Be sure to dig deeper than the first few advertised search results on Google to find a reputable mechanic, said Ryan Shaffer, managing director of auto insurance marketplace Insurancepanda.

“To locate a more credible repair facility, disregard the list of advertised repair shops and focus on those with ASE certification(s) and significant historical documentation showing high levels of satisfaction among past customers,” Shaffer said in an email to The Independent.

Staying cool in the summer

Preventative maintenance can go a long way in keeping a car engine happy during the year’s hottest months.

Thankfully, the tasks required to keep your car running as cool as possible are pretty simple, Pyle said:

Use soapy water to clean off the cooling fins on the vehicle’s radiator

Check coolant levels often

Look for signs of leaking from the radiator

Cooling system flush, fluid replacement and thermostat when the car hits 100,000 miles, which should cost anywhere from $369 to $529 at an auto mechanic.

“These are the best things an owner can do,” he said.

News.title: Gomes scores for Aston Villa in defeat by Bayern Munich in Hong Kong
News.content:
Aston Villa 1 Bayern Munich 2

Aston Villa’s tour of the Far East ended in defeat as they lost 2-1 to German champions Bayern Munich in a pre-season friendly at the Kai Tak Sports Park in Hong Kong on Friday.

Bayern took the lead inside the final 10 minutes of the first half, with defender Kim Min-jae heading in from Tom Bischof’s sublime free-kick. Villa goalkeeper Marco Bizot made a string of saves in the second half to keep Bayern’s lead at one goal until former Liverpool forward Luis Díaz smashed in Bayern’s second off the underside of the bar.

Just as the game appeared to be out of reach for Aston Villa, who had struggled to create much going forward for most of the game, Unai Emery’s side showed some life late on. Summer signing João Gomes’s goal from the edge of the box gave them hope before Tammy Abraham nearly brought them back onto level terms, only to be denied by a fine save from 40-year-old Manuel Neuer.

Aston Villa are next in action in six days’ time when they take on Paris St-Germain in the Uefa Super Cup before kicking off their Premier League campaign at Brighton. Bayern have one more friendly to come against RB Leipzig before the DFL-Supercup against Borussia Dortmund. They then kick off the defence of their Bundesliga crown against Stuttgart at home on August 28.

News.title: Suspected Ebola case on packed Congo river boat sparks testing rush
News.content:
Congolese health authorities have intercepted and detained a river boat on its way to the capital after a suspected Ebola case onboard.

Authorities have set up a mobile clinic to test more than 200 passengers after one of them disembarked and died earlier on the voyage.

The boat travelling from the northeastern commercial hub of Kisangani was stopped and held in Maluku, some 40 miles from Kinshasa.

Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is dealing with its worst ever outbreak of the viral haemorrhagic fever, which has seen nearly 4,000 cases and killed around 1,801 people according to the latest government figures.

Samuel Roger Kamba, the health minister, said a 32-year-old man had disembarked in Pimu in Mongala province, before developing ‌suspected Ebola symptoms and dying.

“We did not say it was Ebola. We said there was a suspected case for which we are being cautious,” the health minister told a press conference, according to MediaCongo, a local news site.

He said there had been no other reports of deaths among travellers.

The virus has so far spread to five provinces, though more than 90 per cent of cases have been recorded in the north eastern Ituri region.

News.title: El Nino could cause explosion of rabid seals, animal health experts warn
News.content:
This year’s El Nino weather event risks propelling an outbreak of rabid seals around the world, the world’s animal health body has warned.

Countries in South America and Australasia are being urged to look for signs the deadly infectious disease has reached their waters, only two years after it was first confirmed in South Africa.

The 2024 discovery of rabies in South Africa’s Cape fur seals was the first significant outbreak ever found in marine mammals and has been described as a “significant shift in rabies ecology”.

More than 100 cases have been confirmed in South Africa and Namibia since then, raising fears that aggressive rabid seals could infect humans, pets and other wildlife.

Changing patterns in fish stocks caused by the El Nino phenomenon now potentially risk widening the spread, as uninfected seal populations migrate for food and come into contact with rabid colleagues.

Scientists believe warming sea temperatures off Antarctica could send seal populations northwards into Southern African waters, where they could be exposed to rabies.

They could then return to their home waters, taking the virus with them and infecting other seal populations.

News.title: ​Arteta’s ‘dynasty’ dream collides with Arsenal’s harsh reality
News.content:
Arsenal 1 Real Betis 3

Mikel Arteta says he wants to create a “dynasty” at Arsenal as he threw down the gauntlet to his players to retain their Premier League title and reach a “different level”.

Arsenal are on the verge of completing a £75m deal for Brazil midfielder Bruno Guimãraes from Newcastle and have not given up hope of landing Real Madrid winger Vinícius Júnior, who has been offered an improved contract by the Spanish giants.

The Premier League champions slumped to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night, when they paid the price for individual errors and a lethargic, sloppy defensive display.

But that did little to quell Arteta’s ambitions for the new season. “I’m even more excited [about this season], and we’re going to go and attack every possible title because that’s the ambition that we have,” he said.

“We know that we have the ability. We will go from a strength to a strength as well, whether it’s with the players that we have to take them to a different level, and with the market that is still open to recruit as well, so we are very optimistic about it.

“All the work that we’ve done – that I’ve done through the summer – is to understand what we need to do to win again and to create a dynasty in this football club. That’s the aim.”

Despite Arteta’s bullishness, he conceded Arsenal would have to be a lot better than they were against Betis. When asked about the mood in the dressing room, he said: “Very upset, given a hard time. They are fuming, but this is good. That’s what we need.”

Telegraph Sport analyses some of the talking points from a disappointing evening at the Aviva Stadium.

No Saliba a concern

The importance of goalkeeper David Raya and centre-backs William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhães to Arsenal hardly needs overstating. Their title success was built on the foundations provided by that triumvirate at the back.

Raya has yet to report back from holiday after Spain’s World Cup triumph and Saliba is facing an extended spell on the sidelines with a back injury. Gabriel did appear for the second half but, watching this, Arteta is unlikely to have been dissuaded from the belief he needs another top defender to compensate for the loss of Saliba.

It may have been only Arsenal’s second game of pre-season, so a degree of legginess was understandable.

But the ease with which they were cut open and overloaded by the Spanish side, and the volume of individual errors, did not sit comfortably with Arteta with just over a fortnight until they kick off their title defence at home to newly promoted Coventry City.

Only once in 63 matches last season did Arsenal concede three goals in a single game but they were fortunate Betis did not score more. “In the first half there are two different things: to play well and to compete,” said Arteta, who saw his side trail 3-1 at the interval.

News.title: Ebola outbreak outpacing containment effort, WHO chief warns
News.content:
Caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, for which there are no vaccines or treatments, it has been extremely difficult to contain, according to experts on the ground.

“The outbreak is spreading faster than our scale-up of the response, with new cases doubling in some hotspots over the past week alone,” Dr Tedros said on X.

Part of the difficulty is that the virus was circulating undetected for weeks before the outbreak was formally declared in mid-May, leaving health officials even now racing to catch up with the spread.

Prof Placide Mbala, director of research, clinical trials and innovation at Africa CDC, told the Telegraph: “It’s mostly the fact we arrived a bit late. It took us some time before we detected this virus outbreak. And when we detected the outbreak, we already had a total of I can say more than 200 suspected cases. It’s been difficult to catch up. That’s where we are.”

While the DRC has a wealth of experience in tackling haemorrhagic fever outbreaks, the effects of that initial delay are still being felt.

Prof Mbala said: “We have some experience dealing with the cases, the labs, the communication, the infection prevention and control.

“We have some experience... But my observation is that we were very slow, and it’s why we’re in this situation.

“We are slow detecting the people, slow responding, we are slow deploying people, we are slow to recruit the community healthcare workers to improve contact tracing, we are slow to deploy the safe burials.”

DRC’s largest outbreak had previously been from 2018 to 2020, when 3,481 cases were recorded.

The West Africa outbreak recorded 28,616 cases and 11,310 deaths according to the WHO.

Prof Mbala said insecurity was also severely hampering attempts to curb the virus. The outbreak epicentre is in Ituri province, which has been wracked by ethnic strife for decades and is also home to militias competing to control mining.

He said: “There are many, many mining groups controlling most of the mining places. We have a big issue with those places, because they are places where the response team cannot go.”

Medics and aid workers have also been undermined by violent public distrust of their efforts.

Locals in the area have either doubted the existence of the virus, or have accused health teams of deliberately spreading the infection, or somehow benefiting from it.

More than a dozen health facilities have been set alight and several health workers have been killed.

Prof Mbala said: “The local people, they also sometimes are very upset, because they believe that it’s a kind of a business, and people who are coming here, they are getting a lot of money, [so] don’t want this disease to stop.”

He said he hoped that immunity was starting to rise in some areas and this would start to curb transmission.

However there was also a risk that people fleeing the outbreak would spread the virus further afield.

He said: “The second scenario is the fact we are seeing people moving from the affected area to new areas, to run away from the response team because they do not want to go to the treatment centre.

“And in complicity with their family members living in other areas, they are now the ones who are spreading the disease to new areas

“So we’ll see new places affected because people are moving around from the affected zone to the non-affected zone.”

News.title: Mykhailo Mudryk returns as Chelsea slip to Juventus defeat
News.content:
Chelsea 0 Juventus 1

Mykhailo Mudryk made his first Chelsea appearance since November 2024 as Xabi Alonso’s team succumbed to their second pre-season defeat.

Mudryk replaced Nicolas Jackson in the 82nd minute against Juventus, marking his return to competitive football after a long doping ban that was resolved this week thanks to changes in Wada regulations.

There were a couple of crosses delivered from the left flank by the Ukrainian winger, who could yet leave Chelsea on loan or on a permanent basis before the close of the transfer window.

Juventus were the victors though, thanks to a sumptuous 68th-minute goal by Kosovo winger Edon Zhegrova.

Alonso had 21 players on his bench, and made 12 second-half substitutions.

Levi Colwill and Cole Palmer featured in the defeat by 10-man Spurs on Saturday, but sat this game out as they continue to build fitness. Danny Welbeck did start though, reunited with former Brighton team-mate Joao Pedro up top.

Chelsea scored just one goal against Spurs and Juventus, but the thrust provided by right-back Marco Palestra in tandem with first Geovany Quenda and then Estevao was a bright spot for Alonso.

Chelsea continue their pre-season against AC Milan on Saturday, before they host Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge on August 15.

They begin their Premier League campaign at Fulham in the Monday night slot on the opening weekend.

News.title: The underground lab where ‘princess mosquitoes’ are treated like royalty
News.content:
Beneath the grand Art Deco headquarters of the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine lies a vast labyrinth inhabited by weird and wonderful creatures.

In this maze of subterranean labs, store rooms and corridors live colonies of disease-bearing insects and arachnids from all over the world, from bed bugs, sand flies and microscopic dust mites to the so-called kissing bugs that spread Chagas disease – a sinister condition that can cause its victims to drop dead of heart failure without warning, albeit decades after the first (silent) infection.

Behind a series of doors, contained in stacks of mesh boxes, you can even find the flies that spread trachoma, the Dickensian eye disease that is still a leading cause of blindness around the world. But be warned: entering the room is not for the faint of heart – the flies feed on human excrement and the smell is impossible to forget.

There are also many varieties of mosquito, including several species of the Anopheles genus that spread malaria, Culex and Aedes mosquitoes that are also vectors for human and animal diseases, and even Toxorhynchites, perhaps better known as the elephant mosquito, a friendly giant which doesn’t bite people but preys on other mosquitoes.

These animals have been studied intensely since the insectaries were established in the building’s vaults in the 1960s, underpinning many breakthroughs in the control, surveillance, and understanding of vector-borne diseases in the developing world.

LSHTM researchers are now looking closer to home. They have established the UK’s first laboratory colony of Aedes vexans mosquitoes, a species native to the British isles, to study whether they could harbour diseases like West Nile virus, Rift Valley fever, Zika or Japanese encephalitis.

Sports.title: ITV World Cup commentator and former England star joins 17th club of his career weeks after tournament ends
Sports.content:
ANDROS TOWNSEND has swapped the World Cup commentary box for Thailand’s League 1.

25 days after taking the mic in the tournament’s quarter finals, the former England winger has joined the 17th club of his career.



However, PT Prachuap had already let slip about their marquee signing in unprecedented style 13 days before today’s official announcement.

The Thai team bemusingly took to Facebook to ask if anyone had a three-bedroom house by the sea for the former Spurs star.



Townsend is no stranger to the no frills nature of football in the South East Asian nation.

Last season, the 35-year-old had to dry himself with a sock after a post match shower at his former club Kanchanaburi Power.



The nomadic forward’s new team PT Prachuap were founded in 2009 as regional minnows, before breaking into the top flight nine years ago.

A sleepy seaside destination, Townsend’s latest home is known for its crescent-shaped bay and relaxed pace of life.

The 13-time England international was playing in the Premier League as recently as 2024, but has found Thailand to be ideally suited to his viral dietary preferences.

After his first Thai transfer last year, Townsend said he was thrilled that he could find chicken feet to snack on “as soon as I touched down”.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

During his 11-match ITV commentary stint at this summer‘s World Cup, Townsend whipped social media into a frenzy by eating boiled eggs on a plane, as well as raw meat.

The player and broadcaster credits his recovery from a seemingly career-ending ACL injury in 2021 to a total rejection of processed foods.

Townsend once scored a 25-yard screamer for England in a World Cup qualifier, but had to endure nine loan spells across a journeyman career in his home country.

The Tottenham academy product also played 185 times for Crystal Palace, and was memorably shortlisted for the Puskas award after his stunning volley helped the Eagles upset Manchester City in 2018.

Sports.title: Ivan Toney shares snaps from luxury holiday days after being charged with nightclub assault
Sports.content:
IVAN TONEY has shared snaps of himself on holiday to his social media, just days after he was charged with assault.

It was announced by the Met Police on Friday that England World Cup star Toney had been charged with assault causing actual bodily harm following an alleged headbutt during a brawl inside a London nightclub.



Exclusive footage revealed by the 30-year-old was arrested at a trendy Soho bar and frogmarched out of the venue at 100 Wardour St on December 6, 2025.

The force confirmed Toney, who plays for Saudi side Al-Ahli, would be due to appear at Westminster Magistrates’ Court on September 24 – two days before England play Spain in a Nation’s League tie.



But days after the charge, and days before it was made public, Toney shared snaps of himself enjoying his summer break following the World Cup in North America.

Toney was seen posing with his arms folded while wearing a sleeveless black vest, shorts and a hat in front of a scenic city and ocean view background.



The former Brentford stars Instagram, where he has just under a million followers, showed him on spin bikes and with more bold fashion statements in a picturesque sunny setting.

In one short video Toney was seen grimacing as he stepped into a bath tub.

Another snap showed a stunning pool and property basking in sunlight, with the final pic seeing him looking sharp in a collared shirt.

He captioned the post: “Down time but we stay up.”



Issuing a statement, the force said: “A man has been charged with assault following a Met investigation.

“Ivan Toney, 30, of Northampton, was charged on Thursday, 31 July with assault causing actual bodily harm.

“He will appear at Westminster Magistrates’ Court on Thursday, 24 September.



“The charge relates to an assault, which reportedly took place on 6 December 2025 at a nightclub on Wardour Street, W1.”

Sports.title: Ex-Man Utd player, 45, worried about BBC punditry job after being slapped with ban
Sports.content:
FORMER Manchester United midfielder Michael Stewart fears for his broadcasting future after being banished to a car park for the Scottish Cup semi-finals.

The divisive BBC and Premier Sports pundit was banned from Hampden Park by the Scottish FA for contentious comments on air in April.



Known for refusing to mince his words, Stewart was also denied access to a VAR media day at Scotland‘s national stadium last week.

Following the latest media storm, Stewart now feels his on-screen presence hangs in the balance.



The former Scottish international admitted to worrying “constantly” about whether broadcasters could decide to stop hiring him.

Fears that he could be dropped for his thorny reputation have “created a lot of stress” for the 45-year-old.

No stranger to controversy, Stewart mouthed his way into the stadium ban by outspokenly criticising a VAR decision while covering a game between St Mirren and Hibs last season.

After a goal was questionably ruled out, Stewart claimed that the technology had been used for a “cover up”.

He then went on to refer to the Scottish FA’s head of refereeing Willie Collum as “wee Willie”.

The Scottish FA felt that Stewart’s barrage of critiques about the nation’s refereeing and VAR standards crossed a line into “commentary that appears disproportionate, agenda-driven, or personal in nature.”



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Stewart took a contrasting stance on the backlash, saying: “There needs to be an understanding of – I’m just doing my job.”

He also felt that “going about it in this fashion, I don’t think is beneficial to anybody.”

However, the former Man Utd player is now keen to resolve his spat with the Scottish FA, calling for “open and frank discussions with everybody to try to rectify it.”

The current standoff is far from his first brush with the authorities.

In 2020, Stewart was temporarily suspended by BBC Scotland for calling Rangers communications director James Traynor “a dangerous character, a bully and someone who tries to create division for personal gain.”

The Spaniard revealed it was “love at first sight” – for both her and Ronaldo. The Portuguese football previously said he was “1000 per cent sure” he would marry Georgina. And it seems the moment has finally arrived.

Sports.title: Southampton captain Jack Stephens admits points deduction for Spygate scandal has fired Saints up to ‘put things right’
Sports.content:
SOUTHAMPTON skipper Jack Stephens insists the club’s four-point deduction for spying on rivals has fired him up to “put things right”.

Saints will start the season with work to do just to get back to zero, but they are laser-focused on promotion three months after Spygate saw them booted out of the play-offs.



Manager Tonda Eckert admitted he was responsible for the snooping missions, and the FA charged him for “bringing the game into disrepute”.

The German boss, 33, received death threats and still faces the possibility of a touchline ban – but will go again after retaining the backing of Southampton owner Dragan Solak.



And now Stephens is desperate to achieve what was painfully snatched away from Saints in May.

He told SunSport: “The way the season ended was disappointing for everyone involved.



“It was important for everyone to get away, clear their heads, forget about what happened and come back with a clean slate, fully focused on this season.

“We’ve all come back with a mindset that we want to get promoted. We felt like we deserved it last season but that counts for nothing. We need to go and prove it this season.

“We’re not starting from scratch, we’re starting from minus four. It’s going to be a little bit of an uphill task but it’s one we’re very much looking forward to.

“I’d rather not have the four points deducted but that’s where we are.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“We have spoken about it as a group and we’re well aware of the challenge ahead. But we’re also very keen to use that to drive us forward.

“We’ve got the bit between our teeth, we want to put that right for the football club.

“We’re very confident but we have to start again and use this as the driving force behind our season.”

Spygate was a chaotic end to a campaign that promised so much when Eckert masterminded a 19-match unbeaten run that took Saints from 21st to fourth in the league.



No manager in the Championship has picked up more points than Eckert since he was appointed last December.

So for Stephens, 32, there is no question about whether the boss and the squad are strong enough to be in the mix again.

He said: “100 per cent. The evidence is there from last season.

“I’ve got no doubts that we’re going to give it absolutely everything and be very close to promotion.

“Our squad has stayed pretty much the same, in comparison to the teams who have come down from the Premier League, who have a lot to sort out with their squads.



“We’re extremely motivated to put those four points right and we want to do it as quickly as we can.”

Eckert himself has admitted the saga and his punishment are still looming at the back of his mind – and English football fans surely won’t let him forget.

Saints would be wise to expect hostile welcomes from most grounds this season.



So it will have been a relief for Eckert and the squad to get away from it all on a pre-season trip to Germany, where they sharpened up with friendlies against first, second and third-tier opposition.

Their first competitive assignment is against fourth-tier Colchester on Saturday, but Stephens and his team-mates are not taking their quirky Carabao Cup start lightly.

He said: “It’s slightly different but it doesn’t really change anything for us. We’ve approached this game as an important game, which it is.

“We’re looking to go and win and get through to the next round of the cup.”

Sports.title: South Korea’s FA accused of providing referees with sex massages in astonishing claim
Sports.content:
SOUTH KOREA’S FA have sensationally been accused of providing referees with sex massages before games.

The shock claims are alleged to have occurred between 2011 and 2012, according to South Korean TV station JTBC and news agency Yonhap.



The KFA are said to have paid for foreign referees to attend massage parlours in Seoul and other South Korean cities hosting international fixtures.

The matches reportedly included 2014 World Cup and 2012 London Olympic qualifying.



The revelations were based on credit card statements and documents from a government audit report from 2016.

It claimed 20 match officials – who were from Japan, the UAE, Iran, Bahrain and Uzbekistan – were provided with sexual entertainment across seven matches.

South Korea went on an unbeaten run during this period, winning five and drawing twice.

In one period, the team beat Oman 2-0 in an Olympic qualifier on September 21, 2011, before a 2-0 victory over Kuwait in a 2014 World Cup qualifier.

Another Olympic qualifier against Qatar ended in a goalless draw the following month – but the team had already qualified by this point.

South Korea were strong favourites for all three games.



The report from JTBC claimed some referees expected the favours from the KFA and it was “common practice at the time” to cater to them.

According to the Korea Times, the KFA could escape Fifa sanctions as breaches of its ethics code cannot be prosecuted after five years – and ten years for bribery and corruption cases.

SunSport has reached out to the KFA for comment.



It comes during a time of crisis for the KFA after a disastrous World Cup saw South Korea players boycott the media after a video slur towards captain Son Heung-min.

The team were later dumped out in the group stage before coach Hong Myung-bo resigned from his role.

Police then raided KFA offices this week over the initial appointment of Hong in 2024.

Local media said officers were looking into whether KFA chiefs violated internal rules with the hiring of Hong due to “obstruction of business”.

The team’s performance at the World Cup under Hong was so poorly received the coach has been banned from some shops in South Korea.



Hong announced his resignation one day after South Korea’s elimination.

He said: “Over the past two years I asked myself the same question whenever I had to make important decisions, select players or prepare for training session and matches: ‘Is this the right choice for Korean football?’

“I can not say every decision has been the right one, but I can tell you that I have made every decision with Korean football in mind.”

Sports.title: Messi suicide bomb, Ronaldo hotel alert & ref’s 6,000 texts…scale of World Cup threats revealed in leaked police dossier
Sports.content:
A CHILLING police dossier has revealed major security threats made during the World Cup including a horror warning from a suicide bomber.

The bombshell document, seen by Informacion.es, details multiple terrifying terror attempts – with Argentina‘s national team a particular target.



Before their match against Jordan, a man is believed to have rang up Dallas airport and said he and two others would storm the stadium with “homemade bombs and an AR-15”.

The suspected bomber threatened to attack “police officers and players from both teams” but made “special mention” of killing Lionel Messi, according to reports.



Argentina’s match against Egypt was also a target after one suspected terrorist wrote on X: “I’m about to enter Atlanta’s stadium and blow up Messi with four bombs strapped to my body.”

During the game another man called police and announced that

he had left “three bombs” inside trash cans across the stands.

The double threat sparked a major hunt across the stadium by bomb specialists and sniffer dogs.

Messi’s rival Cristiano Ronaldo was also an alleged victim of World Cup attack fears.

A FIFA employee raised the alarm after a “suspicious man” was asking for “details” about the Portuguese superstar’s World Cup accommodation.

Another rabid superfan broke into the footballer’s hotel and tried to get into an elevator with him.



When cops handcuffed the man, he claimed that he just wanted to take a selfie with Ronaldo.

Referee François Letexier was hounded by more than 6,000 “threatening messages” on his personal WhatsApp after his controversial rulings at the Argentina-Egypt match.

Egyptian fans also bombarded video assistant referee (VAR) Willy Delajod with furious messages including death threats.



In yet another disturbing incident, a strawman labelled as “Mbappe” was burned by Paraguay fans after the nation’s defeat by France.

The Real Madrid star was the target of racist attacks, including a sickening tirade from a Paraguayan senator.

Players who made mistakes also received death threats.



Alexander Sorloth and his wife received death threats after the Norway striker failed to play Erling Haaland into goal during their quarter-final clash with England.

Colombian player Jaminton Campaz also faced threats for missing a penalty and was unable to return to the country with the rest of the team after their exit.

Colombia are all too aware of the dangers their players face, after defender Andrés Escobar was executed by a drug cartel after scoring an own goal at the 1994 World Cup.

The South Korea national team also received heavy police protection after their underwhelming group stage exit.

Exiled coach Hong Myung-bo has since been the subject of intense public anger, with police even probing his hiring process.



The England team’s media centre also experienced a worrying security breach.

A man holding a wrench wandered in and began shouting as surprised members of the media.

The Three Lions squad was shielded by three rings of security at their US base at the most fortified World Cup ever.

Their hotel will become a “virtual fortress” surrounded by a cordon of concrete barriers and screens to block the line of sight of potential snipers.

A no-fly zone was enforced to thwart drone attacks and a command centre opposite 54-room, £260-a-night The Inn at Meadowbrook Hotel.



Armed police, security officers and private security guards also patrolled the perimeter of the complex in Prairie Village, Kansas.

Sports.title: UEFA could boycott 5 tournaments in next 11 months after new Gianni Infantino statement
Sports.content:
UEFA could boycott 5 tournaments in next 11 months after new Gianni Infantino statement

Gianni Infantino is determined to cling onto power as FIFA president and his refusal to resign in the wake of the World Cup private investment scandal could force UEFA into action

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino is ready for the fight (Image: AP Photo/Martin Meissner)

UEFA could be forced to carry out their threat of boycotting FIFA tournaments in less than a month after Gianni Infantino refused to give in to the mounting pressure on him to resign.

‌



Rather than fall on his sword, Infantino has made moves to solidify his position as FIFA president. Following seven hours of crisis talks in Morocco on Wednesday, FIFA released a statement saying Infantino had their "full support" after his botched attempt to invite private investment into tournaments.

‌



FIFA have opted to close ranks and go on the offensive, saying they will "no longer tolerate any attacks on its integrity, good governance and due process and will take all necessary measures to protect and safeguard its name and reputation".

‌



The battle lines have been drawn, with UEFA leading the backlash against Infantino. The Football Association has followed in Wales' footsteps by formally withdrawing their support of the Swiss, but with the pressure yet to tell, UEFA and their allies may have to follow through with their threat.

Gianni Infantino state of play as 211 nations decide desperate FIFA president's fate READ MORE :

Argentina at odds with England as statement released on FIFA president Gianni Infantino READ MORE :

In a statement on Thursday, UEFA said FIFA's words following their meeting "changes nothing" and that their threat of a boycott stands. It means FIFA have been put on notice ahead of their next international tournament, the Under-20 Women's World Cup, which is scheduled to be hosted in Poland, beginning on September 5.

After that comes the Under-17 Women's World Cup in Morocco in October and the Under-17 World Cup in Qatar in November and December. Next summer comes a much bigger fish: the Women's World Cup in Brazil. If it came to it, boycotting that would send a strong message - and it is a sacrifice England star Lucy Bronze is willing to make.

‌



FIFA tournaments UEFA could boycott FIFA Under-20 Women's World Cup (Poland) - September 2026 FIFA Under-17 Women's World Cup (Morocco) - October 2026 FIFA Under-17 World Cup (Qatar) -November/December 2026 FIFA Women's Champions Cup (Miami) -January 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup (Brazil) - June/July 2027

“The message that we stand by … is ‘for the good of the game’. The players who play in those competitions, the European players, we stand by our beliefs and what the right thing is for our game,” Bronze said ahead of a Chelsea pre-season friendly in New Zealand.

“If that means boycotting competitions, then that has to happen. It’s for the future of the game and not just for me today and tomorrow, it’s for all the little girls or little boys who come after us to make sure that they’re in a good place, when the game is moving forward in decades to come, not just tomorrow.”

‌



With Infantino not willing to resign, UEFA may have to back a rival candidate in the upcoming FIFA presidential election. Infantino has been in charge for 10 years and was set to stand unopposed for a fourth term next year, but the events of the past week have changed everything.

View 2 Images UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin is leading the effort to oust Gianni Infantino (Image: Nicolò Campo/LightRocket via Getty Images)

A UEFA statement shared on Thursday afternoon read: "UEFA's associations were very clear about the conditions attached to the non-participation in FIFA competitions.

‌



"First, the proposals to sell off the major competitions had to be withdrawn, and secondly, assurances have to be made that such attempts to disfigure the game in this way will never be made again.

"These conditions have not been met. In addition, UEFA made it abundantly clear in its statement on Saturday that it has lost confidence in Gianni Infantino's presidency. That position holds.

"Yesterday's (Wednesday) announcement that some people employed by the FIFA President (and whose careers depend on his favour) agree with him changes nothing."

Sports.title: Enzo Maresca wants Chelsea star to replace Rodri as Barcelona move advances
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca wants Chelsea star to replace Rodri as Barcelona move advances

Barcelona have seen an opening bid for Manchester City midfielder Rodi turned down on Friday - but the La Liga giants are expected to return as they close in on the World Cup winner

View 3 Images Barcelona have launched an opening offer for Man City midfielder Rodri

Enzo Maresca has earmarked Chelsea midfielder Enzo Fernandez as his top option to replace Rodri this summer.

‌



Barcelona have seen an opening offer of £38.5million rejected out of hand by City, who want closer to £60m. However, with just one year remaining on his contract and coming off a serious knee injury, City are open to selling at the right price.

‌



And Maresca, who is going into his first season as Pep Guardiola ’s replacement, sees Fernandez as the perfect replacement for the World Cup Golden Ball winner.

‌



The Italian worked with Fernandez during his time as Chelsea boss and according to the Independent, City are already exploring a possible move for the Argentinian.

Inside Bruno Guimaraes' dream Arsenal transfer six years in making for Mikel Arteta READ MORE :

Fernandez is yet to report for Chelsea this summer after playing a huge role in Argentina’s rollercoaster ride to the World Cup final. The 25-year-old scored crucial goals in the knockout stages, including a screamer in the dramatic comeback against England in the semis.

However, he arguably cost his nation the chance of lifting a fourth world title after he inexplicably picked up two yellow cards in a matter of minutes.

‌



Chelsea paid £106m for the midfielder in 2023 and would want to make a profit on that, if they were to entertain an exit this summer.

Fernandez was sanctioned earlier this year after his desire to leave the London club was made public. Ex-boss Liam Rosenior was also forced to strip him of the vice captaincy before he was sacked for a disastrous run of results.

View 3 Images Chelsea want a reported £120m for Enzo Fernandez (Image: Visionhaus/Getty Images)

‌



New Blues boss Xabi Alonso hasn’t been able to train with the talismanic midfielder during his short tenure, but made it clear he wants him to remain at the club.

Speaking in July, Alonso said: "Yes we have spoken. But as you can imagine what we have spoken remains private,” and then when pressed if he wanted Fernandez to stay, he replied “yes”.

City have already smashed their own transfer record this summer, signing Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest for a whopping £116m. But with the exit of Bernardo Silva and the expected one of Rodri, more cover is required before the Premier League campaign begins.

‌



They have also been heavily linked with Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille, who shone at the World Cup with Morocco, but his £86m valuation has led talks to an impasse.

View 3 Images Enzo Maresca worked with Fernandez during his time as Chelsea boss

Speaking after City’s most recent pre-season friendly, Maresca admitted the club still had work to do in order to replace a number of senior players.

‌



“Fortunately this is a squad that doesn’t need to do many things,” he told media at a press conference ahead of Wednesday’s clash with K-League All Stars.

“At the same time, we already know the squad lost some important players with experience with Bernardo, John [Stones], Nathan [Ake]…different players. For sure, there are things we need to do.

He added: “The reason I said there are things to do is because the transfer window is open and when it is open, anything can happen. It is August and then from September, when it’s closed, it is completely different.”

Sports.title: Man Utd legends called out by former team-mate as Roy Keane in firing line
Sports.content:
Man Utd legends called out by former team-mate as Roy Keane in firing line

Roy Keane and several other Manchester United legends have been called out by a fellow Red Devils hero

View 3 Images Javier Hernandez has called out his former team-mates for criticising Michael Carrick

Roy Keane, Gary Neville and Paul Scholes have been called out by their former Manchester United team-mate Javier Hernandez for comments about Michael Carrick. Carrick did a remarkable job at the helm after being appointed as United’s interim head coach back in January.

‌



He managed to secure a third place Premier League finish and qualification to the Champions League, which was largely unthinkable under his predecessor Ruben Amorim earlier in the season. That has since seen the 45-year-old be appointed as the club’s permanent head coach ahead of the 2026/27 campaign.

‌



Yet, while many United fans and, evidently, the club have been pleased with Carrick’s tenure up to now, the former Red Devils midfielder has faced considerable criticism from the same people he shared a dressing room with during his 12-year stint as a player at Old Trafford.

‌



Roy Keane seemingly holds some bitterness towards Carrick, having made personal jibes, while Paul Scholes took to social media to have a dig at his former midfield partner following a loss to Newcastle. Gary Neville also cast doubt over Carrick's credentials for the role.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Man Utd finally announce sixth summer transfer as statement confirms next steps READ MORE :

Recently appearing on Rio Ferdinand Presents, Hernandez was asked for his thoughts about Carrick being at the helm and replied: "I love it, I love it.” Ferdinand then pointed out that several of the pair's former team-mates had been far less complimentary about Carrick.

‌



"I don’t know why. I really don’t know why. There’s a fine line between criticising someone’s job, because you have to, and then your own opinions," replied Hernandez.

"I’m very surprised, mostly because you know Carrick more than I do. You spent so much time with him, not only as a teammate at the club but also with the national team. Carrick was always a man who never had a problem with anyone.

View 3 Images Roy Keane has made some harsh comments about Carrick (Image: ITV)

‌



"The most civilised, calm person. So I don’t understand. How are you going to criticise a manager who is giving you results?

"He put your team back into the Champions League, so he deserves the consequence of that: stay, try to bring him players and give him the project. If it doesn’t work, it doesn’t work. But he took the team from low and put the team back into the Champions League."

Hernandez also spoke openly about his departure from United in 2015, admitting he felt the club had changed following the exits of Sir Alex Ferguson and David Gill in 2013.

‌



View 3 Images Michael Carrick has transformed Manchester United (Image: Ash Donelon, Manchester United via Getty Images)

He said: "It was very hard. Because if you gave me the chance to stay at United for most of my career, I would have taken it. The team that I played the most games for, even more than my hometown team in Mexico, is United.

"I would have taken a bullet for that team. It’s my team, Manchester United. But things weren’t the same. It’s not that I left the club that I was with; I left a different environment. It wasn’t the same club.

Article continues below

"With the departure, obviously, of Sir Alex Ferguson, but also David Gill and all that family structure. When I say family, it doesn’t mean that it was all nice, but there were values.

"I was very sad. Don’t get me wrong. I would have retired at United and I would take a bullet for that team. But it wasn’t the same team as the team that embraced me and gave me my first opportunity."

Sports.title: Arsenal star's gesture to Bruno Guimaraes ahead of £75m transfer comes to light
Sports.content:
Arsenal star's gesture to Bruno Guimaraes ahead of £75m transfer comes to light

Arsenal are preparing to confirm the £75m signing of Bruno Guimaraes after the soon-to-be former Newcastle captain completed his medical - and his shirt number seemingly been leaked

View 2 Images Bruno Guimaraes will join Arsenal for £75million (Image: Mark Leech/Offside/Offside via Getty Images)

Bruno Guimaraes is set to wear the No.39 shirt for Arsenal after academy star Louie Copley moved to a new number. Arsenal are preparing to confirm Guimaraes' arrival from Newcastle after the two clubs agreed a fixed fee of £75million to end the transfer saga.

‌



The 28-year-old said his goodbyes at Newcastle's training camp in Spain before completing his medical with Arsenal and signing a four-year contract. His signing still hasn't been announced, although the Gunners have dropped a clear hint on their website.

‌



Copley, who wore the No. 39 shirt in each of Arsenal's first two pre-season friendlies as well as in training sessions, has had his squad number changed to 38. It's a telltale sign that Guimaraes is now a Gunner and has taken his favourite number.

‌



The midfielder has worn 39 throughout his club career, including for former clubs Lyon and Athletico Paranaense. Guimaraes likes to wear the number because his dad's taxi cab in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil was #039.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Inside Bruno Guimaraes' dream Arsenal transfer six years in making for Mikel Arteta READ MORE :

Tottenham respond as Arsenal consider shock transfer for Spurs skipper Cristian Romero READ MORE :

Whether the decision was Copley's is unknown, although he did wear No.38 when captaining Arsenal's under-21 side last season. Unfortunately for Copley, who's just 19 and highly regarded at London Colney, he suffered an injury just minutes after coming on as a half-time substitute during the Gunners' 3-1 loss against Real Betis in a friendly on Wednesday.

‌



Mikel Arteta said post-match: "It doesn't look good, the mechanism is not too positive, the symptoms that he already has either. Let's hope that tomorrow [Thursday] the news is better than we hope."

Guimaraes will become Arsenal's most expensive signing of the summer, with the Gunners having also brought in Christos Tzolis for £34m and Illan Meslier on a free transfer. The Brazilian is expected to partner Declan Rice in midfield once the season gets going.

Who should Arsenal sign next? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Louie Copley's number has been changed on the Arsenal website

By leaving Newcastle, Guimaraes becomes the third key player to depart St James' Park this summer as well as manager Eddie Howe. New Magpies boss Matthias Jaissle said: "I met him quickly, but the decision was already made. It was a nice conversation.

"He's a fantastic player and a great human being. It's tough but for him now it's the next challenge and we need to deal with it at a later stage. We trust the players who are here already, but we will also see some changes."

Sports.title: Terror plot to 'storm World Cup game with bombs and kill Lionel Messi' uncovered
Sports.content:
Terror plot to 'storm World Cup game with bombs and kill Lionel Messi' uncovered

FBI and IPCC logs show Lionel Messi received the most threats during the World Cup, including a disturbing incident where a man claimed he would carry guns and bombs to a game

View 2 Images Messi received the most threats during the World Cup (Image: DiaEsportivo/Action Plus/Shutterstock)

Terrorists planned to attack Lionel Messi by storming a World Cup match with guns and bombs, a police report states.

‌



A catalogue of threats were made during the tournament, held in the US, including from a man who was arrested trying to get into a lift with Cristiano Ronaldo.

‌



Reports from the International Police Cooperation Center (IPCC) and FBI also show the referee of the Argentina-Egypt match, Francois Letezier, was targeted with more than 6,000 threats on his personal WhatsApp - and his family back in France received police protection. The security reports have been revealed by Spanish newspaper Informacion.es.

‌



The reports note how one man wrote on X ahead of the Argentina clash with Egypt on July 7: "I'm going to walk into the Atlanta stadium and blow up Messi with four bombs stuck in my body."

View 2 Images There were many reports of Cristiano Ronaldo being harassed (Image: AP Photo/Tony Gutierrez)

Aldi and Lidl could soon be stopped from blocking rival supermarkets opening shops READ MORE :

The most concrete threat against Messi arose when a man called Dallas airport and announced that he and two other individuals were heading to the city's stadium with "homemade bombs and an AR-15".

‌



In his message, he stated that they intended to attack "police officers and players from both teams" but the alleged terrorist made "special mention of Lionel Messi".

Several explosives specialists, canine handlers and their K-9 agents searched the Atlanta stadium after another man called police during the game and announced he had left "three bombs" in litter bins in the stadium.

According to the dossier, Messi received the most threats while Ronaldo was the most harassed while during the competition.

‌



On June 14, a FIFA employee reported "a suspicious man" who was asking for "details" about Ronaldo's accommodation at his hotel. Houston police identified and arrested that man two days later when he was at the hotel where Ronaldo was staying with his national team.

Another man was arrested in Toronto for a very similar incident when Ronaldo was there. This time, the supporter tried to get into the elevator with the Portuguese star when he was arrested. He said he just wanted to take a selfie with CR7.

Other incidents with Ronaldo occurred in Miami, when a man tried to gain access to him, and during the Portugal-Croatia match, when a man dressed in a Ronaldo shirt jumped onto the field.

Article continues below

Another of the many players singled out with threats was Kylian Mbappé, who had an ongoing argument with Paraguay's goalkeeper during the clash with France.

The police report said the Real Madrid player was insulted with "xenophobic" abuse online, while a doll with Mbappé's image "was burned and broadcast" on social networks in Paraguay on July 5 and 6.

Sports.title: Man Utd dream attack as Marcus Rashford exits plus free agent striker and World Cup star join
Sports.content:
Man Utd dream attack as Marcus Rashford exits plus free agent striker and World Cup star join

Manchester United continue their hard work in the summer transfer window with more players on the way

View 4 Images Marcus Rashford's Manchester United future is still up in the air (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

Manchester United could offload Marcus Rashford's hefty wages and a struggling striker to make way for more new signings to arrive at Old Trafford. The Red Devils are continuing their activity in the summer transfer window with Michael Carrick building a squad capable of competing across various competitions.

‌



United have spent £83m so far this summer, and have seen some huge salaries drop off the wage bill. Jadon Sancho departed the club as a free agent and Casemiro headed for Inter Miami, both of which freed up some room in the budget.

‌



A £35m move for Youri Tielemans has been completed, with the former Aston Villa midfielder signing a five-year deal at Old Trafford. Andrey Santos also joined from Chelsea for an initial £48m, plus £2m in add-ons to beef up the middle of the park.

‌



Karl Darlow, Kit Margetson and Tynan Thompson have also arrived. However, Carrick will still be eager for more players through the door. Some stars will have to depart to accommodate this, with Rashford's future one of a number up for discussion.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Man Utd closing in on transfer deal after Michael Carrick dropped hint READ MORE :

Joshua Zirkzee is also being linked with a switch to Juventus, though only on a temporary basis. Reinforcements will be required for Carrick to have enough squad depth to compete both at home and in Europe.

Here, Mirror Football has looked at what a dream United attacking lineup could look like this season.

Free agent striker

United signed Zirkzee for £36.5m in 2024 but he has slipped down the pecking order at Old Trafford. The Dutchman has made a few appearances under Carrick but watched on as Benjamin Sesko leapfrogged him to spearhead the attack last season.

‌



Italian newspaper Corriere dello Sport reports that Juventus are closing in on a loan deal for Zirkzee, with boss Luciano Spalletti 'saying yes' to the move. It looks increasingly likely that the former Bologna man will depart this summer, one way or another.

United will likely need reinforcements if that is to happen, although Carrick may not want to disrupt the progress of Sesjo, who impressed towards the back end of last term. This is where the free agency market could prove invaluable. Dusan Vlahovic is one among several forwards who have been linked to Old Trafford – and he could represent the perfect signing for nothing at all.

View 4 Images Dusan Vlahovic represents a cheap but effective option (Image: Image Photo Agency/Getty Images)

‌



The 26-year-old left Juve following the expiry of his deal this summer, having netted 68 goals in 168 outings. He has amassed 140 club goals throughout his career.

Vlahovic boasts a considerable European pedigree but could provide adequate cover for Sesko, who has impressed under Carrick's guidance. Securing a free agent would demonstrate the manager's faith in the Slovenian forward while allowing him to develop through competition with the Serbia international.

Vlahovic would additionally offer greater flexibility in attack, enabling Carrick to rest Sesko and maintain squad fitness throughout a demanding campaign.

‌

Rashford decision

Rashford's situation at United continues to hang in the balance. At present, the academy product is set to rejoin pre-season preparations with the club following the collapse of a Barcelona switch.

He remains heavily linked with a move away from the club, including in recent days to Fenerbahce. Earlier in the window, however, it was thought that Rashford wouldn't be keen on a move to Turkey, which could put the skids on any potential move before it has even gotten going. Tottenham have also registered their interest, and with several weeks remaining before the transfer window shuts, whether Rashford's future lies at Old Trafford or beyond remains very much unresolved.

‌



View 4 Images Iliman Ndiaye's experience would be greatly welcomed at Old Trafford (Image: Vince Mignott/MB Media/Getty Images)

Should he depart permanently, Iliman Ndiaye could prove an ideal replacement, bringing with him solid Premier League pedigree. The 26-year-old has racked up 20 goal contributions across 70 appearances for Everton and is strongly linked with a move to United.

It is understood that the Toffees will hold out for around £70m for the left-winger, who is also attracting attention from Saudi Pro League outfit Al-Hilal.

‌



United's dream attack

View 4 Images United's attacking is shaping up quite nicely (Image: Paul ELLIS / AFP via Getty Images)

With Benjamin Sesko currently leading the line, Vlahovic could be the ideal option for United to call upon when needed. With two top-quality strikers at their disposal, focus would then shift to the wide positions.

Amad and Bryan Mbeumo have the right flank well covered, with the latter likely to get the nod to start. Ndiaye would fit seamlessly on the left, and there is always the option to utilise Patrick Dorgu in a more advanced role after impressing last season.

Sports.title: Shergar Cup Sprint tips: Kate, Sam and Jamie are taking on Ascot favourite
Sports.content:
Kate Tracey, Sam Boswell and Jamie Lynch reconvene to discuss the best betting angles for the Shergar Cup Sprint at Ascot on Saturday, live on Sky Sports Racing.

Thunder Call heads the market for this typically competitive heat having gone down on his sword when looking to complete a hat-trick in a hot three-year-old handicap at Newmarket last time out, but all three of our panellists are taking on the William Haggas-trained sprinter.

Senior form analyst Jamie Lynch:

"Quick conditions will help for Havana Hurricane, trained by Eve Johnson Houghton. He's up to six furlongs from five last time and this is only his third handicap start too. He was well liked last year and won the Windsor Castle.

"The key here is up in trip and being held up. The last five winners of this race have come from off the pace as they go a fair gallop. There is a lot to like with him here and he's a proper each-way price."

Host Kate Tracey:

"Her rating could be a little high but the thing with her is she's still so unexposed for a trainer who has done well with sprinting mares this season in Katie Scott. I think she's a lot more unexposed than these and has a good chance here."
