Sports.title: Doyle: Thunder Call a big player in Ascot's Shergar Cup
Sports.content:
Our ambassador Hollie Doyle, who was the leading rider at the 2023 Shergar Cup, runs the rule over Saturday's international contest at Ascot - live on Sky Sports Racing.

Glamorous can have them singing in the Valleys

It's exciting for Welsh trainer Chris Mason to have a runner in this year's Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup and they'll be singing loud in his Monmouth village on Saturday night if All Ways Glamorous takes the opening Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Dash (1.35) at Ascot.

His five-year-old, who will be representing Team Europe, already has a course-and-distance win to his name after impressing off a five-pound lower rating two weeks ago and can give French rider Marie Velon a great experience.

Europe's Bolo Neighs looks poised to get his head in front soon after flashing home in the same race last time but has work to do to turn the tables, while Ryan Moore can be relied upon to get the best out of my old friend Spartan Arrow who has been working well enough to put points on the board for Great Britain and Ireland.

Shady has Moore to offer in Stayers

Shrimp Shady is a young horse going places and can give Great Britain and Ireland maximum points in the Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Stayers (2.10).

Andrew Balding's four-year-old has landed big marathon handicaps at Chester and Newbury already this summer and looks made for this stiff two-mile trip with Ryan Moore set for another plum ride.

Europe, who haven't won the Shergar Cup since back-to-back triumphs in 2013 and 2014, are also well represented with the Ian Williams-trained Hermetic likely to build on his fourth at Newcastle under the classy Christophe Lemaire. This ex-French winner could be well treated off a mark of 81.

Castle in driving seat for Ferraris

It was good to see Richard and Peter Fahey come off the cold list at Southwell on Thursday, just in time for Castle Stuart's run in the Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Challenge (2.45).

Hong Kong, who are competing as a team for the first time, have a live contender in this reliable four-year-old who has been unfortunate to bump into two Roger Varian improvers at York this summer. South African Luke Ferraris, a well-known name in China, can be relied upon to get the best out of him.

Ian Williams has the services of Irish champion Dylan Browne McMonagle on his likely favourite Night Breeze, a consistent sort who was a good third at Goodwood but needs a career best to win this, which could make him a shade vulnerable. Insanity took this two years ago for Rachel King and can go well again under Europe's Velon.

Thunder a big player for Hong Kong debutant

Thunder Call didn't appear to enjoy Newmarket's undulations last time but can get back to winning ways for the Hong Kong team in the Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Sprint (3.20).

William Haggas' sprinter won in the style of a very nice horse at York before that and promises to be ideally suited to the stiff finish at Ascot, with British racing debutant Jerry Chau on board.

One to watch out for is Great Britain and Ireland's Cape Ashizuri who is unexposed enough to put a disappointing run in a big field last time behind him. John and Sean Quinn will be happy to have McMonagle in the plate.

Archers can hit the target for Ryan

Newmarket-based Italian trainer Marco Botti can put maximum points on the scoreboard for Great Britain and Ireland in the Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Classic (3.55).

Archers Bay, another strong chance for Moore, has been bumping into the likes of Ancient Egypt and Heraldry since winning at Newmarket - form that stands out in what doesn't look the strongest renewal.

Team-mate Hoseki is on a roll after rattling up a hat-trick in a course-and-distance fillies' race under a light weight. I'm not sure how much improvement she has left off this five-pound higher mark, though. A more interesting proposition could be Jessie Harrington's Pierre Grosse who is still a maiden but brings solid form to the race in first-time cheekpieces.

Bullet to make a Point in Cup decider

The closing Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Mile (4.30) could determine where the trophy goes this year with Europe's Bullet Point the one I expect to capitalise.

Lemaire partners Haggas' gelding, who has the sheepskins on for the first time after not hitting top stride in two starts this year. He is only a pound higher than when he won a big handicap at York's Ebor Festival 12 months ago.

I also like Rest of the World's Ebt's Guard, a course-and-distance winner who has run well in big handicaps at Royal Ascot and Sandown and looks a big player for Indian ace Suraj Narredu, who won the competition with Team Asia last year.

Special memories of the Shergar Cup

The Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup has given me some of my most special days on a racecourse and I'm excited to watch the action unfold in front of what will once again be a big, enthusiastic crowd at Ascot.

I've been lucky enough to ride three winners in the competition including a double three years ago when I was presented with the Alistair Haggis Silver Saddle Trophy for the highest points scorer.

I was on the winning team in 2023 and 2018 and can tell you that lifting that cup is such a buzz. Being part of a team competition is something we don't often experience as jockeys so the rivalry out on the turf on Saturday will be intense.

Sports.title: Draper will play Cincinnati Open despite arm injury fears
Sports.content:
Jack Draper has been confirmed for next week's Cincinnati Open despite being left in a flood of tears following defeat at the National Bank Open in Montreal.

Draper's hopes of playing in the US Open had looked to be in doubt after his latest comeback attempt saw him break down in tears mid-match.

The 24-year-old was playing his first match since June in Canada having suffered a recurrence of the bone bruising that kept him out for almost seven months.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the first-round match at the Canadian Open between Draper and Terence Atmane

Draper looked in discomfort, with his serve badly affected against France's Terence Atmane. After being broken to trail 4-1 in the third set, Draper sat on his chair and sobbed, eventually losing 6-3 2-6 6-2.

"This is pretty emotional actually. He's been bent over and just literally erupting with emotion here. Very, very upsetting to see. It just happened at the change of ends, he leaned forward," former British No 1 Annabel Croft told viewers on Sky Sports.

Croft added: "He knows what's going on inside his body, and he knows the work he's done to try and get back on court."

The Brit has been given a wild card for the Masters 1000 event in Cincinnati beginning next week - live on Sky Sports Tennis, while the US Open - for which he would also need a wild card into the main draw - starts on August 30.

Mixed doubles at US Open

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the US Open mixed doubles match of Draper and Jessica Pegula vs Emma Raducanu and Carlos Alcaraz

Draper is due to play in the mixed doubles at Flushing Meadows the preceding week with Jessica Pegula, and the American admitted their participation is now in doubt.

Speaking to reporters in Canada, Pegula said: "I know that he's been really struggling a bit with some injuries and I saw today he had a really tough day with his match.

"We're supposed to play. Obviously I know he's not healthy, so we'll see how that goes."

Pegula and Draper reached the semi-finals last year, and she added: "I've always since then been a very big fan, and it's been fun to watch him. He's a really nice kid, so I enjoy playing with him.

"Hoping that he can just get healthy and we can see him back out there."

Draper's injury woes

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Draper says his focus is on a 'rebirth' after suffering the 'perfect storm' of injury issues in recent times

If Draper is unable to play in New York, it would be a fourth consecutive Grand Slam that he has missed through injury.

Draper's problems first surfaced after a second-round exit at Wimbledon last year, with the former US Open semi-finalist forced off the tour with a bone bruise in his left arm.

He tried to make a comeback at Flushing Meadows but pulled out ahead of his second-round match and did not play again until February.

After initial positive signs, including victory over Novak Djokovic in Indian Wells, a changed service motion to try to help his arm problem led to a knee injury that kept him out for another lengthy spell.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Indian Wells match between Draper and Novak Djokovic

Returning just ahead of Wimbledon in Eastbourne, Draper looked strong and reached the semi-finals only to announce on the eve of his home Grand Slam that his arm had flared up again and he would be unable to play.

Speaking to Sky Sports ahead of Montreal, Draper said: "It's important for people to recognise that the injury I have is very complex, it's very complicated, and everyone around me is doing everything we can to help this keep moving along.

"It really has been a perfect storm for me in a lot of ways. When I do get out of this storm, I'm going to be pushing on to hopefully get to where I want to be and beyond."

Sports.title: Newcastle stand firm on Hall after rejecting Man Utd approach
Sports.content:
Newcastle United have told Manchester United that full-back Lewis Hall is not for sale this summer, after an initial enquiry was rejected.

Manchester United are looking to strengthen at left-back this summer and 21-year-old England international Hall is a player they have long admired.

But Newcastle turned down their enquiry two weeks ago, and are in the market to add another full-back themselves.

Hall has three years remaining on his current Newcastle contract.

Sky Sports News has been reporting since March that Hall was among the names being considered by Manchester United for a summer move as they search for a long-term successor to Luke Shaw, who has one year left on his contract.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Joe Thomlinson, William Bitibiri and Danyal Khan discuss Manchester United's interest in Newcastle left-back Lewis Hall.

Manchester United are currently going into the new season with Shaw as their only senior option at left-back, following Tyrell Malacia's departure on a free transfer.

Manchester United will continue to assess their options this summer as they look to strengthen Michael Carrick's side with an additional midfielder still a possibility at this stage.

Sports.title: Man City reject Barcelona offer for Rodri
Sports.content:
Manchester City have knocked back an initial offer from Barcelona for Rodri that is considered far too low.

Barcelona's initial offer - which Manchester City rejected - was worth in the region of £40m. City are seeking upwards of £60m for the 30-year-old midfielder, who has entered the final year of his deal.

Talks over a deal have therefore halted for now.

Barcelona are not giving up on Rodri by any means. Plans are in motion for another offer to go in at some point in coming days.

Sources in Spain believe Rodri would prefer a move to Barcelona over Real Madrid.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player On the Transfer Show, the panel discuss which Spanish giant is favourite to sign Manchester City midfielder Rodri

City do not want to sell Spain's World Cup-winning captain and instead want to agree a new contract with him.

If Rodri asks to leave, however, then they would not stand in his way.

Chelsea's Fernandez would be 'dream' signing for Maresca

Image: Enzo Fernandez could be a target for Man City if Rodri leaves

As Manchester City assess their options for a replacement, Sky in Italy reports that Chelsea midfielder Enzo Fernández is manager Enzo Maresca's "dream" signing.

Sky Sports News reported earlier this summer that Fernandez was not a player City were considering signing, as their priority at the time was to retain Rodri.

The fluidity of the situation, therefore, means it remains to be seen whether circumstances change with regards to Fernandez, as City may look to bring in two players if Rodri joins Barcelona.

Fernandez is due back at Chelsea training next week after reaching the World Cup final with Argentina. Question marks remain over his future with the Blues despite the fact he has a contract until 2032. Chelsea value Fernandez at £120m.

The midfielder was left out of the squad for two games in April after admitting he would like to live in Madrid. The midfielder and his agent later apologised for the comments. They are also seeking improved terms at Chelsea.

Real Madrid released a statement last month denying any interest in signing Fernandez, while the Argentine enjoyed a strong working relationship with Maresca during the Italian's time at Chelsea.

Carra: Don't sell Rodri for £40-50m!

Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher:

"£40-50m? If you're Manchester City, what's the point in selling them? You might as well just keep them for the extra year.

"He's as good as anybody in that position in the Premier League, probably the best. Seeing what he was like in the World Cup, it was like he was back to his best.

"I thought the second half of the season him and Bernardo Silva were fantastic and almost took Manchester City to the title.

"So, if I was the manager of Manchester City, I'd be keeping Rodri at that price. It'd have to be something really special to want me to lose arguably the best midfield player in world football.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher urges Manchester City to keep midfielder Rodri for the final season of his contract rather than sell him in this transfer window

"I think it'd be really tough for them to win the Premier League without Rodri, even though they've got a lot of midfielders. He's the best, even though they've brought Elliot Anderson, who is one who I'm sure will learn off Rodri.

"And for me, I'd see those two as a pair. I see Elliot Anderson as almost the replacement for Bernardo Silva, who's gone to Real Madrid. So, I think that'd be a big hole. It'd be really difficult to fill.

"When Liverpool won the title under Arne Slot, Rodri got an injury in that season very early on, which helped Liverpool and was to the detriment of Manchester City. So if I was Manchester City, I'd be keeping him and letting him go on a free.

"City paid £60m for him. If they're getting £40m back now, what can they do with that type of money? Not a lot, really. So, I'd rather keep him."

Image: Real Madrid has also shown an interest in Rodri

Sky Sports' Laura Hunter:

Massive. Despite his age, and recent injury record, Rodri remains the most complete central midfielder to have operated in the Premier League over the past five years. "The best midfielder in the world by far," maintains Pep Guardiola.

Under Guardiola, City's in-play strategy revolved entirely around him, always impressing with his use of the ball and ability to receive in tight situations. He set the tempo for his team and controlled games as a result, doing the same for triumphant Spain this summer.

There is no current player who can condition a game like Rodri, and it is no coincidence City failed to retain their Premier League crown in the two seasons he was injury-plagued.

So, how is he replaced?

In short, he isn't.

But in Anderson City have got a surrogate of sorts. The England international might not yet be the dictator Rodri is but he can evolve to become something close. As a box-to-box midfielder, the 23-year-old is putting up numbers that at least mean he is comparable.

Sports.title: Van Barneveld fine and suspension revealed in Darts Regulation Authority case list
Sports.content:
Five-time world champion Raymond van Barneveld has been fined and suspended by the Darts Regulation Authority for inappropriate behaviour and offensive language.

The DRA, which is the independent body responsible for regulating the sport, particularly in events run under the umbrella of the PDC, WDF, Modus and ADC, has published an updated case list for the first time since 2022, listing all backdated hearings from January 2023 to June 2026, relating to various incidents that had occurred in both televised and non-televised competition.

Former world champions Rob Cross, Gary Anderson, Luke Humphries and Van Barneveld all feature in the case list, along with Cameron Menzies and Dom Taylor.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Raymond van Barneveld talks us through his greatest game as he beat Phil Taylor in the final of the 2007 World Championship

Van Barneveld, widely regarded as one of the sport's greatest-ever players, features in two separate incidents.

The first involves 'Inappropriate behaviour and using offensive language' at Players Championship 2 event in Wigan last year, resulting in a three-month suspension [suspended for 12 months] and £3,000 fine.

The second relates to 'failing to report damage caused to hotel room' following a Players Championship event in Germany, which resulted in a formal warning.

'Barney' is a five-time world champion having won the BDO tournament at Lakeside in 1998, 1999, 2003 and 2005 before making the move to the PDC the following year.

The doyen of Dutch darts made his mark by winning the 2007 PDC World Championship with a legendary final against Phil 'The Power' Taylor.

Sky Sports have contacted the DRA regarding Van Barneveld's fines.

Menzies handed four-month suspension

Image: Cameron Menzies repeatedly punched the underside of the drinks table on stage in frustration following his defeat to Charlie Manby at the World Championship

Menzies' sanction for his outburst at the World Championship in December has been revealed, with the Scot handed a four-month suspension, which ended last month, and receiving a £2,500 fine after he repeatedly punched the underside of the drinks' table on stage in frustration following his defeat to Charlie Manby.

The incident drew blood on his knuckles, which he then wiped on his face before walking off the stage.

Shortly after the incident, Menzies issued a statement apologising for his actions.

"First of all, I would like to apologise for what happened," said Menzies. "I am sorry that I reacted in the manner that I did.

"It's not an excuse, but I have had a lot of things on my mind recently and I suppose it all just became too much at the end.

"It has not been an easy time for me with my uncle Gary passing away recently. I saw him four days before he died and he gave a look which told he much he thought of me. He treated me like a son.

"Had I won the game against Charlie, my second match would have been on the day of Gary's funeral and that has not been lost on me in recent days.

"Let me say again, that's no excuse for what I did on the stage. It was the wrong thing to do and I don't want it to take anything away from Charlie. He played well and deserved his win.

"This is not how I would like people to view me. Yes I can get emotional at times, but not like that and that wasn't right."

Taylor's failed drugs test

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Dom Taylor impressed on his Ally Pally debut in a first round win over Oskar Lukasiak at the World Championship with three 100+ checkouts

Taylor's failed drugs test at the World Championship resulted in a six-month suspension until June 18, as well as a £1,275 fine in costs and the forfeiture of his £25,000 in prize money.

Taylor tested positive for cocaine and cannabis with the offence being his second which incurred a mandatory six-month ban under DRA rules.

"Accordingly, and taking into account all of the available evidence, the committee were satisfied that Mr Taylor's ingestion of both cocaine and cannabis occurred out of competition and was not following the commencement of the World Championship on 11th December 2025," the DRA statement read.

"Following on from this finding, the committee has determined that as this is Mr Taylor's second offence, then under these rules, he must serve a six month ban in line with 10.9 (a) and 10.9 (b) of UKAD Anti-Doping Rules 2021".

Taylor also lost his Tour Card as a result of the offence.

He had previously served a one-month ban in 2025 after failing a drugs test at the Players Championship Finals in November 2024. The ban was reduced from an initial two years after he agreed to undergo a UKAD-approved three-month substance abuse treatment programme.

Prakash Jiwa and Andy Jenkins both received hefty bans and were each made to pay costs of over £17,000 after being found guilty of match-fixing in the Modus Super Series from 2022-2023.

Sports.title: Mexico and Argentina line up behind Infantino to deepen football’s civil war
Sports.content:
Mexico’s football federation has broken ranks with the rest of Concacaf by publicly backing the beleaguered Gianni Infantino in a move that has deepened world football’s civil war.

Concacaf has called for a thorough review of Fifa’s governance in the light of the World Cup sell-off debacle, and is backing Uefa’s demands for meaningful change, although has yet to follow its European counterparts by threatening to boycott tournaments if they do not achieve their objectives.

In a statement issued on Thursday night, the FMF went some way towards explaining Concacaf’s reticence, as its second-biggest member after the US was unequivocal in its support for the Fifa president. In a Fifa statement released under Infantino’s name on Wednesday, the world governing body had called for its institutional practices to be respected, a coded way of condemning any leadership challenge before next March’s scheduled presidential election, which the FMF endorsed.

“The Mexican Football Federation is convinced that football is its fundamental value and that its best defence lies in institutional integrity and respect for the governance and processes that safeguard it,” the FMF said. “Therefore, the FMF will not recognise or approve any process convened outside of this institutional framework, and it embraces the call issued by president Infantino on 5 August 2026 to collectively continue developing football for the benefit of its 211 member associations.

“The FMF supports president Infantino’s leadership in continuing to promote the development of football through institutional strengthening.”

The Argentina Football Association (AFA) followed Mexico’s lead by backing Infantino in a gushing tribute and expressing support for his leadership over the past decade. Unlike Concacaf, South America’s Conmebol appears united behind Infantino, while in an intriguing subplot there is growing speculation that Mexico would like to switch confederations to join the latter.

“In relation to the recent events that are public knowledge, we must recognise the decision of the administration to withdraw a project that generated, within the football family and from its inception, many more uncertainties than certainties,” the AFA statement read.

“That is why it is worth highlighting the acceptance of the errors made in this process and the apology expressed in the heartfelt message displayed to the 211 member associations of Fifa. Prioritising governance standards is a fundamental pillar for strengthening good relations between Fifa, its member associations and the confederations.

“In the same way, and as we have already expressed, you are leading a management that led to a profound transformation of Fifa, which opened the doors of the organisation to all member associations and confederations, so that with a frank and direct dialogue, we can, together, continue to promote football at all levels and disciplines.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“This transformation was based on a model of transparent governance, respect for statutory structures and the monitoring of democratic procedures, essential principles for the football family to be united, firm and working to continue generating improvements in sports and institutions, which have an impact on a better quality of life for millions of human beings who practise our beloved sport.

“Accordingly, with the upcoming Fifa congress approaching, the association that we proudly preside over firmly believes and reaffirms that the way forward is to continue to work under your leadership, so that we can continue to develop better and even more inclusive football.”

Earlier on Thursday, the Confederation of African Football had reaffirmed its support for Infantino, providing him with further allies as he fights to extend his 10-year reign.

Sports.title: Norway’s Klaveness tells Fifa president Infantino to resign: ‘There is no trust now’
Sports.content:
The Norwegian FA will ask Gianni Infantino to resign with immediate effect after his doomed attempt to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

Norway is the first federation to call directly for the Fifa president to step down after a series of controversies that came to a head with the crisis engulfing his Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme.

The decision was made at a meeting of the Norwegian Football Federation board (NFF) on Thursday night. Norway has consistently taken a lead in efforts to scrutinise Fifa’s governance and recent events have taken any faith in its leadership beyond the point of no return.

“We decided that there is no trust in Infantino now,” the NFF president, Lise Klaveness, told the Guardian. “We have been worried consistently and there has been one more step in worrying direction every year, every part of the year. The trust is now gone for us, there is no way back for Infantino.

“We’re left in a very polarised cooperation globally and, I would say, chaos. So we will ask him to resign immediately so that the global football community can look ahead and cooperate going into the future.”

The NFF is expected to formally write a letter requesting Infantino’s resignation in the coming week. Norway was among a handful of countries not to back his re-election as president next March, although several European federations have withdrawn their endorsement in the past week.

“We understand that we’re one country, but it’s our position,” Klaveness said. “It’s just one step further for us. We did not vote for him in 2023 but we hoped we would support him, he was elected and the reason why we were so clear in our statements was to really give the signal that we wanted him to implement the good reforms he was part of. But he didn’t, and now we will ask him to resign.”

The NFF agreed to demand a full review into the package of reforms passed upon Infantino’s ascent to the presidency in 2016, which were intended to extricate Fifa from the corruption crisis that had previously dogged the governing body. Klaveness said the investigation should ask “what was implemented, what was not, what should have been implemented and what we should also implement to make this a functioning organisation”.

Norway will also formalise a fresh complaint to Fifa’s ethics committee on three fronts, taking in the FFE scandal, the award of Fifa’s peace prize to Donald Trump and the Folarin Balogun affair at the World Cup. It will attempt to bring a number of major European federations on board for its submission in an effort to further increase the pressure on Infantino.

“We want the ethics committee to show their work transparently because this is a very big part of the issue,” Klaveness said. “There are all kinds of control mechanisms in place but they are not really holding the council and president accountable.”

View image in fullscreen Gianni Infantino leaves after attending the Wafcon match between Malawi and Zambia in Rabat. Photograph: AP

In June, the NFF wrote to the ethics committee supporting a complaint by the advocacy group FairSquare, which centred on alleged breaches of political neutrality by Infantino. It will now make a new submission that asks for the three situations to be considered individually. “We will join them in one letter but they are very different cases and we want the ethical committee to treat them separately,” Klaveness said.

The NFF is understood to have particular concerns that the timing of Infantino’s FFE offer, which promised federations significant financial gains if accepted, may constitute an abuse of position at this proximity to a presidential election. It has also been observed that the FFE scheme, had it been passed, would have locked in commitments extending well beyond Infantino’s term.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to The Recap The best of our sports journalism from the past seven days and a heads-up on the weekend’s action Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Similarly to its call for Infantino to step down, Norway is the first federation to adopt a public stance regarding the peace prize or Balogun case. Fifa’s decision to suspend the USA striker’s red card during the World Cup, meaning he was free to face Belgium in the last 16, came after Trump had called Infantino to discuss the ban.

Uefa’s federations have stood together in backing a potential boycott of Fifa competitions, a stance it reasserted on Thursday despite Infantino’s shelving of FFE. Klaveness said the move is not merely symbolic and is intended to bring swift results.

“There’s no point in Uefa standing in a war position for half a year,” she said. “That would not be good at all. Now it’s crucial that we do it because global football cooperation is at stake. It’s very good to see we have strong leadership in Uefa that knows now is crunch time for this case. We cannot sell out this core of football.”

The first competition in line for a boycott would be the Under-20 Women’s World Cup, which is due to start in Poland on 5 September, but Klaveness expects the continued turmoil to have been resolved by then.

“I hope and think it will not come to that,” she said. “A lot of water will go under the bridge before that. But this is why we ask Infantino to resign. It’s so unstable now that it’s a matter of time. He cannot recover this and we cannot put the sport on the spot. The biggest priority is to be together with Uefa and have this strong position.”

Klaveness and the NFF have held a consistent line in calling for scrutiny of Fifa’s operations since she assumed her position in March 2022. She has been vocal on human rights issues and governance standards within Fifa, criticising failings surrounding the Qatar World Cup and questioning the process that awarded Saudi Arabia the 2034 edition of the tournament.

Sports.title: England striker Ivan Toney charged with assault after Soho nightclub incident
Sports.content:
The England footballer Ivan Toney has been charged with assault after an incident at a nightclub in Soho in December last year.

Scotland Yard said the striker had been charged on 31 July with assault causing actual bodily harm. Toney, who plays for the Saudi Pro League club Al-Ahli, is due to appear at Westminster magistrates court on 24 September.

The Sun newspaper reported in December that Toney had been arrested after an alleged head-butt. It claimed a fan recognised the footballer and grabbed at him while seeking a photograph with him before the incident.

On Friday the Metropolitan police said the charges related to an incident on 6 December at a nightclub on Wardour Street in central London, reportedly the now-closed 100 Wardour Street.

A spokesperson for Toney said: “Ivan acknowledges the charge and although he is naturally shocked, he looks forward to being given the opportunity to clear his name in court.”

Toney was at the centre of one of the most curious transfers on deadline day in August 2024 when he completed a late move from Brentford to Al-Ahli worth a reported £40m. He has also played for Newcastle United and his home town club Northampton Town, as well as several others on loan as he looked to establish himself.

Seen as a late bloomer in football terms, he had made only two Premier League appearances before his 25th birthday, but went on to score 67 goals in 128 appearances over the next three seasons at the top level.

He has played 10 times for England, scoring once in a friendly match against Belgium in 2024, and was part of the 2026 World Cup squad, making appearances against Argentina in the semi-final and in the win over France as England finished third.

Sports.title: Boardroom struggle deepens gloom as West Ham prepare for life on the outside
Sports.content:
There have been 10 summers of West Ham’s London Stadium tenancy and a number of winters of discontent. As the Hammers kick off the new season on Saturday, a Carabao Cup first-round fixture with Portsmouth is a stark reminder of reduced circumstances, further confirmation of last season’s relegation from the Premier League. The summer has been as bleak as any of those winters, with a number of factors colliding to deepen the gloom of relegation.

Certain clubs, including West Ham back in 2011-12 when promotion was achieved at first time of asking under Sam Allardyce, have used the Championship to take a beat, to refresh and replenish. Can this be the case at West Ham 2026? The Hammers are short-odds favourites for promotion but behind the scenes it has been a summer of turbulence, particularly in the boardroom, where a power struggle is being fought.

Portsmouth will bring 9,000 supporters on Saturday but will David Sullivan be present? This week it was revealed the operators of London Stadium had recommended the former joint-chair (but still co-owner) stay away, because of the “potential for demonstrations and anti-social behaviour by some spectators”.

It is expected that Sullivan will turn up, despite a fans’ advisory board statement that his attendance would cause “offence and upset”. It has been suggested that he wants to enjoy the coming season as a fan and is happy to bide his time before any consideration of selling his 38.8% stake. Considering his personal circumstances, his attendance would be a brazenly unpopular act. On 25 May, when relegation was confirmed despite a home win over Leeds, Sullivan was forced to leave the stadium early for his own safety.

View image in fullscreen Daniel Kretinsky wants to increase his shares in West Ham to just under 50.1%. Photograph: David W Černý/Reuters

Sullivan continues to deny allegations of sexually exploitative and predatory behaviour towards women over several decades made by the BBC’s Panorama documentary in early June, though he stepped down from his role on the eve of the broadcast “to avoid disruption to the club while he addresses the matter privately”.

Even before those allegations became public, Sullivan was a lightning rod, lambasted for his stewardship of a club in vertiginous decline since winning the Europa Conference League in May 2023. The £100m fee received for Declan Rice that summer was frittered away. Fellow Prague hero Jarrod Bowen, the club captain, has pledged to stay on, tasked with leading the club back up.

Until his defenestration Sullivan had acted as the club’s de facto director of football, often to the frustration of those in the football department. His chief ally, Karren Brady, stepped down in April as storm clouds gathered, severing a working relationship that dated as far back as 1990.

Among the club’s support, 50,000 season tickets have been sold for the attempt at re-entry to the Premier League. The overriding desire among fans is for Sullivan to completely depart the scene. His announced departure had installed a modicum of optimism.

Potential new sheriffs are circling but the picture is complicated, any future direction opaque as a result. As Sullivan stepped down the expectation was that Daniel Kretinsky, the Czech billionaire owner of Royal Mail who has owned 27% of West Ham since 2021, would make his move. Instead, this week, he cut that share down to just under 25%, though this was part of a strategy.

Last weekend, the familiar face of Amanda Staveley entered the picture. In July 2024 she departed Newcastle, after her leading role in bringing in the Saudi Arabian Public Investment Fund, but now Staveley wants to return to football. Last September, she was linked with a takeover at Tottenham, and it is suggested she will use a similar source of funding to engineer her move for West Ham. Among Newcastle fans, with their club faltering this summer, Staveley’s energy is lamented. With her connections, some Hammers fan hope she could have a similar galvanising effect.

View image in fullscreen David Sullivan’s closet ally, Karren Brady, left the club in April. Photograph: PA Images/Alamy

The key is the 25% that belonged to the late David Gold, Sullivan’s former joint-chair. As Staveley loomed, Kretinsky appeared ready to take up his first refusal on purchasing that 25% from Vanessa Gold, David’s daughter and current co-chair. Adding that to his 27% would take him beyond 50.1%, leaving him liable for a formal takeover offer. But shifting 2% to a Czech ally, the entrepreneur Jakub Havrlant, now means he would be short of that obligation should he cut across Staveley’s ambitions by buying Gold’s stake. Sullivan’s shares also hold the balance of power and Staveley’s next move is keenly awaited.

While that plays out, what of football? The arrival of free agent, the former Brighton and Ajax defender, Joël Veltman, was the first addition of a summer where the sales of Mateus Fernandes to Tottenham and Crysencio Summerville to Al-Hilal fetched a collective £140m, commensurate to a year of Premier League TV money. Youth product Freddie Potts’ departure to Club Brugge for £10m disappointed some fans. Needs must if further players are to arrive. There is interest in Ireland’s World Cup playoff hero Troy Parrott, the striker at AZ Alkmaar, though attracting players to the Championship has its difficulties.

View image in fullscreen West Ham have cashed in on key players, such as Mateus Fernandes to Tottenham, to cushion their descent into the Championship. Photograph: Phil Walter/Getty Images

In the dugout remains Nuno Espírito Santo, who stayed when his departure had been expected. Nuno’s zen-like calm is required at a club where panic regularly sets in. The vacuum created by Sullivan’s situation, relegation and lack of transfer business heightens anxieties. A new season has arrived, with uninviting league fixtures against Burnley, Charlton, Watford and Wolves by 1 September. Karim Virani, previously a club employee who departed in 2020, more recently at Glasgow Rangers, has returned as interim chief executive. Attempts are being made to stitch West Ham into a semblance of unity.

This summer, the London Stadium played host to concerts from Take That and Metallica, and staged the Diamond League athletics meet in July, where Josh Kerr broke the world mile record. Thursday saw a bid confirmed to stage the 2029 World Athletics Championships, following an impasse between the club and the stadium owners. Further reminders that West Ham’s home will never be fully their own, 10 years after departing the Boleyn Ground.

Such were the terms Sullivan, Gold Sr and Brady agreed for a stadium that fans continue to resent, where Sullivan is unlikely to be made to feel welcome.

Sports.title: Football Daily | Vinícius Júnior and a fantasy world of transfers in the football lull
Sports.content:
THE CAPTIVE VOID OF NOBLE RAGE

“We were so close … At the end of the day, really, they made him an offer he couldn’t refuse … It shows where we’re trying to aim for the club … There has been a lot of stuff written in the papers that you have to take on the chin I’m afraid – they should be talking about how well the England cricket team are playing at the moment.” Words said not by Mikel Arteta about Arsenal missing out on Vinícius Júnior after the Brazilian megastar signed a new Real Madrid contract, but by Glenn Hoddle in 2002, as Tottenham missed out on signing … yes, Rivaldo. That last sentence was probably a dead giveaway. Tottenham’s solution to the Brazilian-shaped hole in their transfer ambitions was to sign Robbie Keane to his boyhood club. What might Arsenal do next? Eye up Cristian Romero, you say?

Arsenal’s unrequited chase for Vinícius brought to bear the fantasy world that fans reside in when the transfer window is open and no actual competitive football is being played. Just imagine what he might have done to defences in Our League. In that netherworld of reverie there are no wet Tuesday nights at Stoke, nobody gets knacked, nobody fails to settle, they just score a gazillion goals and outperform their xG. Imagine football heaven, it’s easy if you try.

There is a flip side. Transfer business, or lack thereof, can also lead to a summer of angst. See the social media disgrace wails of certain vocal fans at Liverpool and their exasperation that Virgil van Dijk, 73, is the sole senior Red Men centre-back. Perhaps the balm of signing Bradley Barcola will soothe, though that is not yet a DONE DEAL. Arsenal fans have already consoled themselves with the imminent addition of Bruno Guimarães; who needs Big Vin when the other Brazilian can supply passes to, er Gabriel Martinelli?

Each summer includes a deal that unlocks others. In a sign of the times, Madrid ponying up for a mega Vinícius deal rather than his doing one will likely shift tectonic plates. With him set to stay, Rodri whose winning of the 2024 Ballon d’Or caused an almighty strop from the Brazilian and his club, lest we forget, is now highly unlikely to head to the Bernabéu. With Kylian Mbappé already on silly money, and now Vinícius too, thus there is no room at the inn for the Spain captain. Instead, Manchester City’s main man and the Geopolitics World Cup’s very best player is said to want to join Barcelona, which would be a huge loss to his current club and Our League. Such is the transfer window, where it is far better to have loved and lost than never to have signed anyone at all.

LIVE ON BIG WEBSITE

It’s Friday night. It’s Littlewoods Cup time. Join Billy Munday for updates from Middlesbrough 0-0 Wrexham (1-0 on pens) from 8pm BST.

QUOTE OF THE DAY

“We have been worried consistently and there has been one more step in [a] worrying direction every year, every part of the year. The trust is now gone for us, there is no way back for Infantino” – Norwegian Football Federation president Lise Klaveness calls on Gianni Infantino to do one, although the civil war engulfing Fifa has deepened with Mexico and Argentina backing him.

View image in fullscreen Lise Klaveness, having none of it. Photograph: Amanda Pedersen Giske/EPA

That might go some way to proving it. It would also help the rest of us help to show them the error of their ways” – Peter Holford (no, I’m not the ever-forgiving reader).

Sports.title: Manchester City reject Barcelona’s opening £38.5m bid for Rodri as talks continue
Sports.content:
Manchester City have rejected an offer of £38.5m (€45m) from Barcelona for Rodri and want at least £60m before allowing Spain’s World Cup-winning captain to depart.

Barcelona have emerged as Rodri’s preferred destination after talks with Real Madrid broke down this week. It is understood that the 30-year-old, who is now in the final year of his contract at City, has agreed personal terms with the Spanish champions after indicating that he would like to return to his homeland following the departure of Pep Guardiola.

Rodri moved to the Etihad in 2019 from Atlético Madrid and has turned down the offer of a lucrative extension. Yet City are believed to be adamant that he will not be allowed to leave for less than their asking price. Barcelona are continuing negotiations in the hope of reaching a compromise.

Rodri, who won the Golden Ball awarded to the World Cup’s best player last month. spoke to Barça’s manager, Hansi Flick, and sporting director, Deco, about a potential move on Wednesday. The Spanish champions will be without midfielder Frenkie de Jong for several months after the Netherlands midfielder sustained a knee injury and have targeted Rodri as a replacement. He has had minor surgery on his back and will miss most of City’s pre-season programme.

City have signed Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest for £116m and remain in negotiations with Lille over a deal for Ayyoub Bouaddi. The Morocco midfielder could cost up to £80m but they could be tempted to bring in a more experienced replacement for Rodri should he depart, with Chelsea’s Enzo Fernández among those thought to be under consideration. The Argentinian is also wanted by Real, whose manager, José Mourinho is said to have not taken the news of being gazumped by their great rivals well. Reports in Spain have claimed that the 63-year-old is unhappy after making the signing of a central midfielder his priority after returning for a second stint at the Santiago Bernabéu.

Real have already brought in the winger Yan Diomande for £115m and Marc Cucurella, Bernardo Silva, Ibrahima Konaté, Denzel Dumfries and Carlos Espí so may have to balance the books by selling either Aurélien Tchouaméni and Eduardo Camavinga if they want to pursue Fernández.

Crystal Palace have confirmed the signing of Takehiro Tomiyasu after a successful trial period. The former Arsenal defender has been training with Palace during pre-season and has done enough to earn an initial 12-month deal with the option of extending that by another two years. Tomiyasu becomes new manager Pierre Sage’s second signing of the summer after the arrival of Óscar Mingueza on a free transfer. Palace are expected to complete a deal for the USA youth international Zavier Gozo from Real Salt Lake in MLS.

Sports.title: Tottenham and Atlético in talks over Romero with Van de Ven set to sign new deal
Sports.content:
Tottenham are in talks with Atlético Madrid over the sale of Cristian Romero after categorically rejecting Arsenal’s approach for the Argentina defender and are expected to agree a new five-year deal with Micky van de Ven.

Romero has made no secret of his desire to leave Spurs despite signing a new four-year contract at the start of last season and had looked set to join Inter for a fee of around £35m. But Atlético are long-term suitors of the 28-year-old and are thought to be his preferred destination, with Diego Simeone’s side understood to be prepared to match Inter’s bid.

Reports in Spain on Friday suggested that personal terms have already been agreed with Romero, although his move may have to wait for Atlético to free up space in their squad before they can complete the transfer. Nahuel Molina, Romero’s Argentina teammate, is expected to join Roma while Aston Villa are hoping to sign Matteo Ruggeri.

Arsenal had also made their interest known as they search for a replacement for William Saliba, with the Frenchman out for an extended period due to a back issue. However, Tottenham – who have signed defenders Jan Paul van Hecke and Marcos Senesi this summer – insisted that they did not want to sell to another Premier League club, least of all their north London rivals. Arsenal are also interested in Villa’s Ezri Konsa.

It is understood that Van de Ven had been considering his future in north London at the start of the summer after Tottenham narrowly avoided relegation last season. But the impact of the new manager, Roberto De Zerbi, has persuaded the Netherlands international to commit his future to the club after talks with his representatives.

Tottenham have already spent more than £200m on six new players this summer and are still in the market for a new attacker. Last week, De Zerbi said that they had “completed 60% of our project in the transfer market”.

Sports.title: Afcon’s biennial switch cost African governing body deal worth more than $1bn
Sports.content:
A deal worth at least $1bn in secured income over eight years was abandoned by the Confederation of African Football (Caf) because the governing body decided to switch the Africa Cup of Nations from a biennial to a four-yearly event, the Guardian can reveal.

On 5 July 2025, the eve of the delayed Women’s Africa Cup of Nations in Morocco, the Caf president, Patrice Motsepe, told the Guardian in Rabat, after a prolonged discussion of the bidding process at an executive committee meeting, that a decision on a winning bid would be made “in due course”.

“We announced in Addis Ababa this $1bn partnership that we are looking at over the next eight years. There is a lot of good progress that has been made,” he said.

On 23 July, four days after the World Cup final in New York, Caf opened a fresh tender for the marketing and commercial rights of the 2028, 2032 and 2036 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) tournaments, with bidders given until 24 August to hand in their bid books.

The tender is in complete contrast to the 2025 bidding round, in which the entirety of Caf’s competition portfolio was bundled for sale.

Luxolo September, Caf’s head of communications, confirmed that the change in Afcon frequency is wholly responsible for the abandonment of the 2025 bidding round that was on the verge of completion.

“As foreshadowed by the president in his comments last year, following the receipt and evaluation of bids and presentations from the bidders, in the second half of 2025, Caf entered into detailed discussions with shortlisted bidders regarding the precise terms and conditions of their proposals.

“However, at its meeting on 20 December 2025, the Caf executive committee took a unanimous decision – in the interest of African football – to move the Afcon to a four-year cycle, bringing the competition into alignment with the international match calendar,” September said. “This was a significant decision for African football. That executive committee decision materially changed the scope of the commercial rights available for tender, with the result that the 2025 ITT (Invitation To Tender) process could no longer proceed in its existing form.”

View image in fullscreen Patrice Motsepe (left) said in 2025 that ‘good progress’ was being made over a $1bn deal for Caf. Photograph: Angela Weiss/AFP/Getty Images

It has been seven years since Caf has had a long-term deal to secure its financial future. The 2016-2028 billion-dollar “minimum guarantee” revenue contract that it signed with the French company Lagardère during the tenure of Issa Hayatou, the late Cameroonian president of Caf, was the first of its kind for the organisation.

“The Memorandum of Understanding with Lagardère was agreed by a team I led with Hicham [El Amrani, then Caf general secretary] in May 2015, in Zurich,” Suketu Patel, then chair of Caf’s finance committee, said in 2019.

“On that same day, we met with Infront. Their indicative offer on the table was a $450m minimum guarantee for eight years, as opposed to the $1bn, for 12 years, from Lagardère.

“If you look at our earlier contract of 2009, we had a minimum guarantee of $150m, but our income for the period was actually around $350m. We anticipated that the 12-year contract would have yielded about $1.3bn.

“I can tell you that whilst President Hayatou and I had differences on political matters, we never had one on the management of Caf finances. He did not interfere with the processes established for good governance.”

But that agreement was unilaterally terminated in December 2019 during the tenure of Ahmad Ahmad, Hayatou’s successor as Caf president.

A protracted legal dispute at the International Chamber of Commerce led to Caf, just over a year into the presidency of Motsepe, paying Lagardère a final settlement of $50m, as compensation for the breach of contract, just before the 2022 World Cup in Qatar.

“There is no way that any sponsor will be prepared to pay the same amount of money for a deal in which you would normally have four Afcons over an eight-year period, when you will now only have two. That is certainly a no-brainer,” said a former FA president with expertise in financial matters.

Sports.title: EFL club’s chairman responds to Adrian Durham’s shock relegation claim
Sports.content:
Peterborough United chairman Darragh MacAnthony has called for calm in the transfer market amid Adrian Durham's relegation fears.

Speaking on talkSPORT Breakfast, Posh fan Durham voiced his concerns that the club's lack of activity in the summer window has the club at serious risk of the drop.

3 Posh are aiming for a return to the second tier after four seasons away Credit: Getty

"We lost three of our best players this summer, they've not been replaced," Durham said.

"We haven't signed a player for a month.

"The manager, Luke Williams, says Posh are targeting promotion. With the squad we've got right now, Posh will be relegated.

"If they don't add at least four players to go straight in the first team, a right-back, a winger, a No.10 and a six, Peterborough will be in massive trouble."

Patience is a virtue

However, MacAnthony, who has been the club's chairman since 2006, was quick to allay Durham's fears and claimed Posh are quietly working from a transfer shortlist that has been in place since May.

"I can basically give up what we're trying to do and I can go sign plan C, D and E, and they're not the players we wanted," MacAnthony said on talkSPORT's White and Jordan.

"Or, I can just hang in there and play this the way I'm playing it, which I think will be the right thing for our football club.

"We do need four or five signings, potentially five."

One position MacAnthony didn't believe needed upgrading was the right-back spot.

At present, 21-year-old James Dornelly and Carl Johnston are the main options to play on the right side of defence, with MacAnthony describing the duo as 'two very good right-backs and everyone knows that.'

3 MacAnthony is comfortable with Posh waiting for the right player rather than stressing in the transfer market Credit: talkSPORT

"We have a good young squad, we have a great manager," MacAnthony continued.

"They've been working their backsides off all summer and I just hate the fact they're getting hammered.

"The manager, his staff, the work they've put in with the players... And it's not just Adrian, it's everyone else saying, 'They're going to be bottom, they're going to be relegated.'

"My god, cut us some slack."

MacAnthony: 'Everyone forgets' we've made play-offs in three of last five seasons

It must be noted Durham did back MacAnthony to bring in the right players as Posh look to avoid a similar slump in League One.

Accelerated by injuries to three of the club's best players, Peterborough won just one of their last 15 league fixtures.

3 Williams has won 14 of his first 37 games in charge of the club Credit: Getty

The alarming run of form meant Posh ended the season in 18th and four points clear of the relegation zone.

Yet MacAnthony was quick to point out that type of season is an exception rather than the norm in recent years and reiterated a message of patience in the transfer market.

"I know we finished really badly, but it's not where Peterborough wants to be," MacAnthony said.

"Three of the last five years, we've been in the play-offs, but everyone forgets that.

"I know what we need, the manager knows what we need. But we want the ones we want. What we don't want is worse options."

Sports.title: Ex-Arsenal star joins Premier League rival on free transfer after successful trial
Sports.content:
Crystal Palace have completed the signing of ex-Arsenal defender Takehiro Tomiyasu on a free transfer, talkSPORT understands.

The Japan international joins the Eagles after a successful trial, having been without a club since his departure from Ajax at the end of the 2025/26 campaign.



5 Tomiyasu is looking for a new club after spending the first part of his summer at the World Cup with Japan Credit: Getty

An Eagle has landed

After training with Palace in recent weeks, Tomiyasu has now been officially confirmed as the club's second summer signing.

His arrival follows Spanish defender Oscar Mingueza, who also moved to Selhurst Park on a free transfer following his exit from LaLiga outfit Celta Vigo.

Tomiyasu joined up with with Palace last week for their pre-season training in Como, Italy.



He later featured in their friendly win over Al Ula on Friday, with his performance paving a way for a return to the Premier League.

Reacting to his move back to English football, Tomiyasu told Palace: “I’m excited to get started.



"This club is in a good moment, winning three titles in two seasons. Here is where I wanted to be.”

Comeback trail

Tomiyasu's arrival in south London brings an end to his period as a free agent after leaving Ajax at the end of last season.



He joined the Dutch giants in December after mutually agreeing to end his contract with Arsenal last summer.

The Japan star signed for the club whilst still recovering from a long-term knee injury that had kept him out of action for almost a year prior.

But having only penned a six-month deal until the end of the season, Tomiyasu ultimately departed having made just nine appearances.

5 Tomiyasu was a fan favourite at Arsenal, despite being heavily affected by injury Credit: Getty



5 Pierre Sage is looking to make his mark at Conference League winners Crystal Palace Credit: Getty

He went on to feature three times for Japan in their run to the last-32 of the 2026 World Cup.

With a number of Palace's first-team stars yet to report back for training after the World Cup, they Tomiyasu was allowed to join the team to train and work on his fitness ahead of the new season.

And it appears he took full advantage of the opportunity, with Tomiyaus now set to bring vital Premier League experience to Selhurst Park.



Crystal Palace are currently gearing up for their first season under new boss Pierre Sage, who was named as Oliver Glasner's successor in June.

They had been in the market for a new defender as key man Maxence Lacroix leaving to join Chelsea in a deal worth £52m.

talkSPORT previously reported that Palace were considering Augsburg’s Chrislain Matsima as a potential replacement, while Tomiyasu himself is capable of playing at centre-back.

5 Tomiyasu featured in just one game in his final season at Arsenal due to a knee injury Credit: Getty



Fresh start

Tomiyasu is looking to get his career back on track after seeing his last few seasons blighted by injury.

He departed Arsenal in July 2025 following the mutual decision to terminate his contract a year early, and had not featured for the club since the previous October.

The Japan star had missed the start of the 2024/25 season due to a previous knee injury that needed surgery in 2023.

But another knee issue saw him go under the knife again in January 2025, ultimately leading to his early departure from north London.



Tomiyasu joined Arsenal from Serie A side Bologna in a deal rising to £20million in 2021, and featured 84 times overall, scoring two goals and providing two assists.

After joining Ajax in December last year, he made his debut in January, but only eight further appearances followed.

5 Tomiyasu hadn't started a league game for any club in almost two seasons before his full Ajax debut in March Credit: Getty

The ex-Premier League star ultimately played only 236 minutes of football, failing to earn a new contract as the Amsterdam outfit finished a disappointing fifth in the Eredivisie.



Following his departure, Tomiyasu penned an emotional statement, where he shared his sadness at not having played a bigger role.

He wrote on Instagram: “It was only five months but I would like to thank all who support Ajax.

“Obviously it was not the season we wanted and no one is satisfied with how it ended.

“Personally, I joined this club in January after such a long rehab, I wanted to give much more, I should have done much more for this club but it didn’t work out well."

Sports.title: Coventry stay up as established Premier League team get relegated in EFL club owner’s predictions
Sports.content:
Coventry stay up as established Premier League team get relegated in EFL club owner’s predictions

Darragh MacAnthony has named Fulham as surprise relegation candidates in the upcoming Premier League season, while backing Coventry to stay up.

In what promises to be another hugely competitive affair, a number of managers head into the 2026/27 campaign with a point to prove - not least Sky Blues boss Frank Lampard and Fulham's Alvaro Arbeloa.



8 Alvaro Arbeloa is beginning just his second senior managerial role at Fulham Credit: Getty

After ending Coventry's 25-year Premier League exile by guiding them to Championship glory, Lampard is bidding to prove himself once again at the top of English football.

The Chelsea great now faces perhaps his biggest task yet as a manager, as he looks to steer his side clear of relegation.

Lampard faces unfavourable odds here - as do fellow promoted clubs Ipswich and Hull - with teams who come up from the second tier typically struggling with the jump and heading straight back down a year later.



And while the newly-promoted trio are an obvious tip for the drop, some new faces in other dugouts may give these sides hope.

This summer sees a record nine Premier League clubs set to begin the season with a new permanent manager, and perhaps the most eye-catching appointment has been Alvaro Arbeloa at Fulham.



The Spaniard was named as Marco Silva's successor at Craven Cottage, marking an immediate return to management after being replaced by Jose Mourinho at Real Madrid in June.

But Arbeloa's appointment has left some scratching their heads, whose first-ever senior coaching stint oversaw a rare trophyless season at the Santiago Bernabeu last term.



Ful of worry?

Discussing the fight against relegation, Peterborough chairman MacAnthony labelled Fulham's summer of upheaval a concern.

As well as a change in the dugout, the Whites have also lost key men Harry Wilson, Issa Diop and Raul Jimenez, while they have spent a combined £42m to sign young duo Gonzalo Garcia and Cesar Palacios from Real Madrid.

On Fulham's prospects, MacAnthony told talkSPORT: “Fulham obviously are the one where you go, manager - I didn't really overly rate him at Real Madrid. They're bringing Spanish players in.

8 Alvaro Arbeloa is beginning just his second senior managerial role at Fulham Credit: Getty



8 Harry Wilson scored 10 Premier League goals from midfield in the 2025/26 campaign Credit: Getty

MacAnthony was also unconvinced by Arbeloa's managerial credentials, who questioned his 64 per cent win rate at Real Madrid.

To this, MacAnthony said: “Anything under 80 per cent is poor in Madrid.

“[Marco] Silva was a brilliant manager for Fulham. So you're wondering the hangover of him leaving. You’ve got Spanish players who sometimes take a little while, young Spanish players, to adjust.



“So maybe there might be some concerns there. We don't know."

He added: “Fulham - the model of signing these Madrid boys, these younger players, losing Harry Wilson, the goals, the assists, even the menace, they've lost players that scored goals last year.

“I'm slightly concerned for them.”

8 Lampard heads into the Premier League season off the back of a standout promotion-winning campaign Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Super Frank

Moving on to the newly-promoted sides, MacAnthony gave Coventry a fighting chance of staying up due to their attacking threat.

Lampard's side were the Championship's top-scoring team last seaon with a huge 97 goals, with three members of their forward line reaching double digits - Haji Wright, Brandon Thomas-Asante and Ellis Simms.



By the same logic, MacAnthony tipped Ipswich and Hull to struggle due to a lack of proven goals, while he highlighted Lampard's past experience in guiding Everton to Premier League survival in 2022.

He continued: “I look at the three coming up and I go, Coventry are the favourites out of the three to stay up.

“Before Ipswich fans come at me, Hull fans, I look at the goals. And I know you're going to say, 'Championship goals', and whatever else. I just look at the way Lampard plays - he had experience where he was in a dog battle with Everton.

"So you've got manager experience of dealing with the stress of that. I think that's going to be really advantageous.”



8 USA striker Haji Wright scored 17 league goals last term to help fire Coventry to promotion Credit: Offside via Getty

8 MacAnthony believes Coventry's firepower sets them apart from other promoted sides - despite Hull's Oli McBurnie scoring 18 league goals last season Credit: AFP

On Lampard, MacAnthony added: “He is [a Premier League legend], but that means nothing now that he's a manager.

“And I think he's a superb manager. And I was hot on criticizing him for getting opportunities other people wouldn't get early on.



“But I love and respect the fact that he dropped down and took Coventry, when obviously [Mark] Robbins had done a good job, but it was going stale, he walked in when they were what, fifth, sixth bottom. And the football last year was great to watch."

MacAnthony added: “I honestly look at their personnel, their players, the attack, the way they play - I think they'll be good.”

Tall order?

MacAnthony was less optimistic about the Premier League's other new boys Ipswich and Hull, who he feels are yet to strengthen in the necessary areas this summer.

After winning the Championship Play-Off final, Hull have so far only spent money on goalkeepers Jack Butland and Konstantinos Tzolakis.



8 Gary O'Neil has returned to the Premier League with Ipswich Credit: Getty

8 Peterborough owner MacAnthony admitted Hull and Ipswich could struggle this season Credit: talkSPORT

Meanwhile Ipswich have a new boss in Gary O'Neil following the departure of promotion-winning manager Kieran McKenna.

Their standout signings so far have been winger Abdul Fatawu's £20m arrival from Leicester, while forward Daizen Maeda has joined from Celtic for £10m.



On the two sides , MacAnthony said: “If I was to pick any, I would say obviously your usual favourites - I'd imagine Hull are probably the first favourites because they still have a lot of business to do. so that could change.

“Ipswich need goals potentially and that was I think the issue last time [when they were relegated in the 2024/25 campaign].

"Even though obviously they had the Man City boy they sold to Chelsea - Liam Delap - but he's still not scoring enough to keep them up. So they really [worry me].

“I think there's goals in Coventry, and I just think in that league you score enough goals, the goals in the team for teams who struggle, that keeps you in that league.



"And I do worry about those two newcomers."

Sports.title: Where to watch Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund: Mikel Arteta hints at team news with timeline for player returns
Sports.content:
Where to watch Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund: Mikel Arteta hints at team news with timeline for player returns

Arsenal return to the Emirates this weekend for the first time since being crowned Premier League champions.

The Gunners continue their pre-season with the Emirates Cup, welcoming German giants Borussia Dortmund to London.



7 Arteta is preparing his squad for their return to London for pre-season action where he will welcome back his captain Credit: Getty

Mikel Arteta's men are just two games into their preparations for the new campaign, taking on Spanish opposition so far.

They thrashed Girona 4-1 in their opening friendly before taking on Real Betis on Wednesday, which they lost 3-1 in Dublin.

“I'm disappointed with the result," Mikel Arteta told arsenal.com. "We are here to win football matches.



“We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

“I’m very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It's true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that's the learning from today.”



As for Dortmund, they've played four games already this summer, winning two and losing two of their outings.

The Bundesliga side have just returned from Japan, where they came out on top against Tokyo but lost to Cerezo Osaka.



Where to watch the match

This Emirates Cup clash will take place on Sunday, August 9.

Kick-off at the Emirates Stadium is scheduled for 2pm.

This is Arsenal's first match back at home since their 1-0 win over Burnley in May before lifting the Premier League title on the final day of last season as champions at Selhurst Park having beaten Crystal Palace.

7 Arsenal lost their first match of pre-season friendlies when Real Betis beat them 3-1 Credit: Getty

7 Former Arsenal defender Hector Bellerin was among the familiar faces in Dublin Credit: Getty

7 Arsenal fans and players got a reminder of what they were preparing to defend in the coming season at the Aviva Stadium Credit: Getty



Fans will be able to watch the action live on the Gunners' website and app, via their Pre-Season Pass.

talkSPORT and talkSPORT.com will also keep you up to date with all the latest news, scores and reaction during pre-season.

7 The Emirates is hosting the Emirates Cup, the glamorous annual pre-season tournament involving Arsenal Credit: Getty



What is the Emirates Cup?

The first Emirates Cup game was played 19 years ago in 2007.

It is a friendly clash that has been played yearly in various formats to celebrate the partnership with club sponsor Emirates.

When the event was first founded, four teams competed in a group stage, with each team playing two matches each.

However, more recently, it has changed to a simple one-off tie.

Arsenal have won the Emirates Cup nine times since its creation, aiming to make it to double digits this pre-season.

7 Arsenal captain Odegaard is back training after his World Cup exploits and could play against Dortmund Credit: Getty



Last year, the Gunners beat Athletic Bilbao 3-0 thanks to goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz.

What is the current team news?

Gabriel and Gabriel Martinelli should both be back to feature for Arsenal after rejoining the squad post-World Cup after playing for Brazil.

Meanwhile, Ecuador's Piero Hincapie, who joined the club in a permanent transfer, Germany international Havertz and Sweden striker Gyokeres will continue to get minutes following their earlier return from the tournament.

A host of other big names are due back soon, too, Arteta confirmed as he attempted to offer a timeline for key names returning.



“It has been ten days away from home," he said in reference to the pre-season tour. "So we’re looking forward to coming back, seeing some players as well."

Mikel Merino, Martin Zubimendi and David Raya all won the World Cup with Spain and were given extra-time to recover, while Eberechi Eze, Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka all played for England.

7 Bellingham is following in brother Jude's footsteps in Germany and could play against Arsenal Credit: Getty

"Martin [Odegaard] will be back and then the English and Spanish internationals will be back soon as well. So, we're going to start to have more and more players at the moment, we still miss a lot of them.”



Jurrien Timber remains a fitness worry in pre-season.

For Dortmund, 20-year-old England U21 international Jobe Bellingham is sure to feature, along with World Cup star Felix Nmecha in midfield.

Ex-Chelsea midfielder Carney Chukwuemeka was substituted with a knock last time out, so he is a doubt.

Sports.title: Where to watch Liverpool vs Monaco: Andoni Iraola marks milestone and reveals Victor Munoz decision
Sports.content:
Where to watch Liverpool vs Monaco: Andoni Iraola marks milestone and reveals Victor Munoz decision

Liverpool have returned from their pre-season tour of the United States, but their friendly action continues at Anfield.

New Reds boss Andoni Iraola will be in the home dugout at the stadium for the first time, as his side welcome Monaco.

4 It's not a competitive game, but it still marks a first for Iraola as he takes charge of his first home game as Liverpool manager Credit: Getty

Fans could also see new signing Victor Munoz in action for the first time, too.

The manager told fans the no.23 made the decision to cut short his holiday to link up with his new teammates early having been given an extended break after winning the World Cup with Spain.

"You need time to adapt when you are moving to a new club and a new country so for me it was a case of the earlier I could get started, the better," he told the club's official website.

Asked if he will play against Monaco, he added: "Well, I think I’m ready. Obviously if the coach says so after training and asks me to feature in the starting XI, I’ll be there. I’m keen and I can’t wait to get started. [Against] Monaco, why not?"

So far this summer, Iraola's side have won two and lost one of their outings, being beaten 4-2 by Leeds last time out.

That disappointing result followed a 1-0 win over Wrexham and a 4-2 victory against Sunderland in the States.

As for Monaco, they've won just one of their three friendlies so far, beating French lower-league side Saint Priest 5-2.

After that win, they lost to Sporting Lisbon and then were held to a 2-2 draw against Belgian outfit Cercle Brugge.

Frimpong asked to be substituted last time out, but Iraola said post-match that he had not picked up an injury.

As for Monaco, former Arsenal striker Mika Biereth is set to feature, along with ex-West Ham defender Thilo Kehrer.

4 Liverpool will pay tribute to legend Keegan at the match Credit: Getty

Liverpool have announced that a series of tributes will take place at Anfield in the coming weeks for legend Kevin Keegan.

Keegan, who scored 100 goals in 323 appearances for the Reds, sadly passed away in July.

A statement from the club reads: "Supporters attending the Monaco game will also see special tributes displayed on Anfield's LED screens, with a period of applause observed before kick-off and players wearing black armbands.

"This will be the club's first home fixture since Keegan's passing and will provide an opportunity for fans to remember one of LFC's greatest players.

"LFC are also in direct contact with Newcastle United ahead of the Premier League opener at St. James' Park regarding special tributes to Keegan, who represented both clubs so successfully and managed the Magpies.
