Sports.title: Why Honda only realised the scale of its F1 problems in January
Sports.content:
Heading into Formula 1's major technical overhaul, expectations at Aston Martin were high. With a state-of-the-art factory in Silverstone, legendary designer Adrian Newey and a works partnership with Honda, all the ingredients for success appeared to be in place.

That may still prove to be the case in the longer term, but the start of the new era has proved far more challenging than anticipated. Mike Krack recently admitted that Aston Martin had barely been racing before the summer break, simply because the gap to newcomer Cadillac amounted to around one second.

That changed when the AMR26 received its first major upgrade package in Hungary, although the chassis is naturally only part of the story. Honda has also encountered numerous problems since officially returning to F1, ranging from vibrations that troubled the drivers during the opening weeks of the season to a significant deficit in outright performance.

Speaking in an exclusive interview with Autosport, trackside manager and chief engineer Shintaro Orihara explained that the full extent of those problems only became clear in January.

“So, probably at the end of last year, our position was not so bad,” he said. “Still, performance and drivability were in the development stage, but it looked okay.

"But in January, we realised that in some of the areas we found some, not issues, but we realised that performance was always up, down, up, down. So we found some performance, but then we also found some reliability issues."

Shintaro Orihara, Honda Photo by: EYE4images / NurPhoto via Getty Images

Because reliability is always a top priority, Honda had to take a step back on several performance gains to ensure reliability at that performance level. Naturally, that slowed down its overall development.

"In January, we realised that our performance and reliability would not be competitive,” Orihara added. “When we started running in Barcelona, we realised that our performance was definitely poor compared to the other manufacturers. And also, we found some issues on the battery side."

Those battery-related issues made the development process more complex. They cost valuable track time during winter testing, something that was especially painful given Aston Martin and Honda's need to gather data to recover from their deficit.

"So we realised that we were not in good position, maybe at beginning of this year. Last year, at end of last year, we already saw that we were not competitive, but we didn't expect it so bad," Orihara admitted.

What has been Honda's biggest challenge?

Part of the explanation is that Honda's current F1 project is very different from its successful years with Red Bull, something that ties in with the company's philosophy of transferring F1 knowledge to other parts of the company.

Another part of the explanation is, according to Honda, the complexity of the current regulations. Orihara stressed that there has not been one single stumbling block ahead of 2026, but rather the combination of all the changes introduced at the same time.

Honda Power Unit Launch

"It's difficult to say which component of the power unit is most challenging because in this regulation, everything has changed a lot,” said Orihara. “For example, MGU-K power changed from, let's say, [120] to 350 kilowatts. That is a significant change.

"But also on the internal combustion engine side, we have changed the fuel flow rate. So in this regulation, everything has been changed so much. So, a challenging point for Honda is just the combination of a lot of changes happening at the same time."

That means Honda is lacking outright power from its internal combustion engine, something the long-awaited Zandvoort upgrade is specifically designed to address. It is intended to be the first step towards reducing the brand's still significant performance deficit.

On the electrical side of the power unit, the emphasis is on efficiency. However, Orihara explained that the changes there have also had a major impact on drivability – one of the areas that has been a recurring topic for Honda and Aston Martin in the opening months of the season.

"Removing the MGU-H has also been quite challenging on the power unit side,” he said.

“Probably that is the most exciting point for power unit manufacturers. I have always been mentioning drivability. That is, maybe not mainly, but the majority of that is coming from removing the MGU-H.

"So that is a challenging point for us as a power unit supplier, to keep the boost pressure at a target. Again, it's difficult to pick one component that has been most challenging for us, but it has been the combination of all changes at the same time."

Although Honda knows that returning to the competitive level it is targeting will take time - a lot of time - it hopes to make a first step at Zandvoort. That upgrade is focused purely on improving the internal combustion engine and was already tested during a filming day at the Hungaroring.

Sports.title: Why McLaren has been coy about introducing its rotating F1 rear wing
Sports.content:
McLaren will race its version of the so-called 'Macarena' rear-wing concept – but not until an unspecified point in the future, according to team principal Andrea Stella.

It's understood that the reason for not rushing to race the new rear wing is not linked to Red Bull's well-documented issues with its similar design. Instead, McLaren is being cautiously pragmatic, since the rotating rear wing adds to the complexities of managing car behaviour as it moves in and out of Straight Line Mode (SLM).

McLaren planned to test its new wing in Austria but made a late decision to abandon the evaluation. It then waited until Hungary to run it for the first time in FP1 on Oscar Piastri's car, driven by Leonardo Fornaroli, before parking it for the remainder of the event.

Max Verstappen crashed at the Red Bull Ring and Silverstone, prompting his Red Bull team to temporarily shelve its pivoting rear wing based on suspicions that a delay in airflow reattachment when the wing returned to cornering mode made Verstappen's car unstable.

"I have to say it's been a complicated project," Stella told media including Autosport.

"Which was no surprise because when we saw Ferrari introducing the wing in Bahrain test and testing it in China in the first lap, [Lewis] Hamilton spun. And then it took a few more events to actually being in condition to race it.

"We knew it was going to be a complex project, so I have to say that our engineering department has delivered this project in a way that looks well-behaved – like the wing in terms of mechanical actuation, times of the actuation, because there's some limitations by the regulations, not only for aerodynamic reasons.

Ferrari was the first team to run its rotating rear wing, which operates differently to the McLaren and Red Bull examples Photo by: Alastair Staley / LAT Images via Getty Images

"And then the overall behaviour from an aerodynamic point of view, reattachment – so the time it takes for the car to regain the load, not only the load on the wing, the load on the entire car as driven from the wing.

"All this I have to say has been pretty consistent with expectation, so it's been a positive sign off of this concept and we look forward now to introducing this concept at some future events."

These concepts are a classic example of thinking-outside-the-box creative engineering that is possible for the first time this season because the regulations are relatively open. F1 first adopted the principle of legally shedding drag in a straight line with the Drag Reduction System (DRS) in 2011, which permitted the upper rear wing plane to flatten in prescribed areas of the track.

The speed and actuation procedure for this was clearly defined, along with the dimensions of the wing planes themselves. But under the new ruleset introduced this season, in which front and rear wing flaps can open in specified Straight Line Mode zones, the speed of transition from one state to the other is defined (within 0.4s), but not the means by which it moves between open and closed.

McLaren's pivoting rear wing is closer to Red Bull's than Ferrari's, in that it uses a central actuator to manage the rotation rather than having a mechanism built into the endplates. Also like Red Bull's, it pivots forwards rather than backwards.

The means of actuation gives it an element of air braking as it closes. The trade-off between the two concepts is that Red Bull and McLaren accept a degree of aerodynamic blockage from the actuator and its shroud in exchange for having a wider space between the upper and lower planes when SLM is active.

Ferrari's also has to take a longer path between open and closed because of the angle of rotation.

Verstappen shunted in qualifying in Austria, and a delay in airflow reattachment to the rear wing was cited as one possible contributory factor Photo by: Getty Images

One of the less predictable effects of the new regulations has been the shift in tyre loading during the transition between SLM being on and off. This is because the airflow doesn't reattach to the wing planes instantly, but takes fractions of a second to re-establish its path.

Teams knew ahead of the season that this would be a significant performance factor, but were unable to measure it accurately with simulation tools such as the wind tunnel and Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD).

The true extent of the shifts in loadings, and their effect on car behaviour, could only be measured at the track.

This also applies to the theoretical benefits of the rotating rear wings. The airflow around the rear of an F1 car is tremendously busy because of the interaction between the car's aerodynamic surfaces and the turbulent wake of the rear wheels.

Simulating this with great accuracy is very difficult in the wind tunnel, where model size is capped at 60% scale and the wind is generally blowing in one direction. Historically it is difficult to access a car's aerodynamic performance when it's in a state of yaw (i.e. turning), or facing different wind directions. The different deflection properties of the model tyres, as well as their smaller size, also has a tendency to skew results.

Hence McLaren has done a lot of FP1 running with large aero rakes fitted behind the rear wheels to validate substantial bodywork changes such as the latest-spec floor, introduced in Hungary, as well as its pivoting wing. Practical measurements trackside are the real proof (or otherwise) of any theoretical gains.

"There was a question about comparison with Red Bull, but I don't think the wind tunnel is a major factor in terms of determining the aerodynamic behaviour in reattachment," Stella said.

"I think you can use some other tools for that, and then the most important tool, especially when you have this sort of complicated project, even from an aerodynamic point of view, remains what you observe at the track. So it was important for us to acquire data here trackside, because you would have never relied on a wind tunnel only for such a delicate project."

Sports.title: Why the FIA couldn't intervene sooner over F1's 2026 rules
Sports.content:
With the first Formula 1 season under the new technical regulations approaching its halfway point, the summer break provides a good opportunity to take stock. The 2026 rules, with their much greater emphasis on electric power, have sparked considerable debate both in and outside the paddock.

F1 insists that fan ratings – for example in its own Formula 1 Fan Voice programme – have been largely positive, but drivers have been far more critical.

Max Verstappen described the power unit regulations as "Formula E on steroids" during winter testing in Bahrain, while Oscar Piastri spoke at Spa-Francorchamps about the "self-learning elements" of the power units and "qualifying grids being decided by computers behaving or misbehaving".

Asked by Autosport whether the criticism from drivers over the past few months had been stronger than the FIA expected, Tombazis responded: "I think drivers are, by definition, quite demanding clients. I don't think we expected them to have a sugarcoat or to not speak their minds. So to say that it's been more than expected, no, I wouldn't say so."

The complaints from drivers about energy management, super clipping and algorithms were also in line with what the FIA had anticipated, according to its single-seater director.

"We did anticipate a lot of these things that they have complained about in the two years before the launch of the season. We did try to make some adjustments, but we failed with the governance that was in place," Tombazis said. "So I think it was realistically only to be expected."

Energy-starved circuits such as Silverstone and Spa-Francorchamps have highlighted the shortcomings of the 2026 regulations Photo by: Guido De Bortoli / LAT Images via Getty Images

FIA tried to listen to F1 drivers' criticism in build-up to 2026

If it had been up to Tombazis, the changes to the regulations that have now been agreed for 2027 and 2028 – to gradually move to a 60-40 split – would ideally have been introduced much earlier.

"I think it's a bit of a shame that we had to wait until we discussed things in May and get to a package for 2027 and for 2028. I think we could have ideally done that a couple of years before and then there wouldn't have been all of this discussion," Tombazis said.

Several drivers warned about potential problems with the new engine regulations before 2026. Verstappen was the first to do so publicly during the 2023 Austrian Grand Prix, when Autosport asked him about his initial simulator runs with the new engine formula.

That has perhaps created the impression that drivers were not listened to in the years leading up to 2026, but Tombazis insists the reality is different. According to him, the initial feedback was taken seriously, but the governance framework meant the regulations could not be significantly revised.

"When OEMs decide to participate as PU manufacturers, they sign a governance agreement that is binding towards all parties, so the FIA, FOM and the PU manufacturers. It's similar to what the Concorde Agreement does for the team side of things," Tombazis explained.

"And there was a separate governance agreement signed in 2022 in order to basically outline the requirements for the PU manufacturers during the years of 2023, 2024 and 2025. That is before the championship started because there's such things like financial regulations for the first time."

The FIA states that governance, even with new manufacturers such as Audi, has made intervention impossible Photo by: Pirelli

Among other things, that agreement stipulated that new entrants would not be allowed to spend unlimited amounts of money to develop their 2026 power units.

"If a PU manufacturer who was not participating in Formula 1, let's say Audi, they still had to be bound by regulations and not come to us and say, well, we're not participating, hence we can spend five times the money. That would be unfair," he said.

"So that's why there was a governance agreement that on the one hand forced them to be bound by the regulations, including the financial and operational rules and all of that."

At the same time, that document made it much harder for the FIA to reopen the regulations in the years leading up to 2026 without securing a supermajority.

"On the other hand it put limitations as to how much we could change things unilaterally as the FIA. And therefore any change had to be approved by a significant number of the PU manufacturers," Tombazis explained.

"So for the sort of changes we did [in May], we needed at least four of them to agree. And quite simply, four of them did not agree during the years when we discussed some adjustments."

Tombazis had hoped that the changes for the coming years could have been implemented sooner Photo by: Lars Baron / Getty Images

Challenges known since 2022, but races still entertaining

Part of the reason for that was that the reality of the automotive industry looked very different at the time, with manufacturers placing a much greater emphasis on electrification.

"Overall, it was always a challenging target to have a close to 50-50 power split between the two units," Tombazis said.

"But that was a very important position for the OEMs participating, and frankly having to decide whether they want to be in Formula 1 or not. Don't forget that if we didn't have them in, we would have just two power units in Formula 1, which I think would have been a bit of an issue. So that requirement to have a much stronger electrical part did create these difficulties."

Tombazis explained that the FIA had already become aware of these challenges in 2022, a year before Verstappen publicly voiced his concerns, but by then it was simply too late to fundamentally alter the regulations.

"As simulations came in back in 2022 or so, we knew there were these issues, but we were a bit too far down the line there to change things and some people had committed too much resource," he said. "So that left us slightly on the back foot at the start of the season, discussing that."

Tombazis concluded by stressing that, despite all of this, the races themselves have still provided good entertainment during the first half of the season.

Tombazis feels despite the problems with the F1 regulations, the racing has been exciting Photo by: Kym Illman / Getty Images

"Now with that said, I think most races have been pretty exciting, I would say. There's been quite a lot of fighting," he said.

"I would even say that currently we still have, I don't know if I would go quite as far as to call it domination, but we do have a clear advantage for one manufacturer. And in the past when we've had that at the early start of the regulations, races have been very processional.

"Now I think, even despite the fact that Mercedes have been doing most of the winning, I think the races have nonetheless been quite exciting with quite a lot of changes and so on."

Sports.title: Norris vs Piastri: 2026 F1 team mates’ head-to-head scores at summer break | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The super-close contest between the McLaren team mates last year would have made for a thrilling world championship fight even if Max Verstappen hadn’t got involved.

Now in their fourth season as team mates, with a completely different type of McLaren to get used to, Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri have been fairly well-matched on the whole. However in individual races their relative performance has varied, most notably in Hungary last weekend, where Norris was clearly much quicker.

Norris has been on a strong run lately, out-qualifying his team mate for the last five rounds in a row. Though it bears pointing out that Piastri missed first practice at the last round and was badly baulked by Lewis Hamilton when he began his final run.

It took Piastri until the third round of the season merely to start a grand prix, suffering a mortifying pre-race crash at home, then retiring before the start along with Norris in Shanghai. He rebounded magnificently at Suzuka and might have won had it not been for the timing of a Safety Car period.

McLaren have had further technical trouble since then: Norris had back-to-back failures while Piastri’s retirement in Hungary capped a frustrating race where a wayward backmarker had already cost him the lead. Piastri had a rough race in Canada as well, where both McLaren drivers paid the price for a tactical gamble which backfired.

It was therefore fitting that Norris delivered the team’s first win as F1 headed into the summer break. His 36-point lead over Piastri looks like a fair reflection of their relative performances given the various setbacks both drivers have suffered. The world champion holds the upper hand so far but Piastri is keeping him honest as always.

Sports.title: Hamilton vs Leclerc: 2026 F1 team mates’ head-to-head scores at summer break | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Does Lewis Hamilton have an eighth world championship in him? Has he not recovered from the blow of 2021 or did he simply never gel with the ‘ground effect’ cars of 2022-25?

Those hoping to see the seven-times world champion fight for another title will have drawn great encouragement from what they have seen so far in 2026. Last year, in his first season at Ferrari, he came off badly in comparison to Charles Leclerc , taking a 19-5 pasting in qualifying and making zero podium appearances to his team mate’s seven.

Hamilton has given full credit to team principal Frederic Vasseur for implementing the changes he needed to make a success of his transition to Ferrari, whether that has involved different brake material or swerving the simulator. On the face of it, it has paid off, and Ferrari now have two A-list drivers performing at their peak.

Leclerc is still shading Hamilton on average in qualifying, but the fight between the two has been much closer. Hamilton has delivered more consistently on race day, including that breakthrough victory in Spain.

Both drivers have misfired at times. Leclerc had a spate of errors including costly crashes in qualifying at the Circuit de Catalunya and during his home race.

Hamilton, meanwhile, has picked up a bad habit of incurring the stewards’ wrath, collecting a series of needless penalties in recent races. Though some may not have been his fault or were debatable calls, many others were straightforward, and he was fortunate to avoid a worse penalty for his yellow flag slip in Silverstone.

For all that, Hamilton is Andrea Kimi Antonelli’s closest rival in the championship at the summer break. “Has the time finally come for Hamilton to hang up his helmet?” we asked in May, in what already looks like one of the most poorly-timed polls ever featured on RaceFans.

Sports.title: Antonelli vs Russell: 2026 F1 team mates’ head-to-head scores at summer break | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Early in the season it seemed certain that whichever of the Mercedes drivers came out ahead would be crowned world champion. That remains likely, but the threat posed by rival teams has grown in recent races.

Little about Andrea Kimi Antonelli’s form in his rookie season indicated that 12 months later he would be beating his team mate quite as emphatically as he is. But heading into the summer break, Antonelli holds a valuable 59-point lead over the other Mercedes driver.

It’s a far cry from the situation around 12 months ago. At the end of the ‘European season’, Antonelli was 15-1 down against George Russell in qualifying. He ended the season still with less than half his team mate’s points tally.

But after a difficult mid-season, following a Mercedes upgrade which did not go as intended, Antonelli rebounded impressively with the end of the year in sight. He reached the podium twice over the final four rounds.

So while Russell’s season-opening victory in Australia looked like the shape of things to come, Antonelli shattered those illusions by winning the next five rounds in a row. He got the rub of the green at times – technical trouble hit Russell in qualifying at Shanghai and took him out while he led in Montreal – but he has also seemed fundamentally more at ease with Mercedes’ W17 than his team mate.

The unusually high rate of problems on Mercedes’ cars, and Russell’s particular problems with poor straight-line speed at Silverstone and Spa, have further complicated the picture. Antonelli’s car has not been immune, breaking down in Spain and breaking an aerodynamic component at Silverstone. Overall, Russell has probably had slightly worse luck, but not 59 points’ worth. Antonelli is leading this championship on merit, and Russell will have to dig deep in the second half of the season if he is going to avoid a painful defeat.

Sports.title: Featured Comment: How far is modern F1 like the ‘turbo era’? | Formula 1
Asian Le Mans Series to take place entirely in Europe following war in Middle East | Brief
Sports.content:
The Asian Le Mans Series has announced its 2026-27 season will take place entirely at European circuits.

Since 2021 the series has only raced at the Dubai Autodrome, Yas Marina in the United Arab Emirates and Malaysia’s Sepang International Circuit. Its upcoming championship will take place at Jerez in Spain, Paul Ricard in France and Autodromo do Algarve in Portugal. The championship will be renamed the ‘Winter Le Mans Series’ as a result.

The change is the latest in a series of alterations to the motorsport calendar which have arisen following the war in the Middle East.

“While moving the Asian Le Mans Series to Europe is not ideal, the situation in the Middle East dictated that we worked to find the best solution,” said series promoter Stephane Ratel. “Between SRO, LMEM and the ACO we have a huge pool of experience to draw on, and the consensus was a Winter Le Mans Series in southern Europe was the most sensible option given the mounting external constraints.”

Formula 1 cancelled its races in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia earlier this year. F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali has indicated the series will race in Europe if its final two rounds in the Middle East cannot go ahead.

Sports.title: Filip Hrgovic Not Impressed By Moses Itauma Hype
Sports.content:
“I think I’m the best opponent he’s faced. I think he’s never been until now in the ring with someone like me, with that kind of experience and endurance, toughness, power. So let’s see how good he is,” Hrgovic told DAZN Boxing. “Everyone says he’s a future superstar, future Lennox Lewis.”

“You believe it as well, though,” Itauma said.

“Let’s see,” Hrgovic said. “We’ll see. I don’t know. For right now, I’m not impressed. I must see something more than this to believe he’s the real deal. So, let’s see.”

Hrgovic believes he can force Itauma into situations previous opponents have been unable to create. The young heavyweight has spent his rapid climb through the division overwhelming opposition before being pushed into prolonged, difficult fights.

Hrgovic has already experienced those kinds of battles, including his grueling fight with Zhilei Zhang and stoppage loss to Daniel Dubois. His durability gives Itauma something different to solve if the fight extends beyond the early rounds.

Itauma has looked considerably faster than Hrgovic and carries dangerous power, but the Croatian represents a significant jump from the opposition the prospect has faced so far.

The Lennox Lewis comparisons are especially premature. Itauma does not need to resemble a future Hall of Famer on August 29. He does need to show that his talent remains effective against a durable heavyweight capable of absorbing punishment and firing back.

Sports.title: Daniel Dubois-Fabio Wardley Rematch Could Land October 17
Sports.content:
Dubois stopped Wardley in the 11th round of their May 9 fight in Manchester following an exhausting battle in which both heavyweights had difficult moments. Wardley dropped Dubois twice early, putting himself in position to take control before Dubois worked his way back into the fight.

Dubois gradually took over as the rounds passed, landing the cleaner, heavier punches while Wardley absorbed increasing damage. The punishment accumulated before Dubois forced the stoppage in the 11th.

Wardley exercised his contractual right to an immediate rematch rather than taking an interim fight. An October 17 return would leave him with little time to recover physically before beginning another training camp for the same opponent.

That decision recently drew criticism from former two-division champion Paulie Malignaggi, who questioned the wisdom of going directly back into another fight with Dubois. Malignaggi believes Wardley has the punching power to change a fight instantly but sees a considerable skill advantage for Dubois.

The possible October date makes Malignaggi’s concern more relevant. Wardley would have to recover physically, make tactical adjustments and prepare for another demanding heavyweight fight just over five months after the first one.

A quick return also gives Dubois an opportunity to repeat his first result before Wardley has much time to make major changes. Wardley has already shown that he can hurt Dubois. Five months may not be enough to correct the technical weaknesses Dubois exploited as their first fight progressed.

Sports.title: Héctor Camacho Overwhelms Rafael Limón for First World Title
Sports.content:
The belt became available after the WBC stripped Bobby Chacon when a defense against No. 1 contender Camacho failed to materialize. Limón, 29, had recently held the championship before losing a brutal 15-round decision to Chacon in their celebrated fourth fight eight months earlier.

This was Camacho’s first opportunity to win a world title. Limón also represented something new for the young Puerto Rican: an opponent who had previously worn a world championship belt.

The difference in speed became apparent almost immediately. Limón tried to reach Camacho with wide punches, while the younger fighter attacked from different angles, with his straight left finding the target repeatedly. A clean left floored Limón late in the third round. More punishment followed during the fourth as Camacho had him in serious trouble.

Limón’s situation deteriorated further in the fifth. Body shots put him on the canvas in the center of the ring. He regained his feet, but Camacho quickly resumed his assault. A subsequent barrage knocked Limón through the ropes near his corner.

Limón climbed back into position once more. Referee Richard Steele decided he had absorbed enough punishment and stopped the contest at 2:52 of the fifth round. Camacho was the new WBC junior lightweight champion.

All three judges had Camacho comfortably in front through four completed rounds. Dimas Hernandez scored it 40-34, while Moises Sister and Hector Chaumont each had it 40-35.

The celebration afterward illustrated Camacho’s popularity as much as the fight itself. Spectators and members of his entourage poured around the ring as Puerto Rico celebrated its newest world champion.

The performance showed a version of Camacho that later generations of boxing fans rarely saw. Before age and years in the ring changed his style, Camacho possessed extraordinary speed, reflexes and offensive ability. Limón was a hardened former two-time champion who had survived wars with Bobby Chacon, yet the 21-year-old Camacho overwhelmed him with a combination of speed and aggression that Limón simply could not handle.

Camacho made one defense of the title, knocking out Rafael Solis in five rounds, before moving up in weight. Two years after defeating Limón, he captured the WBC lightweight championship. His flamboyant personality, exceptional speed and success across multiple divisions eventually established “Macho” among boxing’s most recognizable stars.

Sports.title: Dwight Braxton Dominates Saad Muhammad In Philadelphia Rematch
Sports.content:
This time, Braxton was even more dominant. Braxton, 29, gave away considerable height and reach to the 28-year-old Saad Muhammad, but the physical disadvantages meant little once the action began. The 5’6″ titleholder worked his way inside behind his jab, forcing the taller challenger onto his back foot.

Saad Muhammad had replaced longtime trainer Sam Solomon with Steve Traitz following the first loss, but the change did little to alter the outcome.

Braxton bloodied Saad Muhammad’s nose in the second round and dropped him in the third. There would be none of the remarkable recoveries that had defined Saad Muhammad’s prime years. Braxton kept attacking with compact hooks, right hands, and heavy body shots.

By the end of five rounds, judges Tony Castellano, Tony Perez, and Dick Young had Braxton comfortably in front by scores of 50-43, 50-42, and 50-41.

The finish came quickly in the sixth. Braxton drove Saad Muhammad toward the ropes with a left-right combination and continued firing as the challenger struggled to defend himself. Referee Carlos Padilla intervened at 1:23, giving Braxton his second consecutive stoppage over his rival.

The performance established Braxton, who would become known as Dwight Muhammad Qawi, as the premier 175-pound fighter alongside Michael Spinks. He later defeated Eddie Davis before losing a light heavyweight unification contest to Spinks in 1983.

The night ended Saad Muhammad’s time at the top of the division. His championship years had featured extraordinary rallies and grueling wars, but those battles took their toll. He continued fighting long after the Braxton losses and was eventually inducted into the International Boxing Hall of Fame.

There was no miraculous Matthew Saad Muhammad comeback this night. Braxton’s inside control, compact punching, and relentless pressure produced an emphatic conclusion to a rivalry he had already taken command of seven months earlier.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Is Running Out Of Fighters To Reject
Sports.content:
The back-and-forth with WBO welterweight champion Devin Haney illustrates the problem. Shakur wants a 144-pound catchweight, a condition Bill Haney rejected by insisting Devin should not drop below the 147-pound welterweight limit.

Shakur can take the fight at 147, pursue a mandatory position or move on to another opponent. Instead, another potentially lucrative fight has stalled because he wants terms the champion has little reason to accept.

That is almost the opposite of the old-school mentality. Fighters who scored career-defining wins often returned to work quickly, signing another fight and capitalizing on their success while the public was still talking about them.

Seven months is enough time to negotiate a deal, complete a training camp and fight again. Shakur has instead acted like an employee who had the best day of his career at the office and responded by taking an extended vacation.

Shakur spent years trying to reach this position. The question now is how many months of his prime he’s willing to sacrifice by ruling out opponents and demanding terms that keep fights from getting made.

Sports.title: Murat Gassiev Vs Jarrell Miller Talks Underway For WBA Belt
Sports.content:
“There’s a little bit of confusion with the WBA. I mean, Gassiev’s the champion. He’s got to fight Jarrell Miller, our guy, which we’re negotiating at the moment,” Hearn told iFL TV.

The fight offers Miller a shot at a heavyweight belt late in his career. A scheduled 2019 title bout against Anthony Joshua was canceled after Miller failed multiple drug tests before the event.

Miller rebuilt his career and remains a difficult opponent due to his size, constant pressure, and high work rate. A fight against Gassiev puts him near the top of the division without requiring a long series of elimination bouts.

Gassiev’s heavyweight run has moved slowly since leaving the cruiserweight division. The former unified cruiserweight champion possesses considerable punching power, though health issues and long layoffs have prevented him from establishing the same position at heavyweight that he held at 200 pounds.

Hearn is already considering potential opponents if Miller wins.

“Hopefully Jarrell Miller can beat Gassiev. We can do Miller against Kabayel. There’s loads of fights to be made,” Hearn said.

Miller first needs the Gassiev fight finalized. At 38, an opportunity to challenge a WBA champion gives the recently signed Matchroom heavyweight another chance to capture a world title.

Sports.title: Frank Warren Sees No Reason To Delay Fury-Joshua
Sports.content:
“There is still plenty of time,” the Queensberry promoter told a media roundtable. “The fighters will just need to get into training some time in September, so that is what will happen in early September.”

Fury is spending time with his family on the Isle of Man after completing two training camps following his lengthy absence from the ring. He plans to begin serious preparations once the fight date is set.

“I believe the fight will go on in November,” Warren said.

Questions about Joshua’s readiness increased after Prenga dropped him with one of the first clean punches he landed. Pushing the bout into 2027 offers little benefit, particularly with Joshua having already fought twice this year.

“He has got plenty of time to get ready,” Warren said. “So what does he do if he doesn’t fight? He will carry on training, training and training, and he will be getting older as will Tyson, so what is the point? Get on with it.”

Warren believes Joshua’s vulnerability gives Fury a major advantage, pointing directly to the Prenga knockdown when explaining the danger facing the former champion against a more accomplished heavyweight.

“Looking at the Prenga fight, if that had been Tyson in there, that would have been all over.”

The location remains unresolved. Madison Square Garden has been linked to the event, although Joshua and Eddie Hearn have pushed to keep the fight in Britain. Turki Alalshikh will announce the official date and location.

Sports.title: Cassius Clay Dominates Brian London In Three-Round Title Defense
Sports.content:
London gave away advantages in height, reach, and speed, leaving him with few answers after the opening bell. Using a sharp jab, quick footwork, and rapid-fire combinations, the champion controlled the action and repeatedly beat London to the punch. The challenger generated almost no offense. Many accounts credited him with only a single solid left jab in the opening round that briefly caught Clay’s attention.

The finish came at 1:40 of the third round. Clay trapped London in a neutral corner, unleashing a blistering combination described by observers as roughly a dozen punches within a few seconds. A left-right combination sent London to the canvas, where referee Harry Gibbs completed the count.

Clay weighed 209½ pounds, while London came in at 201½ pounds. The champion received a guaranteed purse of approximately $252,000 plus a share of the television revenue. London earned about $112,000 for the brief outing.

Earls Court fell well short of full capacity. Many fight fans dismissed the matchup as a mismatch, and Clay quickly justified those expectations by displaying the hand speed, reflexes, and accuracy that defined his prime.

Clay’s knockout of London set up a meeting with Karl Mildenberger later that year. The event became the final bout under Clay’s agreement with the Louisville Sponsoring Group before Herbert Muhammad assumed management duties.

London remained remarkably candid about the experience throughout his life. He openly admitted Clay held every advantage, describing himself as smaller, slower, and lacking the champion’s athleticism. He frequently joked about accepting a rematch only if Clay entered the ring wearing heavy weights around his ankles. While certain British critics questioned London’s effort, his honesty about facing one of boxing’s greatest champions became an enduring part of the event’s history.

Ghana News.title: GSA begins nationwide sensitisation for shippers
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Shippers' Authority (GSA) has begun a nationwide sensitisation of shippers on the mandatory registration of shippers on the Integrated Customs Management System (ICUMS) in accordance with the Ghana Shippers' Authority Act, 2024 (Act 1122).

Officials of the GSA, the Customs Division of the Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA), and ICUMS have toured the country to explain how the electronic system will ease cargo clearance and support the collection of data for policy formulation and adjustments.

On Wednesday, 5th August 2026, a sensitisation program was organised for executives of Freight Forwarding Associations at the Ghana Shippers’ House.

The engagement was aimed at promoting compliance with Section 26(1) of Act 1122, which requires all importers and exporters to register with the Authority before processing shipment transactions through the ICUMS platform.

Opening the programme, the Deputy Chief Executive Officer in charge of Technical Services, Mrs. Sylvia Asana Dauda Owu, underscored the importance of the mandatory registration and urged freight forwarders to support the process by ensuring that their clients registered to avoid disruptions to cargo clearance.

Officials of the GSA and Ghana Link Network Services Ltd. subsequently demonstrated the ICUMS registration process and responded to stakeholders' questions to facilitate a smooth implementation.

During the discussions, freight forwarders appealed for the implementation deadline to be extended to Monday to 31st August 2026, to allow additional time for stakeholder sensitisation and compliance. Mrs. Dauda Owu acknowledged the request and assured participants that Management would consider the appeal and communicate its decision.

The meeting also addressed the implementation of the Container Administrative Charge (CAC). The President of the Ghana Institute of Freight Forwarders (GIFF), Mr. Stephen Adjokatcher, and the Chairman of the GIFF Tema Chapter, Mr. Johnny Mantey, encouraged freight forwarders to ensure that importers complied with the approved GH¢720 Container Administrative Charge, emphasising the need for industry-wide support.

Also addressing the meeting, the Deputy Commissioner of the Customs Division of the Ghana Revenue Authority, Mr. Divine Agbeko, called for continued collaboration among stakeholders to facilitate seamless cargo clearance and improve trade efficiency.

The engagement forms part of the Authority's ongoing efforts to strengthen regulatory compliance, enhance stakeholder collaboration, and promote efficient trade through the effective implementation of Act 1122 (2024).

Ghana News.title: PETROSOL secures approval to raise capital on Ghana Stock Exchange
Ghana News.content:
PETROSOL Platinum Energy PLC, one of the leading oil marketing companies has received approval from the Ghana Stock Exchange and the Securities and Exchange Commission to raise long-term capital through the Ghana Stock Exchange, Managing Director Michael Bozumbil said.

The approval marks a milestone for the company, which has evolved over two decades from a petroleum consulting firm into an indigenous oil marketing company in Ghana.

“After a thorough assessment of PETROSOL’s business, including our governance systems, our compliance level, our credibility and growth plans, the Ghana Stock Exchange and the Securities and Exchange Commission have approved our request to raise patient capital on the stock exchange for our growth,” Bozumbil said at the Ghana International Petroleum Conference in Accra.

He said the proceeds would fund the company’s long-term expansion strategy, including investments in renewable energy, solar power and electric vehicle charging infrastructure.

“We have a clear plan to grow sustainably. We will continue to look for opportunities and the right partnerships to invest in the energy sector through innovation while taking advantage of government policies to expand our operations and deliver clean, long-lasting fuel and renewable energy solutions to our customers,” he said.

Founded in 2006 as a petroleum business management and consulting firm, PETROSOL entered the oil marketing business in 2014, benefiting from government policies aimed at increasing indigenous participation in Ghana’s downstream petroleum sector.

The company now operates more than 100 fuel stations across Ghana and employs about 490 people.

Bozumbil attributed PETROSOL’s growth to corporate governance, prudent financial management and regulatory compliance despite challenging economic conditions.

He said the company has obtained three International Organization for Standardization (ISO) certifications covering quality management, occupational health and safety, and environmental management.

It has also received recognition from the Ghana Revenue Authority for tax compliance and remains in good standing with the National Petroleum Authority, the Environmental Protection Agency and the Ghana Standards Authority.

Beyond its petroleum business, PETROSOL is investing in renewable energy and plans to install electric vehicle charging stations at selected service stations as part of Ghana’s energy transition.

Bozumbil said policy consistency remains critical to enabling indigenous companies to compete with multinational firms in Ghana’s downstream petroleum sector.

“As an indigenous company that has benefited from the consistent implementation of government policies promoting the growth of indigenous private companies, we believe collaboration and policy consistency are critical to building a resilient downstream petroleum industry,” he said.

He said PETROSOL’s sponsorship of the 2026 Ghana International Petroleum Conference reflected its commitment to supporting industry dialogue and encouraging innovation, investment and sustainable growth.

Looking ahead, Bozumbil said the company would continue expanding its retail fuel network, growing its renewable energy business and creating jobs.

“We will continue to invest for growth. PETROSOL will remain a value-for-money brand, a good corporate citizen and an employer of choice. We will continue to energise dreams, ignite hope and power individuals and businesses to achieve their aspirations in an environmentally sustainable and ethical manner,” he said.

The planned capital raise is expected to strengthen PETROSOL’s financial position and broaden investment opportunities in Ghana’s capital market, the company said.

Ghana News.title: AI must empower entrepreneurs, not replace human creativity – UPS Global Director
Ghana News.content:
Artificial intelligence (AI) should be viewed as a tool for strengthening entrepreneurship rather than replacing human creativity and critical thinking, Global Director of Social Impact at UPS, La’Kerri Jackson, has said.

Speaking at the opening of a two-day entrepreneurship workshop in Accra on Thursday, Ms Jackson encouraged business owners to embrace AI as a practical tool for improving productivity while continuing to rely on their knowledge, experience and innovation.

The workshop, organised by the International Trade Centre’s (ITC) SheTrades Initiative in partnership with UPS, Visa and the Ghana Export Promotion Authority (GEPA), has brought together 200 established and aspiring Ghanaian entrepreneurs.

It is designed to build participants’ skills in artificial intelligence, digital payments, logistics, marketing and access to finance.

According to Ms Jackson, entrepreneurs worldwide face similar challenges, particularly limited access to capital and export opportunities. She said this made collaboration between development partners and the private sector essential.

“There are many challenges that entrepreneurs and small businesses face, from exporting challenges to the lack of access to capital. It’s not just specific to Ghana; it’s all over the globe,” she said.

She noted that UPS works with organisations worldwide to help entrepreneurs overcome these barriers through training, mentorship and access to business support networks.

Among the partnerships she highlighted were collaborations with Opportunity International to provide interest-free, collateral-free microloans; the Fearless Fund to support business growth; and the International Trade Centre to equip entrepreneurs with practical skills and resources.

A key focus of the Accra workshop is helping small business owners understand how AI can be applied to their daily operations without requiring advanced technical expertise.

Ms Jackson said many entrepreneurs already had access to free digital tools that could help improve their businesses.

“It’s not as hard as we think it is. There are practical tools available through platforms like WhatsApp and Instagram for marketing, creating flyers and promoting businesses without investing a lot of money,” she said.

She, however, cautioned entrepreneurs against becoming overly dependent on AI, stressing that technology should complement, rather than replace, human judgement.

“The angle that people should take is that AI is a thought-leadership partner. You are the brands. You have the intellect. You have the intellectual property,” she said.

“There is a danger in becoming so dependent on it, but everybody has to exercise discipline and continue to lean on their own intellect.”

Also addressing participants, UPS Foundation Manager Bassen Anari challenged entrepreneurs to translate the lessons from the workshop into practical business actions.

He observed that although many entrepreneurs enthusiastically participated in training programmes, only a few went on to implement what they had learnt.

Ghana News.title: Keta Municipal Hospital receives over GH¢2m medical supplies to boost healthcare delivery
Ghana News.content:
Healthcare delivery in the Keta Municipality of the Volta Region has received a significant boost after medical supplies worth more than GH¢2 million were donated to the Keta Municipal Hospital.

The donation, spearheaded by Lom Nuku Ahlijah in partnership with the Living Presence Evangelistic Network, includes essential medical supplies that are expected to strengthen patient care, improve emergency services, and support the work of healthcare professionals.

Hospital management praised the donors for their generosity, noting that the intervention comes at a critical time when health facilities continue to require additional support to meet increasing patient demands.

Mr. Ahlijah indicated that improving healthcare remains central to community development and called on more corporate bodies, philanthropists, and organisations to complement government efforts in strengthening health institutions.

The donation underscores the growing role of public-private partnerships and community leadership in advancing quality healthcare and improving the wellbeing of citizens in the Keta Municipality.

Ghana News.title: Ghana: Genser energy buys back Oppenheimer partners’ stake as investor exits after five years
Ghana News.content:
Genser Energy has bought back the entire stake held by Oppenheimer Partners, completing the investment firm’s exit after five years and marking a new phase in the Ghanaian energy company’s regional expansion.

The privately owned energy infrastructure company said it had redeemed the full shareholding previously held by OP Energy Holdings Limited, ending Oppenheimer Partners’ investment in the business.

Oppenheimer Partners first invested in Genser Energy as a preferred shareholder in 2021 before converting its holding into common equity in 2023, when it acquired a 40.4% stake.

The latest transaction concludes that investment and returns the shares to Genser Energy.

Founded in 2006, Genser Energy has grown into one of West Africa’s integrated energy companies, supplying electricity to industrial customers and utilities while investing in natural gas infrastructure.

Before Oppenheimer Partners’ investment, the company had developed five operating power plants and a 325-km natural gas pipeline network, becoming a key supplier of energy to Ghana’s industrial sector.

During the investment period, Genser expanded its infrastructure by adding about 110 km of natural gas pipeline, constructing a 200 million standard cubic feet per day gas conditioning plant in Prestea and entering Côte d’Ivoire through cross-border electricity exports.

“This transaction marks an important milestone for Genser Energy and reflects the strength of the business we have built over the past two decades,” Baafour Asiamah Adjei, the company’s founder, president and chief executive, said.

Chairman Nana Osae Nyampong said the buyback would enable the company to focus on its next phase of growth.

“As we look ahead, we remain focused on expanding our regional presence and creating long-term value for our customers, communities, employees and shareholders,” Nyampong said.

The transaction comes as infrastructure investors increasingly target Africa’s energy sector, where rising industrial demand and regional power integration are driving investment in gas pipelines, power generation and cross-border electricity trade.

Genser said it remains positioned for further expansion through continued investment in strategic energy infrastructure across West Africa.

The company operates more than 310 megawatts of installed generation capacity and owns a 436-km privately developed natural gas pipeline network in Ghana.

It is also completing major midstream projects, including a gas conditioning plant and a natural gas liquids export terminal, while supplying power to industrial customers and utilities and participating in regional electricity exports.

Ghana News.title: Agalga is tough but lacks leadership experience for Majority Leader role — Nitiwul
Ghana News.content:
Former Defence Minister has said the Builsa North MP James Agalga who is the leading contender to become the next Majority Leader of Parliament, lacks the leadership experience required for his new role and must quickly adapt if he is to succeed in managing government business in Parliament.

Speaking on The Pulse on JoyNews on Friday, August 7, while discussing President John Dramani Mahama's recent reshuffle, Dominic Nitiwul said although Mr Agalga is a capable and resilient politician, leading the Majority Caucus demands experience that can only be acquired over time.

"Agalga is a very tough, tough, tough guy. You know, he's a very tough guy."

Mr Nitiwul, however, said toughness alone would not be enough to navigate the demands of parliamentary leadership.

"The only thing he needs to realise is that he does not have the experience of leadership."

He explained that several senior Members of Parliament, including Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin, former Majority Chief Whip Frank Annoh-Dompreh, Patricia Appiagyei and Habib Iddrisu, had spent years in leadership positions and therefore possessed valuable experience.

"Afenyo-Markin, Annoh-Dompreh, Patricia Appiagyei, and Habib have the experience of leadership. They have been there. All the four of them have been there long before him. Some of them have done seven years, six years. Some of them have done six and a half years."

According to Mr Nitiwul, leadership is not only a calling but also a skill that is developed through experience.

"It is a calling. But apart from that, it is a skill that you need to learn on your feet."

He said that Mr Agalga entered Parliament around the same period as Mr Afenyo-Markin and therefore understands parliamentary procedure, adding that he was not surprised President Mahama selected him for the position.

"When it comes to parliamentary work, Agalga came in, I think, 2012. So he came with Afenyo. They are mates. So he has an idea about how to go about leadership. So I'm not surprised that the president picked him to go."

Mr Nitiwul said he believed Mr Agalga would have been considered for the Defence Ministry if he had not been appointed Majority Leader.

"If he didn't go there, then he would have gone to Defence."

Despite expressing confidence in Mr Agalga's ability, Mr Nitiwul cautioned that the new Majority Leader would have to settle into the role quickly or risk losing control of proceedings in the House.

"He has to learn very fast. Otherwise, trust me, the mighty 87 will overrun him."

He warned that the Minority Caucus would take advantage of any weaknesses if Mr Agalga failed to establish himself.

"If he's not on his feet, the 87 will overrun him and overrun him very, very quickly."

Mr Nitiwul also commented on the departure of Mahama Ayariga as Majority Leader, saying the decision had long been expected within Parliament.

"It was obvious to everybody that Mahama Ayariga would leave the front bench. It was very obvious before we left."

He said there had been widespread speculation that Mr Ayariga would be reassigned if changes were made to Cabinet.

Read also: Mahama names Zanetor Rawlings for Environment, nominates Ayariga to Local Government in first reshuffle

The former Defence Minister insisted that Mr Ayariga's exit was not solely linked to his performance, revealing that there were other factors he could not publicly discuss.

"There are some other reasons, which I cannot say on air, that he needed to leave. And it was in his interest to leave the front leadership."

He acknowledged that some members of the governing National Democratic Congress were dissatisfied with Mr Ayariga's handling of parliamentary business, particularly his exchanges with Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin.

"It's not about performance or non-performance, even though the NDC party have their own issues with him. The way he went about things and the way he and Afenyo, in the exchanges and how he came out with, some of them felt unsatisfied with the way he went about things."

Mr Nitiwul, however, said the ultimate verdict on Mr Ayariga's leadership would rest with the Ghanaian electorate.

"That is for the jury to judge, and that jury will be the electorates in 2028." Builsa North Member of Parliament James Agalga is the leading contender to become the next Majority Leader of Parliament following Mahama Ayariga’s appointment to President John Dramani Mahama’s cabinet, sources within the National Democratic Congress (NDC) Caucus have told MyJoyOnline.

Ghana News.title: Two thieves jailed 22 years after convictions in separate cases in Upper West
Ghana News.content:
The Upper West Regional Police Command has secured a combined 22-year prison sentence for two convicted thieves in separate stealing-related cases.

In a statement issued on August 6, 2026, the police said 20-year-old Nasiru Muftawu was sentenced to 12 years' imprisonment with hard labour after being convicted for a series of motorbike thefts across the region.

He was arrested on July 11, 2026, following intelligence-led investigations and convicted by the Wa Circuit Court on August 5.

In a separate case, Eric Salia, 36, was sentenced to 10 years' imprisonment with hard labour after he was found guilty of breaking into the residence of a public officer and stealing valuable personal belongings. He was arrested on July 26, 2026, and convicted by the same court.

The Upper West Regional Police Command said the convictions demonstrate its commitment to tackling crime and ensuring the safety of residents.

"The Command reiterates its unwavering commitment to creating a safe, secure, and conducive environment for all law-abiding residents of the Upper West Region. It assures the public that it will continue to pursue criminals relentlessly and bring offenders to justice," the statement said.

The police also urged the public to support law enforcement by providing timely and credible information to help prevent crime and enhance community safety.

Ghana News.title: From Deputy to Defense Boss: Gilbert Adjei returns to lead ministry where he once served number two
Ghana News.content:
Nearly a decade after he walked out of Ghana's Ministry of Defense as its second in command, Kenneth Gilbert Adjei is walking back in, this time to sit at the head of the table.

President John Dramani Mahama has named Adjei as substantive Minister for Defense, filling the seat left empty by the death of Dr Edward Omane Boamah and handing full charge of the ministry to a man who first entered it as a deputy under the same President. The reassignment was announced Friday by Presidency Communications.

Because Adjei was already vetted and approved by Parliament as Works and Housing Minister, his move to Defense does not require a fresh vetting. Under Ghana's practice, a sitting minister reshuffled into another portfolio is not sent back before the Appointments Committee, so Adjei can be sworn into his new role without further parliamentary scrutiny.

His history with the ministry runs back to Mahama's first term. He was appointed Deputy Minister of Defense in 2015 and served until January 2017, when the National Democratic Congress handed power to the Akufo-Addo administration. Now he returns to the same building with a bigger mandate and a heavy in-tray.

He takes over a portfolio that has become one of the government's most ambitious spending priorities. In the 2026 Budget, the Ministry of Defense was handed a 69 percent funding increase for a comprehensive retooling of the Ghana Armed Forces to strengthen defence readiness. Presenting the budget, Finance Minister Cassiel Ato Forson paid tribute to the late Boamah as a fallen hero and the architect of the modernisation strategy Adjei now inherits.

The promises are substantial. The government said it would begin procurement in 2026 for four modern helicopters, one long range aircraft and one medium range aircraft to replace an ageing Air Force fleet that has struggled with readiness, with delivery expected within four years if procurement is completed on schedule.

For the Navy, the government pointed to a 272 metre offshore patrol vessel fitted with helipads and modern combat systems to guard Ghana's maritime borders and offshore energy assets. For the Army, Forson revealed that 40 million dollars had already been paid to Elbit Systems for 19 armoured personnel carriers that were never delivered, and said the contract would be renegotiated and brought back to Parliament to protect state funds.

Adjei appears in no doubt about the assignment. Within hours of the announcement, he had already updated his social media profile, dropping his old title as Minister for Works and Housing and replacing it with Minister for Defense.

Delivering on the budget pledges now falls to him. The modernisation drive followed the findings of a government committee that investigated the August 6 crash and recommended that the Air Force fleet be modernised, giving the programme an added weight the new minister will be expected to carry.

The appointment closes a vacancy that had lasted a year. The ministry lost its substantive head on August 6, 2025, when a military helicopter crash killed Boamah, Environment Minister Ibrahim Murtala Muhammed and six others shortly after take off from Accra. In the aftermath, Mahama asked Forson to oversee Defense in an acting capacity, a stopgap that stretched on for months and drew criticism from lawmakers and security analysts who argued the vacancy was untenable as jihadist violence spread across West Africa.

Adjei was not the only name in circulation. Ahead of the announcement, some speculation had pointed to Dr Zanetor Agyemang-Rawlings as a possible pick for the security portfolio, but in Friday's nominations she was instead sent to the Ministry of Environment, Science and Technology, leaving the Defense job to Adjei.

He moves to Defense from the Works, Housing and Water Resources portfolio. A member of the NDC and a native of Trede in the Ashanti Region, he holds an MBA from the University of Ghana Business School and, more recently, a master's degree in peace, security and intelligence management earned in 2022.

With the portfolio settled, attention now turns to whether Adjei can convert the budget's bold defence promises into delivered aircraft, ships and vehicles on the ground.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.
