World.title: Otedola acquires additional 138 million First HoldCo shares worth ₦18.1 billion
World.content:
Femi Otedola, chairman of First HoldCo Plc, has acquired an additional 138 million shares in the financial services group, valued at about ₦18.1 billion.

The transaction was announced on Friday in a regulatory filing signed by the group’s Company Secretary, Abiola Baruwa.

Mr Otedola acquired an additional 138,041,465 shares at ₦131.2 per share through Calvados Global Services Limited.

The new share purchase represents 0.30 per cent of the company’s outstanding shares, bringing Mr Otedola’s total stake in the financial services group to 27.16 per cent of the company’s issued share capital.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Otedola now holds approximately 11.9 billion shares in the financial institution, valued at about ₦1.74 trillion based on the company’s share price of ₦146.20 as of 12:35 p.m. (WAT) on 7 August.

The First HoldCo chairman has steadily increased his investment in the company since emerging as its largest shareholder in 2021.

On 30 July, Mr Otedola increased his stake in the financial services group by acquiring an additional 1.78 billion shares, valued at about ₦222.2 billion.

About a week earlier, on 22 July, he acquired 706.1 million shares valued at ₦77.6 billion. This was separate from the 672.9 million shares worth ₦29.6 billion that he purchased in June.

The June acquisition was completed during the ₦45 billion second tranche of First HoldCo’s ₦350 billion private placement programme, in which shares were offered at ₦44 per share.

The group said it plans to inject the proceeds from the capital raise into First Bank of Nigeria Limited, its flagship commercial banking subsidiary, as part of its capital restoration and broader balance sheet strengthening programme.

World.title: JRS launches project to strengthen oil spill resilience in Akwa Ibom community
World.content:
The Jesuit Refugee Service (JRS) Nigeria has launched a new project aimed at strengthening the resilience of an oil-producing community in Akwa Ibom State against the devastating impacts of oil spills.

The project, funded by CARITAS Canada and titled “Strengthening Community Resilience to Oil Spill Impacts in Akwa Ibom State,” was inaugurated during an inception meeting held on Thursday in Eket, bringing together government officials, community leaders, traditional rulers, civil society groups and development partners.

The initiative will focus on the Okoro Utip community in Ibeno Local Government Area, where residents have complained for years about the environmental and socio-economic consequences of oil pollution.

PREMIUM TIMES reported how oil spills contaminate rivers and destroy livelihoods in Ibeno. The newspaper also reported how communities affected by oil spills have threatened legal action against oil firms over pollution.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

According to JRS Nigeria, the project is designed to strengthen the resilience of climate-vulnerable residents by promoting meaningful community participation in addressing the environmental, social and economic effects of oil contamination.

The organisation said decades of oil spills across the Niger Delta have degraded ecosystems, affected public health, weakened food security, reduced biodiversity and undermined the livelihoods of many residents.

Community-centred approach

JRS Nigeria said the project would adopt the African Palaver approach which is a traditional model of communal dialogue to create inclusive spaces where residents can share their experiences, deepen understanding of environmental challenges and collectively identify locally driven solutions.

It explained that the initiative is not intended to replace the responsibilities of government agencies but to encourage collaboration among communities, government institutions, civil society organisations, traditional institutions and other stakeholders in advancing environmental restoration and ecological justice.

The project will also promote awareness campaigns, community advocacy and community-based environmental monitoring to strengthen local capacity to respond to the long-term impacts of oil pollution.

The inception meeting, according to the organisation, introduced stakeholders to the project’s implementation strategy and expected outcomes while seeking their support for its successful execution.

‘Communities must have a voice’

Speaking at the event, the Country Director of JRS Nigeria, Temple Anuforo represented by the Deputy Head of Programmes, Iniobong Ikpang, said meaningful community participation is essential to building resilience in environmentally vulnerable communities.

“For communities like Okoro Utip, resilience begins with ensuring that people have a voice in decisions affecting their environment and their future,” Mr Anuforo said.

“Through this partnership with CARITAS Canada, we are creating opportunities for communities, government institutions and civil society to talk, walk and work together in promoting environmental justice, restoring livelihoods and strengthening hope for both present and future generations.”

He added that the project reflects JRS Nigeria’s mission of accompanying, serving and advocating for vulnerable communities by placing them at the centre of developing lasting solutions.

Community welcomes intervention

The youth leader of Okoro Utip, Nsoh Nsoh, welcomed the project, saying years of oil pollution and gas flaring had significantly affected the community’s environment, livelihoods and public health.

“Our environment, livelihoods and health have been severely affected by oil pollution and gas flaring,” he said.

“Pollution has become part of our lives to the extent that we are beginning to accept it as normal. With this project, we are hopeful that we will learn legitimate ways to resist it so that we can have a better life.”

NOSDRA pledges support

The Assistant Director of the National Oil Spill Detection and Response Agency (NOSDRA) in the Uyo Zonal Office, Akaninyene Odungide, reaffirmed the agency’s commitment to responding promptly to oil spill incidents and holding polluters accountable.

Mr Odungide also urged residents to refrain from engaging in crude oil theft and illegal bunkering, advising them instead to report such activities to the appropriate authorities.

READ ALSO: JRS launches project to strengthen oil spill resilience in Akwa Ibom community

He assured stakeholders of NOSDRA’s readiness to collaborate with JRS Nigeria and other partners to ensure the successful implementation of the project.

JRS Nigeria, which has operated in the country since 2018, said it remains committed to supporting displaced and vulnerable communities through education, livelihoods, peacebuilding, mental health and psychosocial support, advocacy and community resilience programmes. Together with CARITAS Canada and other partners, it said the new initiative seeks to empower communities to advocate for a healthier environment while promoting sustainable livelihoods and long-term resilience.

World.title: Omidiran pledges support for ABU’s 2028 NUGA, sports excellence drive
World.content:
The Executive Chairman of the Federal Character Commission (FCC), Ayo Omidiran, has pledged support Ahmadu Bello University’s plans to host the 2028 Nigeria University Games (NUGA) and develop one of the country’s National Centres of Excellence in Sports.

Ms Omidiran made the commitment on Thursday when the university’s management, led by Vice-Chancellor Adamu Ahmed, paid her a courtesy visit at the FCC headquarters in Abuja.

An alumna of the institution, Ms Omidiran said Ahmadu Bello University (ABU), Zaria, played a defining role in shaping her leadership journey and reaffirmed her commitment to supporting initiatives that promote education, youth empowerment and national development.

“I remain immensely proud to be an alumna of Ahmadu Bello University. The university shaped my character, broadened my perspective and prepared me for the responsibilities of leadership and national service. I will always cherish the institution and remain committed to supporting initiatives that promote education, national development and youth empowerment,” she said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

She welcomed the university’s request for closer collaboration, describing its selection to host the 2028 NUGA Games and its designation as one of Nigeria’s National Centres of Excellence in Sports as significant opportunities to promote youth development and strengthen the country’s sports ecosystem.

The former member of the House of Representatives also accepted an invitation to attend the university’s 64th anniversary celebration scheduled for 4 October.

Earlier, Mr Ahmed described Ms Omidiran as one of ABU’s distinguished alumni, praising her contributions to public service and sports administration.

“As an alumna of Ahmadu Bello University, where you obtained your Bachelor of Science degree in Biochemistry and served as Student Union Government Secretary of Queen Amina Hall, you exemplify the values of leadership, excellence, integrity and service that our university seeks to instil in its graduates,” the vice-chancellor said.

He also highlighted her record as a two-term member of the House of Representatives, a pioneering member of FIFA’s Women’s Committee, Secretary of the Board of Trustees of the Nigerian Olympic Committee, founder of Omidiran Babes Football Club and now Executive Chairman of the Federal Character Commission.

Mr Ahmed said the university looked forward to drawing on Ms Omidiran’s experience in sports administration as it prepares to host the 2028 NUGA Games and establish a world-class sports development centre.

“These landmark developments present enormous opportunities for the university to contribute to sports development, talent discovery and youth empowerment. We look forward to drawing upon your vast experience, guidance and support as we prepare to deliver a memorable NUGA Games and build a Centre of Excellence that will become a national model for sports development,” he said.

The vice-chancellor also formally invited the FCC chair to participate in the university’s 64th anniversary celebration, describing her as an inspiration to students and alumni alike.

The ABU delegation included the Registrar, Rabiu Samaila; Director of Public Affairs, Awwal Umar; Director of Sports, Omeiza; Professors Danladi Amoh, Sani Ibrahim and Aliyu Salihu; Deputy Registrar Ingino Danjuma Voh; and Liaison Officer Haruna Ajo.

World.title: “Our mum asked Paul and Jude to apologise before she died, but they never did” — Mr P
World.content:
Nigerian singer Peter “Mr P” Okoye has alleged that his late mother, Josephine Okoye, repeatedly urged his brothers, Paul and Jude Okoye, to apologise to him and his wife, Lola Omotayo-Okoye, over the family’s treatment of them, but said the apology never came before her death.

PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that the singer’s mother died in 2012 at a hospital in India following heart surgery. Doctors initially admitted her to St. Nicholas Hospital on Lagos Island before transferring her abroad for further treatment.

Mr P made the claim in the latest instalment (part eight) of his ongoing tell-all video series on social media, where he has been revisiting the events that led to the collapse of P-Square and the strained relationship within the Okoye family.

The singer, who married Lola in 2013 after several years together, said his relationship with her was strongly opposed by Jude and, at times, Paul, long before their wedding. He alleged that the hostility continued even after the birth of their first child and persisted despite efforts by their late mother to reconcile the family.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Apology

According to Mr P, only his eldest brother apologised after his mother intervened, while Paul and Jude never did before she died in 2012.

The 44-year-old said, “While our mum was still around, she felt my pain. She said, ‘Don’t worry.’ When I was telling her everything, I said, ‘Mum, look at it this way: you thought you were telling me some good news, that the child is mine, but see how everyone left.’ She said, ‘No problem, I’ll talk to your brothers — they will apologise to you.’ I said, ‘No problem.’ My mum went back to Jos, and after about a week, she called me.

“She asked me, ‘Have they apologised?’ I said, ‘Only the first son, our firstborn, has apologised.’ She said, ‘Don’t worry, they will all apologise.’ After a few more weeks, Henry apologised too, except Paul and Jude, the ones I live with; they never did. One month, two months, three months, four months, five months, our mum died, and the apology was never made. My mum told them to do it, but they never did.”

Lola and Psquare’s mother’s relationship

Furthermore, the singer dismissed his brothers’ claims that their late mother never liked his wife.

He explained that his mother and Lola enjoyed a cordial relationship before her illness led to her hospitalisation in Lagos.

According to him, his mother had already accepted Lola and often referred to her as “our wife.”

“When our mum was sick in Jos, we flew her all the way to Lagos; we took her to St Nicholas Hospital on the Island, we live on the Mainland. Our mum was admitted, and four of her pastors came all the way from Jos to be with her. Guess where they stayed? Lola’s house. Lola got up as early as six o’clock every morning to make food for them, breakfast, everything. By seven o’clock, she would take them to the hospital and stay there. We lived on the Mainland so that we would arrive around eleven. When we came, Lola would leave for work.

“We stayed with our mum in the hospital with the pastors. By around six o’clock, Lola would leave work; her office wasn’t far from St Nicholas, and she would come back to the hospital. As soon as she arrived, we would leave. She stayed at the hospital until midnight, then took the pastors back to their house. The next morning, the same routine was repeated for over two months. During that time, in that hospital, they still tried to create a narrative that Lola and my mum never had a relationship, even though before I married Lola, my mum was already addressing her as ‘our wife’”, said Mr P.

Wedding

Mr P expressed concern that Jude was using his own twin brother as a pawn in what he described as his “evil games”, insisting that he had never been at odds with his brothers.

He also alleged that Jude scheduled a show for him in Ghana a day before his wedding to Lola.

According to him, despite personally giving Jude the fabric for the ceremony, Jude failed to attend the wedding.

“When I had my own wedding, my elder brother, our so-called manager, never attended. Let me tell you how bad it was: the night before my wedding, Jude booked a show with Globacom in Ghana, and showed me a return ticket for the next day, my wedding day, on a 2 o’clock flight. I said no, and insisted until they got us a private jet. I was at my own wedding. I was trending online for the wrong reason; Jude had posted a picture of himself at Mavin studio with Wizkid, Dr SID, Phyno, Don Jazzy and the rest of them.

“Jude posted that picture and started trending. Someone commented, something like, ‘You didn’t attend your brother’s wedding.’ He responded along the lines of, ‘If our mum were alive, this wedding wouldn’t have happened’, or something like that. And people said Jude was with Don Jazzy, Dr SID, Wizkid and Phyno, but all of them still left that studio and attended the wedding. My own senior brother, my manager, refused. I even arranged a barber for him and everything.”

Rudeboy responded to Mr P regarding their late mother’s legacy

Meanwhile, Rudeboy responded to Mr P’s claims about their mother. In a statement posted on his Instagram page, he said he regretted that their mother was no longer alive to defend herself.

He wrote, “Unfortunately, you’re not here to defend yourself and us. Continue resting, mum.”

As of the time of filing this report, Jude hasn’t responded to Mr P’s latest allegations.

The newspaper also reported that the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) investigated the dispute, leading to criminal charges against Jude over alleged money laundering involving about ₦1.38 billion, $1 million and £34,537.59.

Jude pleaded not guilty to the charges, and the case remains before the Federal High Court in Lagos.

During the court proceedings, Mr P testified for the prosecution, while Rudeboy publicly defended Jude, further exposing the rift within the family. The court initially remanded Jude in custody before later granting him bail.

Before P-Square split and the controversies that followed, the duo released several hit songs, including “Bizzy Body”, “Do Me”, “Personally”, “No One Like”, “You” and “Chop My Money”.

World.title: Davido, ex-presidential aide trade barbs amid Osun account freeze fallout
World.content:
Afrobeats star David Adeleke, popularly known as Davido, and former presidential aide Bashir Ahmad on Thursday exchanged sharp criticisms in a social media row sparked off on X by the controversies surrounding the 15 August Osun governorship election.

They traded barbs about their political influence, electoral credibility and Grammy nominations.

It began after Davido reacted in apparent excitement to presidential spokesperson Bayo Onanuga post on X sharing an update on the President Bola Tinubu’s intervention in the Osun State Government account freeze controversy.

Mr Onanuga announced in the post that President Tinubu had a phone conversation with Governor Ademola Adeleke, Davido’s uncle, to notify him that he had ordered the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) to lift the restriction it placed on the state government’s account.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Apparently thrilled by the phone call and suggesting that he was with the governor during the phone conversation, Davido wrote, tweetquoting Mr Onanuga’s post, “I was there live! I witnessed history!!!” The remark ended with Nigerian flag and laughter emojis.

However, Mr Ahmad, a former Special Assistant on Digital Communications to the late President Muhammadu Buhari and All Progressives Congress (APC) member, responded to the post by predicting that Davido would return to X to complain if the 15 August election did not go in his preferred candidate’s favour.

“This tweet is bookmarked. It will serve as a reference for future events. I know you will come back here to lament if the August 15 results don’t go your way,” Mr Ahmad wrote.

The exchange shifts to political and career records

Mr Ahmad’s ressponse set off a crossfire of barbs.

The clash moved beyond the Osun account controversy as both sides took aim at each other’s careers and records.

Davido suggested that concerns about possible electoral manipulation were legitimate. “Of course, because [the] same way you clowns can call the INEC Chairman to write Election results… guy free me my own no good.”

The singer then dragged up Mr Ahmad’s 2022 defeat in an All Progressives Congress (APC) primary election in Kano State.

During the APC primary election, Mr Ahmad lost the bid for the House of Representatives seat in Gaya/Ajingi/Albasu Federal Constituency, Kano, polling 16 votes against the winner’s 106.

“U got 16 votes bro in primaries!!” Davido tweeted on Thursday.

Mr Ahmad, rather than continuing the argument over the election, shifted the discussion to Davido’s Grammy record.

“We have talked enough about the number of votes I got in my primaries. Can we now talk about the number of Grammy Awards you have won from your five nominations, David? Fair is fair.”

He subsequently accused Davido of anticipating electoral defeat and using the possibility of rigging as an excuse ahead of the election.

“In politics, it is always those who know they lack a solid structure and have no real support on the ground who start screaming and crying rigging even before a single ballot is cast,” said Mr Ahmad.

He added that he believed Osun voters would return the state to the APC on August 15. “The good people of Osun are taking back their state on August 15th and we will be here to celebrate with them.”

Davido: ‘We all have different trophies’

Davido responded by rejecting Mr Ahmad’s attempt to measure his career solely by Grammy wins, pointing instead to his commercial success and international reach.

“You measure success by one award. I measure it by sold-out arenas, billions of streams, global influence, and people singing my songs across continents,” Davido tweeted.

The singer then returned to Mr Ahmad’s political career, arguing that his time in government had not translated into sufficient electoral support in his constituency.

“You had government backing and still couldn’t convince enough people to back you in your small constituency.”

Davido described Mr Ahmad as a “small boy who came into politics by accident” and said he had spent eight years around the late president without making what the singer considered a meaningful difference in his community.

He concluded: “We all have different trophies, Bashir. I’ll keep inspiring the young ones and generations to come while you wait for the next government job to get crumbs.”

Bashir brings Tyla into Grammy spat

Mr Ahmad later continued the Grammy-themed trolling by posting an AI-generated image of Davido holding a Grammy award with the caption, “Congratulations, David.”

He followed that with a photograph of South African singer Tyla holding her Grammy award, accompanied by the caption “Water. @davido.”

The post triggered another wave of reactions on X, with some users criticising Mr Ahmad for bringing a South African artiste into the argument, particularly amid recent concerns over attacks and xenophobic sentiments against Nigerians in South Africa.

Some commenters argued that if the intention was simply to mock Davido over the Grammy issue, Nigerian Grammy winners such as Burna Boy, Wizkid or Tems could have been used instead. Others defended Mr Ahmad or returned to the original argument over Davido’s five Grammy nominations.

Intersection of politics and entertainment

The exchange has since become one of the latest intersections of Nigeria’s entertainment and political conversations, coming just days before the keenly contested Osun governorship election.

Davido has openly backed Mr Adeleke’s re-election bid and joined the Accord Party’s campaign structure while Mr Ahmad rose to prominence during the APC-led administration of former President Buhari.

The clash also highlights how the August 15 election has increasingly spilled beyond conventional political campaigning, with prominent figures using social media to debate the credibility of the poll, the strength of political structures and the competing records of those involved.

The clash was an offshoot of the controversies surrounding forthcoming Osun State governorship election.

PREMIUM TIMES reported on Wednesday that the EFCC froze an account of the Osun State Government domiciled with First Bank, after which the anti-graft agency said the action followed suspicious movement of public funds from the account amid an ongoing investigation into alleged financial misconduct involving about 11N billion in Ecology Funds, Intervention Funds and Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) allocations.

On Thursday, Mr Tinubu directed the EFCC to lift the restriction on the account, describing the timing of the action, coming about 10 days before the governorship election, as inauspicious and capable of creating the impression that a federal agency was being used to interfere with the poll.

The president said he found the EFCC’s action deeply embarrassing.

Presidential spokesman, Mr Onanuga subsequently announced on Thursday that Mr Tinubu spoke with Mr Adeleke in a phone conversation, informing the governor that he had directed to lift the order restricting the account of the Osun State Government.

World.title: WAFCON 2026: Nigeria-Cameroon, Morocco-South Africa headline blockbuster quarter-finals
World.content:
The quarter-final picture at the 2026 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations is now complete, with defending champions Nigeria handed a blockbuster meeting with Cameroon in what promises to be one of the tournament’s most compelling last-eight ties.

The final quarter-finalists were confirmed on Thursday after Cameroon secured top spot in Group D with a 1-1 draw against tournament debutants Cape Verde in Casablanca.

The result ensured the Indomitable Lionesses finished the group stage unbeaten, collecting seven points from three matches after recording two victories and a draw.

That was enough to set up a mouthwatering clash with Nigeria, who progressed to the knockout rounds as Group C runners-up after recovering from a shock opening defeat to Malawi with victories over Zambia and Egypt.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

For Cameroon, the quarter-final represents another significant test of their credentials. They have shown consistency throughout the group stage and will now face a Nigeria side determined to defend the continental crown it won at the previous edition.

The Super Falcons will also have history and experience on their side, but Cameroon’s unbeaten run means they will arrive at the quarter-final with plenty of confidence.

Cape Verde, meanwhile, bowed out of their maiden WAFCON campaign with a point to show for their efforts. The debutants secured their first-ever point at the continental finals with the draw against Cameroon, bringing a memorable first appearance to an end.

Four heavyweight quarter-finals, one prize beyond the trophy

The quarter-finals begin on Saturday, with four intriguing encounters spread across Casablanca and Rabat.

Côte d’Ivoire will face Algeria in Casablanca in the opening quarter-final before hosts Morocco take on defending runners-up South Africa in Rabat later in the evening.

The Ivorians have impressed on their return to the continental stage and finished top of Group B unbeaten, while Algeria will be looking to continue their impressive campaign against one of the tournament’s emerging forces.

The second fixture of the day could be equally explosive, with Morocco enjoying home advantage against South Africa.

The hosts will look to draw on the backing of their home crowd to overcome a Banyana Banyana side that secured their place in the knockout rounds with a strong finish to Group B.

Sunday brings the headline fixture, as Cameroon and Nigeria will meet in Casablanca, with the winner advancing to the semi-finals and taking another major step towards continental glory.

The other quarter-final will see Malawi face Ghana in Rabat.

Malawi have already produced one of the biggest shocks of the tournament by defeating Nigeria in their opening Group C fixture. However, Ghana will provide another major test as both sides chase a place in the final four.

World Cup qualification adds another layer

Beyond the battle for the WAFCON title, there is an even bigger prize at stake.

The four teams that win their quarter-final ties will automatically qualify for the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup in Brazil, and this makes the last-eight fixtures more than a straight fight for a place in the semi-finals.

For the four winners, victory will secure continental glory ambitions while also guaranteeing a place on football’s biggest global stage next year.

With Nigeria, Cameroon, Morocco, South Africa, Côte d’Ivoire, Algeria, Malawi and Ghana all still dreaming of the title, the knockout stage promises little room for error.

The race for the trophy has entered its decisive phase.

2026 WAFCON quarter-final fixtures

Saturday

Côte d’Ivoire vs Algeria

Morocco vs South Africa

Sunday

Cameroon vs Nigeria

Malawi vs Ghana

Four matches, four straight World Cup tickets; but, only four teams can emerge with their WAFCON title dreams still alive.

Which of these would they be?

World.title: Okowa backs state police, says reform will strengthen fight against insecurity
World.content:
By Ochuko Akuopha, Asaba

Immediate past Governor of Delta State, Senator Ifeanyi Okowa, has described President Bola Tinubu’s push for the establishment of state police as a bold step towards addressing Nigeria’s security challenges and deepening the devolution of powers to the states.

Okowa said the campaign for state police dates back to 2000, noting that previous administrations had been reluctant to pursue the reform.

“The agitation for state police started as far back as the year 2000. No president had been bold enough to allow the devolution of power. But this president is bold enough to say that this is the best way to ensure that we are able to secure the land,” he said.

Speaking on Friday at the All Progressives Congress (APC) Delta North Stakeholders’ Meeting in Asaba, Okowa argued that state police would better position governors to tackle insecurity in their respective states.

The meeting also endorsed President Tinubu and Delta State Governor Sheriff Oborevwori for second terms in the 2027 general elections.

The motion for the endorsement was moved by the APC House of Representatives candidate for Aniocha/Oshimili Federal Constituency, Mr. Ndudi Elumelu, and seconded by Mr. Frank Esenwa. It was unanimously adopted by stakeholders.

Okowa stressed that the proposed state police system would complement, rather than replace, the Nigeria Police Force.

“We are not talking about ending the federal police. Let each state have its own police, committed to its people, properly trained, properly armed and dedicated to securing the land,” he said.

According to the former governor, Nigeria requires leaders who are prepared to take difficult decisions in the national interest.

“We want a president who is able to take bold decisions that will secure today and the future. The lives of Nigerians matter more than what is politically correct,” he added.

Also speaking, Delta State Deputy Governor, Sir Monday Onyeme, called for unity and cohesion within the APC ahead of the 2027 elections.

He urged party members to reconcile with aggrieved aspirants who lost out during the party’s primaries and encourage them to work for the party’s success.

Onyeme also commended President Tinubu for supporting the state police initiative.

“We need state police because the federal police cannot reach all the nooks and crannies. Today, it is becoming a reality. Who made that possible? President Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” he said.

The Delta State APC Chairman, Chief Solomon Areyenka, and the party’s Delta North Chairman, Mr. Dan Ossai, also urged members to remain united and work diligently to ensure the party’s success in the 2027 general elections.

World.title: Gunmen kidnap two farmers in Ondo, demand N100m ransom
World.content:
Stock image

…Police, Amotekun launch rescue operation

By Dayo Johnson, Akure

Suspected gunmen have abducted two farmers in Parubber Community, Ile-Oluji/Okeigbo Local Government Area of Ondo State, with the kidnappers reportedly demanding a ransom of N100 million for their release.

A family source said the victims were ambushed on their farms on Monday and taken into a nearby forest by the assailants.

One of the farmers who escaped the attack, Pastor Yemi Omowale, said the incident had been reported to the police and the Ondo State Security Network Agency, codenamed Amotekun.

Omowale, who operates a piggery farm in Parubber Community along the Ondo-Ife Road, recounted the incident.

“I run a piggery farm in Parubber Community along Ondo-Ife Road in Ile-Oluji/Okeigbo Local Government Area. We went there in the morning to feed the animals.

“Between 12 noon and 1 p.m. on Monday, we were working outside when I saw a masked man carrying an AK-47 moving towards one of the victims, Adetan Adebanjo Gbemi, because we were not standing together,” he said.

According to him, the abductors have contacted the wife of one of the victims and are demanding N100 million as ransom.

“They have been calling the victim’s wife to ask how much she has been able to raise. We are appealing to the security agencies and the government to help rescue our brother and sister unharmed,” Omowale said.

Confirming the incident, the spokesperson for the Ondo State Police Command, DSP Jimoh Abayomi, said the Oke-Igbo Divisional Headquarters received a report that the victims were missing.

He said a joint security team comprising police operatives, including the Anti-Kidnapping Squad, Amotekun personnel, local hunters and vigilantes, had been deployed to the area.

“Search and rescue operations are currently ongoing, with all available operational and intelligence resources being deployed to locate the victims and bring the perpetrators to justice,” Abayomi said.

He added that efforts were being intensified to rescue the victims unharmed and apprehend those behind the abduction.

The police spokesperson urged residents to remain calm and provide any credible information that could assist the ongoing operation through the nearest police formation.

He reaffirmed the command’s commitment to securing the safe release of the victims and ensuring the suspects are brought to justice.

World.title: US economy loses 23,000 jobs in July, raises concerns for job seekers
World.content:
The United States labour market suffered an unexpected setback in July, with the economy losing 23,000 jobs amid signs that employers are becoming increasingly cautious about hiring.

The latest figures, released Friday by the Bureau of Labor Statistics, came well below economists’ expectations of a 95,000-job increase.

Despite the job losses, the unemployment rate fell slightly to 4.1 per cent from 4.2 per cent, as more people exited the labour force.

The July figures represented a sharp deterioration from June, whose employment gains were revised down to 20,000 from the previously reported 57,000.

May’s employment gains were also significantly revised, falling to 66,000 from 129,000.

The latest figures add to concerns about the health of the US labour market, which had appeared to be stabilising after recording weak employment growth in 2025.

The labour market has remained in what has been described as a “low-hire, low-fire” environment, leaving fewer opportunities for people searching for work.

Economists say employers are facing several pressures, including an ageing population, the rapid adoption of artificial intelligence, higher oil prices, policy uncertainty and the war with Iran.

Nicole Bachaud, a labour economist at ZipRecruiter, said employers could be becoming more reluctant to recruit amid economic uncertainty.

“Price volatility may be contributing to increased hesitation from employers,” Nicole Bachaud, labor economist at ZipRecruiter, wrote in a note Friday. “With job opportunities remaining scarce, more workers are exiting the labor market entirely.

Healthcare leads job growth

Job creation was also uneven across sectors, with healthcare and social assistance accounting for most of the gains.

The sector added an estimated 22,600 jobs in July, making it the largest job creator during the month.

However, several other sectors recorded significant losses.

Local government employment fell by 57,000 jobs, while the leisure and hospitality sector lost 40,000 jobs in July, following a decline of 43,000 positions in June.

Wage growth also slowed during the month.

Average hourly earnings increased by just 0.1 per cent from June, pushing the annual wage growth rate down to 3.2 per cent — its lowest level in five years.

The weaker wage growth comes as inflation remains elevated, with the latest Consumer Price Index showing inflation at 3.5 per cent.

The combination of slower hiring, weak wage growth and persistent inflation could make conditions more challenging for workers and job seekers in the US.
