Poland’s largest opposition party, the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), has called for Ukrainian men of conscription age who are not legally working to be deported to Ukraine. The policy, which continues a recent hardening of PiS’s position towards Ukraine and Ukrainians as it competes with the far right for support, was condemned by government figures, who called it “absurd” and “disgusting”. 🇵🇱 Bezpieczeństwo obywateli powinno być priorytetem każdego rządu. Potrzebne są zdecydowane działania wobec osób przebywających w Polsce niezgodnie z prawem. 👉 Udostępnij! 🔥 Ku nowemu rządowi! pic.twitter.com/m8MctmmPXd — Prawo i Sprawiedliwość (@pisorgpl) August 6, 2026 On Thursday, PiS, which has recently been hit by falling support in the polls and the defection of a large breakaway group of more moderate MPs, held a policy convention at which it presented ideas it wants to implement if it returns to power after next year’s parliamentary elections. “One of [our] government’s first, most significant decisions will be to deport men, Ukrainians of military age, who are not legally working in Poland,” announced Tobiasz Bocheński, a deputy leader of the party. “They will have the opportunity to fight for their homeland, so that the horrors of this war can quickly end,” he continued. “Because for Central and Eastern Europe to be secure and free, Ukraine must win.” Bocheński denied that the policy was inhumane, noting that, in 2022, when PiS was in government, “Poles, like no other nation in Europe, opened their hearts, their homes and their wallets to women, children, the elderly and disabled people fleeing Putin’s bombs”. Poland was the primary destination for refugees fleeing Ukraine in 2022. Almost one million of them remain in the country, alongside hundreds of thousands of other Ukrainian immigrants, many of whom arrived before 2022. They are by far Poland’s largest foreign national group. In their announcement of the proposed policy, PiS gave no details of how it would work in practice, nor on what legal basis Ukrainians who are legally resident in Poland and have not violated any laws would be deported. News website Interia, which had reported on PiS’s plans shortly before they were officially announced, notes that data from Poland’s labour ministry show that only around 11,000 Ukrainians are registered as unemployed in Poland. The figures are not broken down by gender, but most are believed to be women. However, PiS’s policy would also apply to Ukrainians in the so-called grey economy, where people work informally without registering or paying taxes, reports Interia. Military-age Ukrainian men in other European countries should not receive social benefits, says Poland's foreign minister, @sikorskiradek. "There should be no financial incentives for avoiding the draft" https://t.co/5TcTqyDa6X — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 16, 2024 PiS’s plan was immediately criticised by government figures, with interior ministry spokeswoman Karolina Gałecka calling it “an absurd idea” and “pure demagoguery”. She noted that over 95% of Ukrainian men of conscription age in Poland are working legally and paying taxes. “Without these people, many key sectors of the Polish economy would simply grind to a halt,” wrote Gałecka. “Stop the incitement.” Deputy interior minister Maciej Duszczyk, meanwhile, told broadcaster TVN that, among the Ukrainian men not working, many are wounded soldiers in Poland for treatment and rehabilitation or fathers caring for disabled children. Deportations are a “purely political, disgusting idea”, he added. Interior minister Marcin Kierwiński wrote that, “when [PiS] was in power, they couldn’t even deport those who were breaking the law, and now they’re supposedly going to deport everyone without rhyme or reason”. Since taking power, the current government has increased deportations of foreigners who are in Poland illegally or broke the law while in the country. Last year, it carried out over 9,000 deportations, up from 7,200 in 2023, the last year that PiS was in power Absurdalny pomysł @pisorgpl ws. deportacji Ukraińców to czysta demagogia! Ponad 95% mężczyzn w wieku poborowym legalnie pracuje w 🇵🇱 i płaci podatki (dane ZUS).@OficjalnyJK zapowiada deportacje. A jak miałoby to wyglądać w praktyce? Patrole sprawdzające dokumenty na ulicach?… — Karolina Gałecka (@K_Galecka) August 6, 2026 During the conference on Thursday, PiS emphasised its tough approach to migration more broadly, saying that it would “create a new, restrictive system for foreigners” that would track each immigrant in the country. “Every foreigner will have their own individual account,” and if they commit any offences or fail to abide by any administrative obligations, “the information will be immediately entered into the system, and the deportation process will begin”, said Bocheński. “The only good migration is the return of Poles from abroad,” declared the party on social media. 🛡️ Bezpieczne granice to bezpieczna Polska. Skuteczna ochrona granic i walka z nielegalną imigracją to obowiązek każdego odpowiedzialnego państwa. 👉 Udostępnij! 🔥 Ku nowemu rządowi! pic.twitter.com/rRPZpmXi5U — Prawo i Sprawiedliwość (@pisorgpl) August 6, 2026 In fact, it was during PiS’s time in power from 2015 to 2023 that Poland saw the largest wave of immigration in its history, and one of the largest anywhere in Europe. In every year between 2017 and 2022, Poland was the EU member state that issued the highest number of first residence permits to immigrants from outside the bloc. There are now over two million foreigners registered as living in Poland, making up just 5% of the population. Around three quarters are Ukrainians (1.55 million), with the next largest groups being Belarusians (139,300), Indians (26,100), Georgians (22,200), Russians (19,500), Vietnamese (15,100) and Turks (14,500). The number of foreigners with residence permits in Poland has reached two million, making up just over 5% of the country’s population, new government data show. The largest national group by far are Ukrainians, followed by Belarusians and Indians https://t.co/SI09WtR7hR — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) April 26, 2026 While in government, PiS welcomed Ukrainian migrants and refugees and was a strong supporter of Ukraine in its defence against Russian aggression. However, since going into opposition, it has taken an increasingly tough line. That has reflected a broader shift in Polish society, with a variety of polls showing rising negative sentiment towards Ukraine and Ukrainians. Recent months have also seen a rise in reported hate crimes against Ukrainians in Poland, including a number of high-profile incidents. Meanwhile, two far-right parties that have long taken an anti-Ukrainian stance, Confederation (Konfederacja) and Confederation of the Polish Crown (KKP), have soared in the polls, placing pressure on PiS to toughen its own position. One Confederation MEP, Stanisław Tyszka, mocked PiS’s latest policy announcement. “PiS wants to heroically deport hundreds of thousands of Ukrainians whom they themselves let into Poland,” he wrote. “Comedy.” The number of reported hate crimes against Ukrainians in Poland is up 30% so far this year, police data show. Poland’s power grid operator, PSE, has, for the second time in three days and third time this summer, invoked emergency measures to ensure supply amid an ongoing heatwave. Before this summer, it had only done so twice in the eight years since such powers were introduced. However, following a meeting with PSE and other state energy officials, Prime Minister Donald Tusk has assured Poles that, despite “a very difficult period”, the “situation is under control” and power supplies are secure, thanks in part to the growth of renewables in recent years. ❗️PSE ponownie ogłaszają okresy przywołania na rynku mocy❗️ To już 3. raz w tym roku, kiedy operator sięga po to narzędzie. W historii zdarzyło się to tylko 5 razy, wliczywszy 3 przypadki tegoroczne, co pokazuje wyjątkowość roku 2026 dla energetyki. pic.twitter.com/DbCPnpyae4 — Jakub Wiech (@jakubwiech) August 6, 2026 PSE has called on contracted electricity generators to increase output and large consumers to cut use to help balance the grid on Thursday between 5:00 p.m. and 10:00 p.m., as temperatures have this week approached 40°C (104°F) in many parts of the country. The same measures were introduced on Tuesday, as the heatwave pushed up electricity consumption, partly due to increased use of air conditioning and refrigeration. Participants in Poland’s capacity market are paid for maintaining standby capacity and fulfilling their obligations when called upon by the operator. According to PSE, the mechanism is “a remedial measure” used when the generation capacity available to the operator falls significantly below the required safety level. Previously, the measures were invoked in June this year, amid another heatwave that saw Poland hit its highest-ever recorded temperature of 40.5°C. But before that, they had only been used twice since being introduced in 2018. Temperatures in Poland have reached the highest level on record, with a figure of 40.3°C (104.5°F) recorded this afternoon, as the heatwave that has hit Europe this week moves eastwards https://t.co/eRhRxiuCGq — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 28, 2026 Poland’s weather institute IMGW issued heat warnings on Thursday for 13 of the country’s 16 provinces, with daytime temperatures forecast to reach between 33C and 38C. High temperatures and prolonged drought conditions have also pushed water levels in many rivers to extremely low levels, with the Vistula, Poland’s longest river, only 5 centimetres above the historic low of 4 centimetres it fell to in Warsaw last year. Some other parts of the river have hit all-time record lows, reports Polsat News. One result has been a disruption of cooling supplies to Poland’s power sector. State energy firm Enea this week announced reduced operations at two of its coal-fired plants that are cooled by water from the Vistula. Around 1.1 gigawatts (GW) of capacity (just over 1% of Poland’s total) has gone offline. On Wednesday, Prime Minister Donald Tusk convened a meeting of a government crisis team, including PSE’s deputy president, to discuss the current heatwave and its potential impact on the power sector. However, afterwards he assured that “the situation is under control” and that the fact that Poland now has “a lot of energy from solar panels and wind turbines makes our system relatively secure”, reports the Polish Press Agency (PAP). Poland’s renewable sector has expanded rapidly over the last decade. Last year, it provided just over 29% of the country’s power, with onshore wind supplying 14% of the energy mix and solar 12%. Renewables generated 29.4% of Poland's electricity in 2025, almost exactly the same figure as in 2024, ending a period of strong growth since 2021. Coal (52.2%) remained the dominant source, though its share declined. Poland’s top administrative court has upheld a decision by the finance ministry to withhold state subsidies from the national-conservative opposition Law and Justice (PiS) party due to campaign finance irregularities. The decision was welcomed by the government, with Prime Minister Donald Tusk saying that there will be “no money for grifters”. PiS, however, argues that the money is being withheld for political reasons and accuses the authorities of “Russian standards”. Naczelny Sąd Administracyjny oddalił w środę kasacje ws. dotacji i subwencji dla PiS. – Miażdżący dla PiS wyrok podtrzymany! – stwierdził szef MF Andrzej Domański https://t.co/bcL18WbiYf — OKO.press (@oko_press) August 6, 2026 The dispute dates back to August 2024, when the National Electoral Commission (PKW) rejected PiS’s financial report for the previous year’s parliamentary election campaign after identifying around 3.6 million zloty (€838,000) in unauthorised expenditure. As a result, the PKW ordered that PiS should lose 10.8 million zloty from the state subsidies that political parties in Poland receive based on their level of electoral support. The party would normally have received 25.9 million zloty based on its 2023 election result. The decision triggered months of legal wrangling, with PiS arguing that the funding should be restored after the Supreme Court upheld its complaint against the PKW’s decision. However, finance minister Andrzej Domański refused to release the money, saying there were unresolved legal doubts over the ruling. The finance minister has refused to comply with the electoral commission's decision to pay out subsidies to the opposition PiS party He says there are "legal doubts" over the issue. But PiS says he is obliged to pay and will be held criminally responsible https://t.co/ZwIZRqn5tp — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) January 9, 2025 Those doubts stem from a broader dispute over the controversial and contested judicial reforms implemented by PiS when it ruled Poland from 2015 to 2023. The chamber of the Supreme Court that ruled in PiS’s favour was created as part of those reforms. It has previously been found to not be a legitimate body by both the European Court of Justice and European Court of Human Rights because it contains improperly appointed judges. After the Supreme Court chamber’s ruling, the PKW initially said it would not recognise the decision until the chamber’s legal status was clarified. Two weeks later, however, it reversed that decision and approved PiS’s financial report. Domański still declined to restore the subsidy, arguing that the PKW’s resolution was internally contradictory. While it approved the payments, it also stated that the chamber’s ruling should come from a body recognised as a court and that it was not determining whether the chamber met that standard. PiS challenged Domański’s decision. However, its case was initially rejected by a lower court in June last year, and that decision has now been upheld by the Supreme Administrative Court (NSA), which is the final court of appeal for administrative issues. The NSA found the minister had acted lawfully in withholding the funding. It also said the Supreme Court chamber’s ruling had no legal effect because it had been issued by a body that was not a properly constituted court, reports news website OKO.press. The ruling was welcomed by Domański, who called it a “crushing blow to PiS” and said that “yet another PiS lie has been exposed”. Prime Minister Donald Tusk, meanwhile, wrote on social media: “Just as we said, there is and will be no money for grifters.” Tak jak mówiliśmy, dla przekręciarzy pieniędzy nie ma i nie będzie. https://t.co/4Kqexj6NoC — Donald Tusk (@donaldtusk) August 5, 2026 The PKW’s decision to cut PiS’s funds was made after it found that government resources – including from the justice ministry, Government Legislation Centre (RCL) and Research and Academic Computer Network (NASK) – had been used to support the party’s election campaign. However, PiS has always argued that the decision was a political one, implemented at the behest of the new Tusk government in order to undermine the main opposition party. Radosław Fogiel, a senior PiS lawmaker and former party spokesman, said that the new NSA ruling “does not change the essence of the matter: it unlawfully deprives the main opposition party of the subsidy to which it is entitled. World.title: Polish prosecutors end 10-year treason investigation into Tusk over Smolensk air disaster
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. After a ten-year-long investigation, prosecutors have concluded that Poland’s government in 2010 – which was led by current Prime Minister Donald Tusk – was not guilty of “diplomatic treason” in its response to the plane crash in Russia that killed President Lech Kaczyński. The national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) party – which ruled Poland from 2015 to 2023 and is led by Lech’s twin brother, Jarosław – has always rejected the findings of official Polish and Russian investigations into the crash, which found it to have been an accident. Instead, PiS claims that the disaster, which claimed the lives of 96 people, many of them senior Polish state officials, was caused deliberately by Russia and then covered up with the help of Tusk’s government. However, while PiS launched various investigations during its time in power, it has never substantiated its claims. And prosecutors now say that there is no evidence that diplomatic treason, a crime that carries a potential prison sentence of up to ten years, took place. Uprzednio wygrałem sprawę cywilną z posłem @OficjalnyJK, który w efekcie musiał wpłacić 50,000zł na siły zbrojne broniącej się Ukrainy. Teraz potwierdzenie @PK_GOV_PL: nie było żadnej zdrady dyplomatycznej ani żadnej intencji jej popełnienia. Oczywiście żaden z kłamców… https://t.co/VKZHlF5xkX — Radosław Sikorski 🇵🇱🇪🇺 (@sikorskiradek) August 5, 2026 Wednesday’s announcement by the National Prosecutor’s Office was welcomed by Radosław Sikorski, the current foreign minister, who held the same role in 2010. He condemned the “Smolensk liars”, such as Jarosław Kaczyński, who he suggested had exploited the tragedy for their own benefit. “They brainwashed millions of people, divided families, stirred up hatred within the nation,” he wrote. “They’ll burn in hell for it. But the power, money and satisfaction they gained from spitting on their rivals – that’s theirs.” The idea that Smolensk was an assassination of Lech Kaczyński has been a core part of PiS rhetoric. In 2022, for example, Jarosław Kaczyński said that the decision was made “at the highest level of the Kremlin” and Tusk’s government then “covered up” the incident as part of a “macabre reconciliation with Russia”. Smolensk was an “attack decided at the highest level of the Kremlin”, says Jarosław Kaczyński ahead of the 12th anniversary of the crash. Donald Tusk's government then “covered up” the incident as part of a “macabre reconciliation with Russia”, he adds https://t.co/5ae0gHJj3B — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) April 4, 2022 The investigation into diplomatic treason – a crime consisting of acting to the detriment of Poland while authorised to represent the country in relations with foreign states or organisations – was launched in August 2016, less than a year after PiS had come to power. Among the individuals who had formally notified prosecutors of a potential crime was PiS deputy leader Antoni Macierewicz, who from 2015 to 2018 served as defence minister. He has been the foremost proponent of conspiracy theories around the Smolensk air disaster. In their notifications to prosecutors, Macierewicz and the others accused Tusk and other officials of, in their relations with Russia, deliberately choosing a legal basis for an investigation into the crash that was unfavourable to Poland by giving it no real influence over how it was run. However, prosecutors now say that, after ten years in which they questioned 488 witnesses, gathered extensive documentation and requested legal assistance from several countries, they have “concluded that no crime of diplomatic treason was committed”. In a statement explaining the decision, the National Prosecutor’s Office said that the legal basis chosen for cooperating with Russia on an investigation – Annex 13 of the Convention on International Civil Aviation – was, in fact, “the most advantageous solution” for Poland. It ensured the participation of Polish representatives in the Russian-led investigation, including access to the wreckage and crash site. Other legal options would have offered no greater benefits and involved significant risks, concluded the Polish prosecutors. They acknowledged that Russia “subsequently failed to fulfil some of its obligations arising from the adopted procedure”, but said this should have no bearing on assessing the decisions that were previously made on setting up the investigation. The defence ministry will notify prosecutors of 41 suspected crimes linked to a commission established by the former PiS government to investigate the 2010 plane crash in Russia that killed President Lech Kaczyński https://t.co/aEAlmk9lDM — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 24, 2024 The prosecutors also found that, not only did Polish officials choose the best legal solution, but there was also “no evidence indicating that individuals authorised to act on behalf of Poland, including the prime minister and members of the Council of Ministers, acted with the intent to harm Poland”. Given that the crime of diplomatic treason requires intent, this finding further reinforced the decision to drop the investigation. However, the prosecutors note that their decision can still be appealed. At the time of writing, neither Kaczyński, Macierewicz, nor other senior PiS figures had commented on the prosecutors’ announcement. Poland has urged the European Union to adopt tougher measures in response to the recent migration crisis in Spain’s African exclave of Ceuta, including making migrants who enter the bloc illegally ineligible for obtaining residence rights. Dozens died while trying to cross. Among those who managed to enter Ceuta, Spain says that the vast majority have been returned to Morocco. The incident prompted expressions of concern from many European leaders, including calls to restrict Spain’s participation in the Schengen free movement zone (despite the fact that anyone leaving Ceuta for the European mainland is subject to identity checks). Among those to speak out was Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk, who on Friday called on Spain to “follow our example if Schengen is to survive”. Poland has tightened asylum laws, border procedures, and has built effective barriers on its border with Belarus, which is the eastern border of the EU. We have invested billions of euros and engaged thousands of soldiers, police officers and border guards. Spain must follow our… — Donald Tusk (@donaldtusk) July 31, 2026 That was a reference to Poland’s response to a crisis on its eastern border, where since 2021 Belarus has encouraged and assisted tens of thousands of migrants – mainly from Asia and Africa – to try to cross irregularly into the EU. Both Poland and the EU have accused Belarus and its ally Russia of deliberately “weaponising” migration in an attempt to destabilise European societies as part of Moscow and Minsk’s broader “hybrid threats” against the EU. Tusk noted that, in response, Poland has restricted the right to asylum, invested billions in strengthening physical and electronic barriers along the border, and has deployed thousands of soldiers, police officers and border guards there (who have also been given expanded rights to use firearms). A court has ruled that Poland's recently introduced partial suspension of the right to asylum is justified and lawful. It rejected a complaint by a Sudanese man who had been denied the right to claim asylum after crossing irregularly from Belarus https://t.co/jx3s1AxRgG — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 10, 2025 On Saturday, Tusk and 21 other EU leaders jointly signed a letter expressing “serious concern” at the situation in Ceuta and warning that the EU “cannot allow uncontrolled mass border crossings, the instrumentalisation of migration, or other hybrid threats to create the impression that illegal entry…is possible”. While they welcomed Spain’s cooperation with Morocco to send most of the migrants back, they also called for an extraordinary meeting of EU interior ministers to “agree on a coordinated European response, including the rapid mobilisation of available EU instruments and the necessary support to Spain”. At that meeting, which took place on Tuesday, Poland’s interior ministry said that it had expressed the view that “illegal entry into the European Union should automatically exclude the possibility of obtaining residence permits, and therefore the possibility of permanent stay in the future”. While Poland’s statement did not mention it directly, earlier this year Spain’s government launched an amnesty that allowed undocumented migrants to apply to legalise their stay in the country. Over one million people had signed up for the scheme by the time it closed at the end of June. In its statement, Poland’s interior ministry warned that “migration must be fully controlled”, as otherwise it can “be used against the values that guide the EU”. It also called for the “official recognition of migration as a challenge directly linked to security”. It added that during Tuesday’s meeting it had “presented its own experiences with border protection in the context of the instrumentalisation and weaponisation of migration and adapting law to migration challenges”, including restrictions on asylum claims. “The example of Ceuta clearly demonstrates that absolute access to asylum is impossible to maintain in the face of such real threats,” wrote the interior ministry, which said that it “welcomed the shared perspective on migration among a growing number of member states”. In a statement of its own, the European Council noted that there had been a “common understanding of the need to continue relentlessly fighting migrant smuggling networks, to reinforce returns, to strengthen EU borders, to build deep partnerships with third countries, and to improve foresight.” It added that member states “were united in expressing strong solidarity with Spain”, appreciated its “swift and effective efforts” to deal with the crisis, and had also expressed their condolences for the people who died while attempting to cross from Morocco to Ceuta. World.title: Construction Disrupts Prague Tourists and Businesses During Peak Summer Season
World.content:
Construction projects across Prague’s historic center are proving a pain for tourists and locals alike who say the clumps of dirt, building supplies and equipment block popular sites and make it difficult to move around one of Europe’s most visited cities.



Heading down Národní to the Charles Bridge or going for a beer near the Vltava river now looks more like a vast construction site where tourists need to look out for more than the cobble-stone streets and baroque spires.

“It’s their first time here too, [they’ve] never seen it and now it’s torn up,” said Sherryl, a tourist visiting from the United States with her friends.

A major source of the disruption are upgrades to the public transport system. The central tram route delivering travelers to the heart of the city near the Národní Divadlo stop has been shuttered for weeks.

The disruption has taken a heavy toll on surrounding businesses like Aggeo, an Italian grocery store along the corridor. Its manager, Irena Kumpová, noted a sharp drop in foot traffic from travelers and regular local customers, who stroll by the National Theater on their way to gaze at the artist David Černý’s famous Kafka head.

“I’d rather stay closed… it’s a catastrophe,” remarked Kumpová.

With tourism growing every year in Prague, the widespread construction is making its mark this summer. So far this year, 1.7 million people have visited Prague, marking the strongest start in 15 years, according to Prague City Tourism and the Czech Statistical Office.

Tram services are suspended through the city center, clogging the streets and forcing many to find another way to work or home. For businesses that rely on heavy foot traffic during the busiest months of the year, that means less earnings.

“I have a table outside, but mainly just to signal to people that we’re open, but no one sits there right now,” said Kumpová.

The reconstruction is part of Prague’s broader effort to modernize its transport network, including long-term investments such as the future tram connection to Wenceslas Square and the expansion of Metro Line D as the city seeks to expand public transport.

Not everybody minds the disruption. The loud machines, dusty air, and obstructed sidewalks offer a certain charm for some who view the construction as part of the sightseeing experience.

“Despite the construction, it’s still beautiful,” said Raluca Costachescu, a traveler from Romania.

Written by: Mae Bryant, Bilyana Spasova, Milica Petrušová, Zuzana Kormančíková, Zhanna Bekiryan

World.title: Live Nation and PPF to Run Three Major Prague Venues
World.content:
Live Nation and PPF Group are forming a joint venture that will operate three of Prague’s major event venues — O2 Arena, O2 Universum and Forum Karlín.

The companies plan to invest in the venues and upgrade their facilities, with Live Nation set to hold a 51 percent stake in the new company.

The agreement will bring together one of the world’s largest live entertainment companies and PPF, the investment group that owns O2 Arena and O2 Universum through its subsidiary Bestsport.



PPF has also operated Forum Karlín, which has been owned by Patria Investment Company since last year.

The companies announced the planned partnership in a joint statement. Financial details of the transaction and the amount of the planned investment have not been disclosed. The deal remains subject to the required regulatory approvals.

Under the agreement, the new operator will be responsible for the day-to-day running of all three venues, including event planning and programming. The venues themselves will remain under their existing ownership structures, and their names will not change.

The partners said they intend to invest substantially in the facilities over the coming years. The aim is to improve conditions for audiences and performers while expanding the number of events held in Prague and strengthening the city’s position on the international concert and entertainment circuit.

PPF said the cooperation with Live Nation is also part of its strategy of developing the long-term value of its assets alongside major international companies.

Live Nation Entertainment operates across several areas of the live entertainment industry, including concert promotion, ticketing and sponsorship. Its businesses include Live Nation Concerts, Ticketmaster and Live Nation Sponsorship.

PPF Group is an international investment company with holdings across Europe, North America and Asia. Its portfolio includes telecommunications, media, financial services, real estate, e-commerce, industry and biotechnology.

World.title: Prague to Restore Tram Service Between Holešovice and City Center
World.content:
Residents of Prague 7 will regain a tram connection between Holešovice and the city center from September, with tram line 5 set to operate through the district and continue toward Wenceslas Square.

The change follows months of pressure from Prague 7 officials and local residents, who have called for better tram connections since the cancellation of line 14.

The district had previously requested either the return of line 14 or the introduction of an equivalent service and organized a petition supporting the demand.



The new arrangement will initially be temporary. According to the Prague Integrated Transport (PID) system, two trams will operate on the route at least through December 2026.

Line 5 to replace temporary route

The new service is linked to planned transport changes in Žižkov. Because of a traffic closure there, tram line 34 will be replaced by line 5 in Holešovice.

At Holešovice train station, line 5 will connect with line 6, effectively creating a continuous service between the two routes. Trams will run from the station through the Holešovice area, past the market and across Vltavská Street before continuing toward Wenceslas Square and other parts of central Prague.

For passengers in Holešovice, the move restores a connection that was lost when line 14 was discontinued.

Service could change again next year

The situation between January and June 2027 has not yet been fully settled. According to PID, the final arrangement will depend in part on discussions between the incoming leaderships of Prague 3 and Prague 7.

Maintaining the additional tram service in Holešovice during that period could require limited reductions elsewhere in Prague 3. Another option would be to temporarily return to the existing arrangement using combined tram lines 6 and 34.

PID has warned that permanently combining lines 5 and 6 could also create delays at both ends of the route. Such a change could affect passengers travelling through Prague 2 and Prague 5, even though it would provide the direct connection sought by Prague 7.

World.title: “Ivan, Go Home!” Rally to Take Place Outside Russian Embassy in Prague
World.content:
A Czech-Ukrainian rally will take place outside the Russian Embassy in Prague on August 20 to mark the 58th anniversary of the Soviet-led invasion of Czechoslovakia.

The event, titled “Ivan, Go Home!”, is scheduled to begin at 6 p.m. on Thursday, August 20, at Boris Němcova Square in Prague 6.

The rally comes one day before the anniversary of the night of August 20-21, 1968, when troops from five Warsaw Pact countries entered Czechoslovakia to crush the Prague Spring reform movement.



The invasion brought an end to the country’s attempt to pursue a more liberal form of socialism and was followed by two decades of political repression and Soviet military presence.

The event is being organized jointly by People in Need (Člověk v tísni), Memory of the People (Paměť národa), Million Moments for Democracy (Milion chvilek pro demokracii), and the European Congress of Ukrainians.

Organizers say the rally will connect the historical experience of the Soviet occupation with Russia’s ongoing war against Ukraine.

Participants will gather to remember those killed or persecuted following the 1968 invasion and the people who lived under the communist regime that followed. The organizers also plan to express support for Ukraine and draw attention to what they describe as the continuing use of imperial violence by Russia.

The choice of the rally’s name refers to one of the best-known slogans associated with the 1968 invasion. “Ivan, go home!” appeared on posters, walls, buildings and military vehicles as Czechoslovaks protested against the foreign troops occupying the country.

The invasion halted those reforms. Soviet troops remained in Czechoslovakia until the end of the communist era, while the subsequent period of “normalization” brought censorship, political purges and restrictions on civil liberties.

World.title: World of Warcraft Film Ibelin to Shoot in Prague
World.content:
Production of Ibelin, a new film based on the life of Norwegian World of Warcraft player Mats Steen, is moving to Prague this summer.

Filming is expected to take place at Barrandov Studios from early August through early October, following the production’s spring shoot in Norway.

The film is not connected to the 2016 Hollywood movie Warcraft. Instead, it tells the real-life story of Steen, who lived with Duchenne muscular dystrophy and built friendships, relationships and a social life inside the online world of World of Warcraft.



The Prague production is reportedly seeking extras for roles including blacksmiths, guards and innkeepers. The casting suggests that parts of the film set in the game’s fictional world could be filmed in the Czech Republic. The producers have not yet officially confirmed which scenes will be shot in Prague.

Charlie Plummer leads the cast

American actor Charlie Plummer will portray Mats Steen. Toni Collette and Stephen Graham will play his parents, while the supporting cast includes Bill Nighy, Isabela Merced, Maisy Stella, John Bradley and Ivanna Sakhno.

The film will be directed by Norwegian filmmaker Morten Tyldum, whose credits include The Imitation Game and the science-fiction film Passengers.

At the center of the story is the difference between Steen’s increasingly restricted physical existence and the freedom he experienced online. His character, known in World of Warcraft as Ibelin, became an important figure to people he met through the game.

One of Norway’s largest film projects

The Prague shoot is part of an international production with a reported budget of CZK 1 billion.

According to the Norwegian Film Institute, the project received 20 million Norwegian kroner in production support.

Ibelin is being produced by Vendôme Pictures, Pathé and Neby-Tyldum as an international co-production. The Norwegian Film Institute describes it as an English-language drama with a planned running time of around two hours.

The film is being developed for theatrical release, with its premiere currently expected in the third quarter of 2027.

World.title: GALLERY: Time Capsule Buried Beneath Prague’s Wenceslas Square Tramline
World.content:
A time capsule containing different items, newspapers and messages documenting life in 2026 has been buried beneath Prague’s reconstructed Wenceslas Square.

The capsule was placed on Wednesday, August 5, near the statue of St. Wenceslas as work continues on the upper section of the square.

The Prague New Town Association, which is involved in activities around the statue and the surrounding area, organised the ceremony.

The date was not originally chosen for its historical significance. Construction work ultimately determined both the day and the location of the burial. But the association later discovered that August 5 also marks the 60th anniversary of the release of the Beatles’ Revolver album.

“We were wondering what made August 5 go down in history. Then we found out that it was 60 years ago that the Beatles released their famous album Revolver. So now we are leaving a message here for future generations,” said Monika Vlková, the association’s executive director.



The box, measuring 60 by 40 by 23.5 centimetres and weighing about eight kilograms, was then taken to a prepared pit beside the statue. Workers had excavated the hole to a depth of around 1.7 metres, where the capsule was placed before the site was covered.

The container had been wrapped in transparent protective film, as had its contents.

The collection includes coins, newspapers published during the first week of August 2026, T-shirts, badges and written messages. It also contains proposals submitted by architects during the competition for the redesign of Wenceslas Square.

The box reportedly also holds a hammer and a beer glass.

The objects are accompanied by a 20-page report describing everyday life in the Czech capital in 2026. The capsule also contains USB drives with digital material documenting the period of the Covid-19 pandemic and its effects on life in central Prague.

The capsule is intended to remain underground for decades. The association estimates that Wenceslas Square could undergo another major reconstruction in roughly 50 years, although nobody can predict when the next intervention will actually take place.

World.title: Czechia Tightens Temporary Protection Rules for Ukrainian Men Aged 23 to 60
World.content:
New rules affecting Ukrainian men seeking temporary protection in the Czech Republic will take effect on August 5, 2026.

Under the changes, men aged 23 to 60 applying for temporary protection will have to demonstrate that they are exempt from military service in Ukraine.

The requirement will apply to new applications and certain other applications for protection, but not to people who already hold valid temporary protection.



The Czech Interior Ministry says the new rules follow an EU Council decision published in the Official Journal of the European Union on August 4. The decision also extends temporary protection for people fleeing Russia’s war in Ukraine until March 31, 2028.

For applicants aged 23 to 60, military registration documents will be checked as part of the application process. Applicants will use Ukraine’s Reserv+ system to demonstrate their military status, with the electronic military registration document showing whether they are exempt from military service.

The rules are different for younger applicants. People aged 18 to 22 will only need to demonstrate that they are registered in the Reserv+ system.

The new requirement concerns people applying for temporary protection for the first time, as well as repeat applications and applications connected with family reunification. It does not apply to people who already have valid temporary protection.

The military-service requirement will also not be introduced as part of the regular extension process. Ukrainians whose temporary protection is already valid will therefore not have to provide this additional documentation when extending their status through March 2028.

Interior Minister Lubomír Metnar said the Czech government had pushed for stricter conditions for new applicants. According to the ministry, the change is expected to reduce the number of new arrivals and ease pressure on public services, including health care and social security.

World.title: Filming of American Spy Series to Bring Restrictions to Prague 7
World.content:
Filming for the American series Birdwatcher will take place at the Prague 7 tax office on Kapitána Jaroše Embankment from August 8 to 24, bringing temporary restrictions to the area.

The production will use the tax office building at Kapitána Jaroše Embankment 1000/7, while part of the sidewalk outside the building will be closed to accommodate filming equipment.

The restrictions will not affect the normal operation of the tax office.



Drivers should also expect temporary parking restrictions on nearby Na Ovčinách Street. Vehicles will still be allowed to pass through the street, but parking will be prohibited during the designated filming periods.

The restrictions will not be in force continuously throughout the filming period. They will apply only on specific dates, with Prague 7 publishing a map showing the affected areas and individual dates on its website.

Prague has become a major filming location

Birdwatcher is an American spy fantasy series set during the Cold War. The production is being led by Legendary and Apple TV, with Andy Goddard directing. Wyatt Russell plays the lead role.

The story follows Colonel Lee Shaw as he embarks on a covert mission behind enemy lines to prevent the Soviet Union from unleashing a new Titan capable of devastating the United States and altering the balance of the Cold War.

The series is set in the 20th century against the backdrop of the Cold War, and parts of the production are being filmed in Prague.

Czech production company Stillking Films is handling the local production. The company has previously worked on major international productions filmed in the Czech capital, including The Gray Man.

World.title: Hungary’s next president: PM Magyar’s four frontrunners – or will a fifth candidate triumph?
World.content:
Hungary is due to elect its next president on Tuesday, 11 August, with the ceremonial oath of office already listed on Parliament’s official agenda. Before then, the governing Tisza Party’s parliamentary group is expected to decide on Saturday whom it will nominate for the largely ceremonial post. At present, several names are in contention.

No official candidate has yet been announced. However, recent political consultations and public statements have brought four figures to the fore: András Baka, former president of the Supreme Court; Ágnes Forsthoffer, the acting head of state; Ignác Romsics, the distinguished historian; and Botond Fülöp, the lawyer better known as the “Vidéki Prókátor”, or Rural Advocate.

With András Baka (c). Photo: Facebook/Péter Magyar

Read our full Substack analysis for detailed profiles of the four leading contenders, an examination of Fidesz’s faltering strategy, and our view that one name is conspicuously absent from this shortlist.

World.title: Power and water concerns at Sziget Festival? Founder reveals what’s really going on
World.content:
Sziget Festival founder Károly Gerendai has vowed that there will be no power or water shortages at this year’s event.

Lots of guests expected at this year’s Sziget Festival

Gerendai told MTI on Friday that daily attendance of 60,000-70,000 would be reassuring, and the festival would not need to use its backup diesel generators, which have a larger environmental footprint. Whereas the festival has enough generators to cover 95 percent of its power needs, recent government announcements suggest no additional self-imposed restrictions from the country’s grid will be required, he added.

How the number of festivalgoers changed since the start of the Sziget Festival. The peak was years ago. Photo: MTI

To mitigate water supply issues, organisers have installed sprinkler systems at their own expense and prepared water tanks in case of low pressure in the main system. They have also laid down more walkway panels than in previous years to reduce dust on the main stage area, he noted.

Gerendai said ticket sales have slowed in the past week or two, likely due to the “mood of catastrophe” caused by extreme heat and energy restrictions. However, he said a sell-out crowd was unlikely, and 60,000-70,000 punters a day would be preferable to the permitted 95,000 in the current dry and dusty conditions.

Major international performers coming to Sziget Festival 2026

The official programme runs from 11 to 16 August on Óbuda Island (Hajógyári Island), with headliners including Twenty One Pilots, Florence + The Machine, Bring Me The Horizon, Skrillex, Zara Larsson, and Lewis Capaldi. Two Hungarian acts, Sisi and Carson Coma, will also perform on the main stage.

Other announced performers include Ashnikko, Biffy Clyro, Parcels, Underworld, Wolf Alice, Richie Hawtin, Dom Dolla, Sara Landry and Hungarian rapper Beton.Hofi. Organisers say the complete festival will feature more than 600 music, theatre, circus, dance, workshop and sporting programmes.

If you missed: MÁV railway group preparing with extra services for the Sziget Festival – details

A special Day Zero will also be held on 10 August, reviving a feature familiar from earlier editions of Sziget. Faithless, Morcheeba and Goran Bregović and his Wedding and Funeral Orchestra will return to evoke some of the festival’s most memorable previous decades.

Sziget Festival in Hungarian ownership again

In November 2025, the festival left Superstruct and returned to the hands of its founder, Károly Gerendai, and the existing management team. Gerendai rejoined Sziget after an eight-year absence, while chief executive Tamás Kádár remained in his position.

The new owners have placed renewed emphasis on Sziget’s relationship with Budapest, its cultural diversity and its identity as an independent festival. Sziget City is one of the clearest signs of that strategy: an attempt to ensure that international visitors discover not only the stages of the Island of Freedom, but also the neighbourhoods, clubs and cultural communities that shape Budapest throughout the year.

Sziget Festival 2026 wristband holders offered discounts across Budapest!

World.title: Soviet shell, cannonball and German Panzerfaust warheads found near Budapest university
World.content:
Hungarian Army bomb-disposal experts removed explosives from the Danube embankments near the Raoul Wallenberg Holocaust Memorial Park and the Budapest University of Technology early on Friday, the armed forces’ bomb-disposal unit said.

Earlier reports said a Soviet 203mm concrete-piercing shell from the Second World War and a cannonball believed to date from the 19th century had been found near the Raoul Wallenberg embankment. A German Second World War ammunition container discovered near the university held eight Panzerfaust launching tubes, their Faustpatrone warheads and detonators, MTI wrote.

The unit said the Soviet shell was too corroded to be defused on site. It was therefore taken under police escort to a designated demolition area, where it will be destroyed along with the other explosives.For the operation, Szabadság Bridge and the embankments, university buildings and a petrol station on the Buda side were temporarily closed early on Friday. Police lifted the restrictions and reopened the roads once the operation had been completed.

World.title: Plunging inflation in Hungary: analysts surprised, but how long can the favourable trend last?
World.content:
In recent years, we had grown used to inflation figures bringing unpleasant news: rising prices, soaring food bills or ever more expensive fuel. For the first time in a long while, however, Hungary’s inflation rate can be discussed in a positive context, having fallen to a ten-year low. Experts explain what lies behind the plunge – and what may be in store over the coming months and year.

Even experts surprised by low inflation

The public’s experience of prices in recent years could be summed up as follows: although everyone was earning more in nominal terms – something Orbán’s governments were only too keen to boast about – our money somehow bought less and less. High wage growth was accompanied by even higher price rises, with some sectors becoming prohibitively expensive. The property market alone is enough to illustrate the point.

Property prices in Hungary rose between 235-240% between 2016 and 2026. The growth is even bigger in Budapest. Photo: depositphotos.com

For the first time in many years, shoppers may now be finding that their money goes further in certain cases. One reason is that Hungary’s inflation rate has fallen to a ten-year low – a development that also caught Hungarian experts by surprise. Annual inflation stood at just 1.2 per cent in July, well below the 1.5 per cent previously forecast. According to portfolio.hu, Hungary has not seen inflation this low since 2016. Analysts had expected annual inflation of 1.5 per cent in July, following figures of 1.7 per cent in June, 1.8 per cent in May and 2.1 per cent in April.

Photo: MTI

The economic news website attributed the sharp slowdown in inflation to three factors:

favourable trends in food prices; calmer conditions in fuel markets; a strong forint.

Reasons for concern remain

The newspaper also pointed out that core inflation rose by 0.3 per cent, which is not low. Moreover, inflation plunged because of factors beyond the authorities’ control – external forces that could change in the future.

Services have also become significantly more expensive. Major telecommunications and financial-services providers have now raised their prices after exercising “restraint” before the election, at the request of the previous government. According to portfolio.hu, this caused a “smaller price shock” across the services sector.

The central bank could cut interest rates further in the future, the outlet said. The only reasons for caution, at most, would be turbulent geopolitical developments and volatility in energy markets.

What experts expect next

Gábor Regős, chief economist at Gránit Fund Management, said that the strong forint, low inflation expectations and rising business confidence had combined to create an environment of subdued inflation, MTI reports. The National Bank of Hungary could therefore cut its base rate to 5 per cent in September, even if the forint continues to weaken.

Orsolya Nyeste, Erste Bank’s chief macroeconomic analyst, said July’s figure could prove to be the annual low. Inflation may edge up from August onwards, but is expected to remain below the central bank’s 3 per cent target.

Photo: Daily News Hungary

Dávid Németh, chief analyst at K&H Bank, emphasised that rising gross wages had pushed up the cost of services. He expects inflation to remain below 2 per cent for the rest of the year, with the annual average likely to come in at around 1.8 per cent.

If you missed: Hungary’s central bank governor sends a strong message about the country’s financial position

Dániel Molnár, chief analyst at the GFÜ Centre for Economic Analysis, said the poor harvest caused by drought could feed through into food prices. The current energy crisis, meanwhile, is forcing companies to reassess how they calculate their energy costs. Inflation is likely to accelerate next year, he predicted, reaching around 3 per cent.

Record fall in food prices

The National Trade Association highlighted a 4.4 per cent fall in food prices, which is almost certainly a record. It said the decline was not the result of the margin cap, but of the favourable exchange rate of the forint and positive domestic and international market trends. These had more than offset the increase resulting from rising energy costs.

World.title: What could he have found? Georgian authorities send home Hungarian journalist who criticised Orbán-friendly government
World.content:
The Hungarian journalist who has reported extensively on the Georgian Dream government’s excesses – and its ever-closer ties to the Orbán administration and Moscow – has been effectively expelled from the Caucasian country. Local authorities cite irregularities in his residence permit; back home, newspapers suggest he may have stumbled upon something awkward in the nexus between the Orbán system and the Georgian ruling party, which is cultivating increasingly warm relations with Russia.

Detained, then sent home

László Róbert Mézes, a Hungarian journalist who has lived in the country for years and regularly filed reports for Magyar Hang on the country’s political crisis, anti-government protests and Georgian Dream’s grip on power, was taken into custody in Tbilisi before being deported. The Georgian Interior Ministry said Mézes was in the country “without legal grounds” and had exceeded the permitted period of stay, invoking a provision of the aliens’ law that allows detention where there is a risk of absconding. His lawyer maintained that his client’s stay was lawful. Mézes ultimately left the country at his own expense, escorted to the airport by migration officials.

Mézes leaves Georgia – at his own expense:

The case is notable not least because Mézes is no ordinary Hungarian correspondent based in Georgia: he has been an outspoken critic of Georgian Dream. For Magyar Hang, reporting from Tbilisi, he wrote repeatedly on the so-called “foreign agents” law – a near word‑for‑word translation of the Russian model – and on the suffocation of civil society and independent media, the blocking of voting rights for the diaspora (some one million of Georgia’s five million citizens, whose remittances underpin the economy), the imprisonment of opposition politicians and critical journalists, and the near‑constant street protests. He also reported for Magyar Hang that Prime Ministers Orbán and Fico were obstructing EU moves towards targeted sanctions against Georgian political leaders.

On the 612th day of protests following the 2024 election, he published these photographs last Saturday:

Beaten in Tbilisi – and he told Orbán what he thought

In October 2024, during Viktor Orbán’s visit to Tbilisi, Mézes shouted at the Hungarian Prime Minister in Hungarian that he had come to legitimise “stolen elections”, and asked whether he was proud that Georgian Dream was copying Fidesz. Orbán, alone among EU leaders, congratulated the victors almost immediately after the poll, while the rest of the EU (save Slovakia), the European Parliament, the Georgian President and the opposition all rejected the result. Mézes’s situation deteriorated further in September 2025: while working as a journalist at an anti-government demonstration, he was attacked by Georgian Dream activists outside the party headquarters. He was beaten, required stitches to his face and sustained hand injuries; Georgian authorities later formally recognised him as a victim.

In this post, featuring a photograph with Péter Magyar, he informed his Georgian followers that Péter Magyar would be the next Prime Minister:

A pro‑Russian turn

Although the Caucasian country was at war with Russia in 2008 over South Ossetia and Abkhazia – territories occupied by Moscow and subsequently recognised as independent states – the Georgian Dream party has lately been cultivating conspicuously pragmatic relations with Putin’s Russia. The “foreign agents” law, passed in 2024 on the Russian model, targeted critical NGOs and media outlets; in November 2024 the government announced it would not commence EU accession talks until 2028. Tbilisi has not joined sanctions against Russia and continues to trade with Moscow, even though diplomatic relations have never been restored since the 2008 war.

If you missed: Georgian-Israeli businessman linked to former propaganda minister Rogán allegedly sought to gain access to key aide of PM Péter Magyar

Good relations to be maintained, PM Péter Magyar pledges

Péter Magyar, Hungary’s prime minister-elect, said at a press conference shortly after the 12 April election that he would maintain good relations with Georgia. Asked by a reporter from the pro-government Georgian broadcaster Rustavi 2, Magyar said that the fact Viktor Orbán’s government had forged strong ties with a country in the Balkans – or anywhere else – did not mean Hungary would have a less close relationship with that country.

“But if Hungary has bad relations with a country, we will improve them, because it is in our shared interest to work together, to co-operate and to prosper together,” he added, according to civil.ge. Magyar also said he was open to visiting Tbilisi and looked forward to working with the Georgian government.

“But we are not going to interfere in the internal affairs of other countries. We will not try to influence elections in your country, North Macedonia or anywhere else. That’s not our style, and it is not the job of any European government. Everyone is elected to support and represent the electorate of their own country,” he said.

The media outlet noted that Irakli Kobakhidze, Georgia’s prime minister, had visited Hungary on 21 March to address CPAC Budapest and express his support for Mr Orbán. On 13 April, following the Tisza party’s victory in Hungary’s general election, the Georgian Government congratulated Mr Magyar and his party, while thanking Orbán for his “outstanding and steadfast support for Georgia’s national interests and the Georgian people over the years”.

World.title: PM Magyar shared good news about voluntary consumption cuts as heat records were broken again

There will be no need for voluntary consumption cuts from Friday, PM Péter Magyar announced on his Facebook page on Thursday evening.

Magyar said: “Together, we did it, and we protected our country’s energy security. Thank you, Hungary!” He added that the Defence Council’s decisions will be announced on Friday morning.

Multiple heat records, along with a wind-speed record, were broken on Thursday, the weather service HungaroMet said on Facebook, citing preliminary data. The new national daytime heat record was recorded in Kiskunfélegyháza, where the temperature reached 41.8 degrees Celsius, surpassing the previous record of 40.2 C set in Orosháza in 1905.

Meanwhile, a thunderstorm also led to a new daily wind-speed record in Szolnok, where a gust of 113kmh was recorded. The previous daily wind record was 107kmh in Körösladány in 2010.

World.title: PM Magyar: Orbán knew that Hungary’s energy system was on the brink of collapse, but failed to act
World.content:
Prime Minister Péter Magyar on Thursday accused the former prime minister, Viktor Orbán, of knowing that Hungary’s energy system was on the brink of collapse but failing to act.

Hungary could not provide as much electricity as Orbán promised

In a video posted on Facebook, Magyar quoted a 2022 bill submitted by the previous government, which stated that Hungary’s energy supply was on the edge of a precipice because the government had burdened the system with a “full Paks-worth” of electricity demand to benefit major investors, MTI wrote.

“In other words, they promised more electricity to major industrial players, often battery investment projects, than the domestic energy system could safely provide,” the prime minister said. Magyar said Hungary needed “an energy and water revolution”, including “unprecedented development” of energy storage capacities and the electricity grid.

Negative prices for solar energy

Magyar noted that while Hungary has over 8,800MW of solar capacity, its energy storage capacity is only 980MW, meaning the country can produce roughly nine times more energy from the sun than its storage facilities can absorb at any given moment. As a result, Hungary often produces surplus energy during sunny periods, which it can only sell at minimal or even negative prices, yet it struggles to store enough for night-time or cloudier conditions, he explained.

Despite this, he said, the Orbán government had consistently removed requirements for storage capacity development from regulations and subsidy programmes for industrial and residential solar projects. He vowed that the current government would develop energy storage capacity to reduce Hungary’s import dependence.

Magyar also blamed the previous government for the underdevelopment of the electricity grid. He said that on Friday, the government will announce the results of a nearly 600 billion forint (EUR 1.7bn) EU-funded tender to develop the electricity grid, enabling the construction of new power lines, substations and higher-capacity transformers. “Hungary’s energy will be safer, cheaper and increasingly domestic,” he said.

If you missed – Danube water crisis: hotel ships and cargo vessels stranded in Hungary

Water and energy crises almost over

Referring to the current heatwave and drought, which has led to a reduction in output of the Paks plant, the prime minister noted that major industrial consumers are still expected to voluntarily reduce energy consumption, and he thanked the public for avoiding or rescheduling electricity use between 5pm and 10pm.

Photo: Anadolu/Robert Nemeti

Magyar added that the Danube’s water level at Paks has risen by 11cm since Sunday, and rain is currently falling in the Austrian catchment areas. However, this will likely not be enough to fully restore Hungary’s nuclear power plant, and a new period of dry, hot weather is expected next week, meaning “we will have to count every centimetre again,” he said.

World.title: Romanian shipyard delivers hull of largest cable-laying ship in Japan
World.content:
The VARD shipyard in Tulcea, eastern Romania, has completed the construction of the hull of “Discovery,” the largest vessel intended for the installation of submarine cables and the first such project delivered by the VARD group for the Japanese market.

The ship, valued at over USD 200 million, will have an important role in the development of infrastructure for offshore wind energy and the transport of electric energy through submarine cables.

The construction of the vessel’s hull was carried out in Romania, at the VARD shipyards in Tulcea and Brăila, and after launching, it was towed to the VARD Langsten shipyard in Norway, where the specialized equipment was installed, and the final tests were carried out before delivery. The vessel was officially handed over to the Japanese company Toyo Construction at the end of June and is currently heading to Japan, where it will be based in the port of Ishikari Bay.

“Discovery” was designed to meet the specific conditions in Japan, where the water depth increases rapidly near the coast. The vessel can operate both in shallow waters and offshore, where future floating wind farms will be installed.

The vessel is approximately 151 meters long, 28 meters wide, and can transport up to 9,000 tons of submarine cables, distributed in two carousels with capacities of 4,000 and 5,000 tons.

On board, the ship has a main crane with a lifting capacity of 400 tons and an auxiliary crane of 100 tons. The vessel is also equipped with a dynamic positioning system, a heliport and equipment for the operation of remotely operated underwater vehicles.

In addition to the installation of submarine cables, “Discovery” can also be used for offshore construction works, including the installation of foundations for wind turbines and anchoring operations for floating turbines.

The vessel is equipped with a hybrid propulsion system, in which diesel engines are used to produce electric energy, while propulsion is provided by electric motors. The system includes batteries and the possibility of shore power supply during stationing, in order to reduce fuel consumption and emissions. Up to 90 crew members and technicians can work on board.

The Japanese government has set the rapid expansion of offshore wind energy capacities as an objective in the coming period, and this vessel will be used for the installation of the submarine electric cables necessary to connect the new farms to the energy grid.

For VARD, the project marks the first delivery to the Japanese market in the segment of specialized vessels for the offshore wind industry. In recent years, the VARD Tulcea shipyard has specialized in the construction of the hulls of some of the most complex vessels intended for the offshore industry, including vessels for the installation of submarine cables and for the development of offshore wind energy projects.

Several of the most advanced vessels of this type currently used worldwide were built in Romania and subsequently equipped at the VARD group’s shipyards in Norway.

World.title: Romania’s eMAG to come under sole control of Naspers after EU approval
World.content:
The European Commission has approved, under the EU Merger Regulation, the acquisition of sole control over Dante International of Romania by South African investment fund Naspers Limited.

"The Commission concluded that the notified operation does not raise competition concerns, as the companies are not active on the same markets or on markets that are in a vertical relationship, and the impact on the market structure is limited. The transaction was examined under the simplified merger control procedure," the EC stated in a press release.

Last month, businessman Iulian Stanciu announced the sale of his stake in the eMAG Group to global consumer internet and technology investment group Prosus, 17 years after taking over the company and 14 years after signing the partnership with Naspers, the owner of Prosus.

After the sale, eMAG will continue its development and extensive investment plans, with RON 1.2 billion budgeted in this fiscal year alone for technology, logistics and financial services, with the support of Prosus and an experienced management team, company representatives stated. They also noted the regional growth potential of e-commerce, which remains significant, with growth rates of up to three times in the coming years, compared to the current penetration rate of 11-12% of total retail.

"The investments will be directed predominantly toward logistics and delivery infrastructure, AI and financial services, consolidating the foundation for a strong digital economy in the region. I want to thank Iulian for his dedication, vision, and for keeping us focused on the customer and on continuous personal development," said at that time Tudor Manea, CEO of eMAG Group, cited by News.ro.

At group level, eMAG recorded in fiscal year 2025 a turnover of RON 11.4 billion (USD 2.64 billion), up 11% compared with the previous financial year. The eMAG Group portfolio includes the eMAG brand, the Fashion Days online store, Romania’s 100% online hypermarket Freshful, the IT and electronics specialist store PC Garage, the Romanian national and international express courier company Sameday, the Depanero repair workshop, the most relevant recommerce platform in South-Eastern Europe Flip, as well as the financial services company HeyBlu.

World.title: Eurostat: Romania allocated only EUR 18.8 per inhabitant to R&D in 2025, lower than in 2015
World.content:
European governments allocated an estimated EUR 130.2 billion, or 0.69% of their combined GDP, to research and development in 2025, according to a Eurostat analysis published on Friday, August 7.

The sum represents an increase of 2.4% compared to 2024 (EUR 127.14 billion) and an increase of 60.5% compared to 2015 (EUR 81.13 billion).

In 2025, on average, government budget allocations for research and development at EU level amounted to EUR 288.9 per inhabitant, an increase of 57.7% compared to 2015 (EUR 183.2 per inhabitant). Luxembourg (EUR 917.2 per inhabitant) recorded the highest budget allocations for research and development per capita among the EU member countries. It was followed by Denmark (EUR 627.1) and Germany (EUR 553.5).

At the opposite end, the lowest values were recorded in Romania (EUR 18.8), Hungary (EUR 57.4) and Malta (EUR 73.7). Moreover, compared to 2015, Romania (-9.6%) was the only EU country that recorded a decrease in budget allocations for research and development expressed in euros per inhabitant, from EUR 20.8 in 2015 to EUR 18.8 in 2025.

The other EU countries recorded increases ranging from +14.7% in Sweden (from EUR 363.4 per inhabitant in 2015 to EUR 416.7 in 2025) to +495.5% in Bulgaria (from EUR 15.5 to EUR 92.3).

As regards the distribution according to socio-economic objectives, 37.3% of the amount was allocated to the general advancement of knowledge, financed mainly through a global public grant known as public general university funds, used by public higher education institutions to support their activities. In addition, 18.4% of R&D funds were allocated to the general advancement of knowledge from sources other than the general university funds, 9.5% to industrial production and technology, 6.7% to health, and 5.8% to defense.

World.title: EIB lends EUR 100 million to BRD Sogelease to increase financing for businesses in Romania
World.content:
The European Investment Bank (EIB) is lending EUR 100 million to the leasing subsidiary of BRD Groupe Société Générale to expand financing for businesses in Romania.

The goal is to facilitate financing for Romanian SMEs and Mid-Caps, which face greater hurdles in accessing long-term funding than their counterparts in many other European Union countries, EIB said.

The operation will enable BRD Sogelease to provide funding to Romanian companies seeking business expansion, productivity improvements and sustainable development.

Of the total loan, 15% is earmarked for green projects such as energy efficiency, renewable energy and sustainable transport.

Around 80% of the EIB loan is projected to be deployed in less-developed areas known in the EU as “cohesion regions.”

The new operation builds on previous EIB loans to BRD Sogelease IFN that total EUR 305 million over the past decade.

“In today’s rapidly changing economy, access to finance is a key enabler of competitiveness,” said EIB Vice-President Ioannis Tsakiris. “By partnering with BRD Sogelease, we are mobilizing investment where it matters most: among Romanian entrepreneurs. This financing will help businesses become more resilient, more innovative and better prepared for the opportunities of tomorrow.”

“Our long-standing partnership with the European Investment Bank reflects a shared commitment to supporting the growth and resilience of the Romanian economy. This new financing facility will enable us to provide SMEs and Mid-Caps with enhanced access to long-term funding on attractive terms, helping them invest in expansion, innovation, productivity and sustainable development,” said BRD Sogelease GM Gabriel Mihai.

BRD Sogelease IFN SA is the leasing subsidiary of BRD Groupe Société Générale, one of the leading banks in Romania with total assets of RON 96.3 billion as of June 2026. Established in 2001, BRD Sogelease IFN provides financial lease and other asset-based financial solutions to over 10,000 SME and Small-Cap clients in Romania.

World.title: Platform for foreign workers coming to Romania up and running, authorities say
World.content:
Romania’s Interior Ministry announced on Thursday, August 6, that the platform WorkinRomania.gov.ro is now up and running, simplifying the process of hiring foreign workers.

The platform aims to make it easier for immigrant workers to enter the domestic labor market. Among its benefits is the facilitation of the relationship between the employer and the future employee.

The platform helps both Romanian employers looking for a workforce and aids the state in managing more efficiently the employment of new workers coming from other states. “Less bureaucracy, shorter deadlines and the possibility to track each application in real time,” the Ministry noted, cited by Agerpres.

The services of this platform include: permanent access to one’s own electronic file; the possibility to track each stage of the procedure; automatic notifications regarding requests for additional documents or the adopted solutions; reduction of waiting times; increased transparency of the entire administrative process. The platform also connects future employees with the Trade Register, the Employee Records Register, as well as with IT systems for the checks provided by law.

The platform also centralizes the actions of several Romanian state institutions.

The General Inspectorate for Immigration within the Ministry of Internal Affairs handles the procedures within its competence regarding the regime of foreigners and the right of residence for employment purposes; it analyzes and resolves applications regarding the granting and extension of residence

The right of residence for employment purposes, issues the specific documents and participates in the electronic exchange of data necessary for substantiating administrative decisions.

The National Agency for Employment operationally administers the module intended for the registration and authorization of employers and agencies for the placement of foreigners and configures the workflows related to these procedures;

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs, through the national visa system and the eViza platform, participates in the workflows regarding the granting of long-stay visas for employment;

The National Agency for Fiscal Administration provides the information necessary for the fiscal checks provided by law;

The Ministry of Education and Research, through the National Center for the Recognition and Equivalence of Diplomas, contributes to the verification of qualifications and diplomas, in the cases provided by legislation.

The platform offers useful information for employers, placement agencies and foreign workers, available also in English. Interested persons can find on WorkinRomania.gov.ro all the information they need for creating and validating an account on the platform, the registration and authorization conditions, the necessary documents and the method of using the electronic services available on the platform.

At the same time, users have a support chat service, available both in text and voice format, which provides assistance and guidance in the use of electronic services, in Romanian and other languages.

In terms of security, the program is included in the Ministry’s Services Hub, specially designed to keep personal data safe at the level of each county.

Although Romania set an official quota of around 90,000 newly admitted foreign workers for 2026, employer demand significantly exceeds that ceiling. In some years, requests have reportedly been more than double the approved quota. Still, filling vacancies is only part of the challenge. A large share of newly arrived workers subsequently seek opportunities in other EU member states, where wages, working conditions, and social benefits are often more attractive.

World.title: Thriller starring Nicolas Cage to open this year's horror and fantastic film fest in Biertan
World.content:
The Full Moon Horror and Fantastic Film Festival, presented by the Transilvania International Film Festival, returns to Biertan for its 11th edition, bringing three days and three nights of premieres, cult films and open-air screenings.

The festival opens with the Romanian premiere of The Carpenter’s Son, starring Nicolas Cage. Another highlight of this year’s edition will be the cine-concert Trenul Fantomă, featuring live music by Dubase, preceded by an acoustic performance by Ana Coman and her guitar as part of Full Moon Unplugged.

At Bastion Open Air, the programme kicks off on Friday, August 14, with Nightborn, the new film by Finnish director Hanna Bergholm, known to horror audiences for Hatching. Selected for the competition at the Berlin International Film Festival, the film follows a couple who move into an isolated house in the Finnish woods, where the arrival of their first child awakens a disturbing presence. The evening continues with The Rocky Horror Picture Show, the horror musical that has become one of cinema’s great cult phenomena. The story behind the film will also be explored from behind the scenes in the documentary Strange Journey: The Story of Rocky Horror, screening on Saturday at Cinema Ion Hobana.

On Saturday, Bastion Open Air will screen Her Private Hell, the new film by director Nicolas Winding Refn, as well as the original Dutch version of the thriller The Vanishing. The programme also includes the 1993 American remake, also directed by George Sluizer, giving audiences an opportunity to compare the two versions.

On Sunday, Carrie returns to the Bastion screen. Directed by Brian De Palma and based on Stephen King’s novel, the classic marks 50 years since its release.

On Friday, August 14, Méliès Open Air will host the Romanian premiere of The Carpenter’s Son. Directed by Lotfy Nathan, the supernatural thriller stars Nicolas Cage as Joseph, alongside FKA twigs as Mary and Noah Jupe as their teenage son.

On Saturday, August 15, audiences are invited to the cine-concert Trenul Fantomă. Made in 1933 by Jean Mihail, the first Romanian-language talking film tells the story of travelers forced to spend the night at a railway station believed to be haunted. The film will be screened with live music performed by Dubase.

The Méliès programme concludes on Sunday, August 16, with The Virgin of the Quarry Lake, directed by Laura Casabé. Inspired by the prose of writer Mariana Enríquez, the film blends adolescence, jealousy and black magic against the backdrop of Argentina’s 2001 crisis.

The selection continues at Cinema Karloff and Cinema Ion Hobana, with titles including The Turkish Coffee Table, Gaua, Species, Roqia, Veins, The Uncertainty Principle, Feels Like Home, Anemoneciacs and Transylvania Tapes.

The program also includes Romanian short films, the documentary Strange Journey: The Story of Rocky Horror, and repeat screenings of The Carpenter’s Son, Nightborn and Her Private Hell.

The festival takes place between August 14 and August 16.
