World.title: Past tense, eye on future: Air India hikes pilots’ pay by 8% to 15%
World.content:
Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Air India on Friday hiked pilot salaries by 8% to 15%, with commanders getting the biggest hikes and then the same tapering with rank. Going ahead, first officers or co-pilots will primarily get command upgrade (become captains) in AI Express (which has only single aisles) and then move to AI (which has wide body aircraft too that have higher pay) for a âstrong foundation for progression within the groupâ. The group has tried to do multiple things â make AI Express more attractive for pilots through better pay and address shortage there mainly on the Boeing 737 fleet; check resignations and retain cockpit crew.AI pilots have for years been facing a 40 hour guaranteed pay â meaning they will get minimum for these many hours irrespective of actual flying and flying more will for more pay â while IndiGo has fixed pay for 70 hours. This has been a cause of heartburn among pilots. Under the revised framework while AI will continue to provide guaranteed pay for 40 flying hours but has enhanced flying allowance rates. Flying allowance rates beyond 40 hours have also been increased, aligning compensation with industry benchmarks while rewarding productivity.Now AI is restoring international flights that were slashed post the West Asia crisis and will return to Jan-Feb level by next month.The constraint of Pakistan airspace closure remains for Indian carriers and the longer routes they have to take for flying to and from the west â unlike direct routes taken by foreign carriers â means higher flying time and greater pilot requirement.Now a senior commander flying for about 55 hours in a month will get Rs 8.3 lakh, up from Rs 7.5 lakh at present. And a first officer doing so will get Rs 3.3 lakh, up from just over Rs 3 lakh as of now.While privilege leave has been reduced from 30 to 24, the airline will not be counting mandatory weekly off time pilots get as per regulatory requirement and the new leave structure accounts does not factor that which comes across as a cut in leave, said people in the know. IndiGo may relook at its leave policy too for pilots.Since Tata Group took over AI and AI Express in Jan 2022, the Maharaja has lost over Rs 55,000 crore due to multiple factors. The pilot pay hike announced Friday indicates it is looking at the future and preparing for growth with hundreds of aircraft on order without being bogged down by the tumultuous recent past.âNew career pathways, enhanced compensation and benefits, and improved quality-of-life initiatives support Air India Group's next phase of expansion. At the heart of these initiatives is a clear, structured and transparent career pathway that provides faster command opportunities, long-term progression and access to one of the most significant widebody growth programmes in global aviation,â said an official.Since 2022, AI Group has grown from around 100 aircraft to nearly 300 aircraft and has placed orders for 600 new aircraft, including 80 wide body aircraft. Tatas are investing in capability building, including the establishment of a modern aviation academy in Gurugram with Airbus and Boeing full-flight simulators, and a new flying training school in Amravati, Maharashtra.âAs AI group expands, it is focused on developing and retaining internal talent through a structured progression model across Air India Express and Air India. Pilots across Air India and Air India Express will operate under a common seniority framework, creating an integrated and transparent pathway for career progression across the group. This framework provides greater visibility into future opportunities while ensuring a consistent and structured approach to advancement,â said teh official.Under the new framework, AI Express will serve as âthe primary pathway for pilots seeking command upgrades. This approach is designed to accelerate command opportunities, enable pilots to build command experience earlier in their careers, and create a strong foundation for progression within the Group.âFollowing command experience at AI Express, pilots will have the opportunity to progress to Air India and subsequently pursue widebody flying and command opportunities. âWith 80 additional widebody aircraft on order and scheduled for induction over the coming years, Air India offers pilots a long-term pathway that is unique in the Indian market,â the official said. An additional incentive is being offered to pilots who sign up to support the growing Boeing 737 fleet in Air India Express under which they will receive a fleet allowance.

World.title: India’s first satellite-guided chopper approached launched at HAL airport
World.content:
BENGALURU: HAL Airport in Bengaluru has become the first airport in India to operationalise a satellite-guided helicopter approach procedure, a move expected to improve safety, reduce flight times and enable more reliable all-weather operations.

âThe Required Navigation Performance Category H (RNP CAT H) approach, developed by the Airports Authority of India (AAI), is designed exclusively for helicopters. The procedure was validated through flight trials by HAL test pilots and approved by the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA),â HAL said Friday.

The new approach, it added, enables helicopters to fly highly accurate, optimised flight paths using satellite-based navigation, allowing them to safely negotiate terrain and urban obstacles while operating in adverse weather conditions.

According to HAL, the procedure cuts the approach time to HAL Airport from around 12 minutes to about 4 minutes.

âThe operationalisation of Indiaâs first RNP CAT H helicopter approach is a significant milestone for the countryâs aviation ecosystem. This capability enhances the safety, efficiency and accessibility of helicopter operations and establishes a benchmark for similar procedures to be implemented at airports across the country,â HAL chairman and managing director Ravi K said.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines





Besides improving safety, the system is expected to enhance operational efficiency and airspace capacity by allowing smoother integration of helicopter and fixed-wing aircraft movements. It also reduces the noise footprint over urban areas by enabling more precise flight paths.

The faster approach routes are expected to benefit time-critical operations such as air ambulance services and search-and-rescue missions. HAL Airport, which handles nearly 50 helicopter movements every day, is one of the countryâs busiest helicopter hubs. The introduction of the RNP CAT H procedure addresses a long-standing gap in Indiaâs aviation infrastructure and could serve as a model for similar helicopter navigation procedures at other airports.

World.title: 'Why fear eggs in politics?' SC tells Mauha freedom fighter took bullets to chest
World.content:
NEW DELHI: "You are a member of Parliament. Having taken the plunge into politics, you fear eggs? When our freedom fighters have taken bullets on their chest?" the

remarked on Friday while refusing to entertain

(TMC) MP

's plea against a Calcutta high court order directing her to appear before police in connection with a hate speech case.

A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu said it was not inclined to interfere with the high court's direction requiring the Krishnanagar MP to join the investigation.

Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, appearing for Moitra, argued that she should be allowed to appear before the investigating officer virtually as she was entitled to do so under the law.

"The requirement as per the police's notice is to be at the police station in my own constituency.

Last time I went there two things happened. First there were threats that eggs will be thrown etc. and second time eggs were actually thrown," he submitted.

The bench, however, was unconvinced and orally observed, "You are a member of Parliament. Having taken the plunge into politics, you fear eggs?

"When our freedom fighters have taken bullets on their chest? These are applications that should not come before this court at all," it added, according to news agency PTI.





With the bench indicating that it would not grant relief, Moitra's counsel withdrew the petition, following which it was dismissed as withdrawn.

The plea challenged a July 21 order of the Calcutta High Court, which had granted Moitra interim protection from coercive action until October 5 in the hate speech case, while directing her to cooperate with the investigation.

The MP has claimed the case registered at Hogolberia Police Station in Nadia district is based on fabricated allegations.

She had sought the quashing of the proceedings and protection from any coercive action by the police.

Justice Saugata Bhattacharyya of the Calcutta high court had directed Moitra to appear before the investigating officer on August 14 for questioning and ordered that no coercive steps be taken against her until October 5, subject to her complying with the investigation.

World.title: Astrobase unveils 800kN rocket engine, eyes reusability
World.content:
BENGALURU: Space start-up Astrobase Space Technologies Friday unveiled what it described as Indiaâs first privately built â800kN Full-Flow Staged Combustion (FFSC) liquid oxygen-methane rocket engine, named âEverestââ, as it seeks to develop reusable launch systems and expand domestic launch infrastructure.

The Bengaluru-based company said the engine is designed for medium-lift launch vehicles and forms part of its long-term plan to build an integrated launch ecosystem covering propulsion, manufacturing, testing and launch operations. The next major milestone for the programme will be a full-engine hot-fire test, followed by vehicle integration and orbital launch development.

According to the company: âEverest uses the full-flow staged combustion cycle, one of the most complex rocket engine architectures, and is powered by liquid oxygen and methane.

The engine has been designed for reusability and offers 800 kN of thrust, a specific impulse of around 340 seconds and a throttle range of 50% to 110%.â

The company said it plans to manufacture up to 50 engines annually once its facilities are fully operational, with the capability to hot-fire about one engine every week. It aims to test around 20 engines before attempting its first orbital mission.

Its first phase of expansion is intended to support about 100 tonnes of annual launch capacity, with a longer-term goal of exceeding 1,000 tonnes through a higher launch cadence.





It also said it was âworking towards a launch-on-demand capability that could enable a dedicated mission within 15 days of an urgent national requirement. These targets are yet to be demonstratedâ.

Astrobase co-founder Neeraj Khandelwal said the engine was intended to establish an industrial capability rather than serve only as a technology demonstrator, adding that India would require indigenous high-thrust propulsion systems as satellite launches increase globally.

IN-SPACe director (technical) Rajeev Jyoti said Astrobase was among the recipients of IN-SPACeâs Technology Adoption Fund, which is supporting development of the 800 kN engine. He said the programme, as it progresses through development and testing, could contribute to Indiaâs launch capability and create new opportunities in the global space economy.

Founded in 2024, Astrobase is developing propulsion systems, test infrastructure and reusable launch technologies from its Bengaluru base.

World.title: 'Govt stealing money, destroying lives': Rahul Gandhi vows campaign against E20
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha

on Friday said Congress will soon take up the issue of the Centre's E20 ethanol-blended fuel programme.

In a social media post on X, Rahul shared a video and accused the government of "stealing directly out of people's pockets".

"This E20 issue is a very serious matter. Usually, we say, 'Daal mein kuch kaala hai.' But here, the whole daal is black," the Congress leader said.

"Brothers and sisters, this is a matter of priorities. In any campaign, we have to decide the order in which issues are taken up. The problem right now is that there is so much corruption that there is a long list of issues we have to prioritise. But don't worry. We will take up the E20 issue in a big way because it is damaging people's cars and scooters and their lives and is, quite literally, stealing money directly out of their pockets," he added.

The remarks came days after Congress alleged that the Centre's push for E20 petrol had increased fuel costs for consumers while primarily benefiting ethanol producers, claiming motorists were paying more despite assurances of cheaper fuel.

Congress leader Jairam Ramesh said that since March 2025, regular fuel stations across the country had been supplying "practically only E20 petrol".

Referring to earlier statements by Union road transport and highways minister Nitin Gadkari, he said the government had claimed ethanol blending would bring the price of diesel down to Rs 50 per litre and provide a petrol alternative at Rs 55 per litre, but no such reduction had materialised.





"On the contrary, according to an independent analysis, between April 2023 and March 2026, consumers collectively spent an additional approximately Rs 88,234 crore to compensate for the lower mileage from ethanol-blended fuel," he wrote in a post on X.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

He further claimed that the Centre could have reduced the retail price of E20 petrol to offset the lower fuel efficiency and noted that NITI Aayog's Ethanol Roadmap had recommended financial and tax incentives for E10 and E20 fuels to compensate consumers.

"E20 has stripped the average middle-class Indian of options, imposed higher fuel costs on them, and placed an extra burden on the very vehicle they saved for years to buy. If any segment has benefited the most from E20, it is the ethanol producers," Ramesh said.

However, the Centre has maintained that ethanol blending helps reduce India's dependence on imported crude oil and supports farmers by creating demand.

World.title: MEA dismisses foreign concerns over FCRA Bill, says it is an internal matter
World.content:
Breaking its silence over concerns expressed by international stakeholders regarding the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment (FCRA) Bill, 2026, the Ministry of External Affairs on Friday (August 7, 2026) said that “legislative matters concerning India are internal affairs”.

“We have seen the comments. Legislative matters concerning India are our internal affairs to be decided by our Parliament. May I point out that several nations, including the U.S. regulate the flow of foreign funds,” Official Spokesperson of the Ministry of External Affairs, Randhir Jaiswal, said at the bi-weekly press briefing.

Though Mr. Jaiswal did not name anyone, it is inferred that the response came after U.S. Congressman Riley M. Moore slammed the government over the Bill.

Earlier, on August 4, Mr. Moore had described the upcoming amendments to the foreign funding regulation rules as a “clear attack against Christians”. “If this Bill proceeds in this way, it would be a point of major concern in our bilateral relationship with India,” Congressman Riley had said in a social media post.

The Bill is expected to be taken up next week and Home Minister Amit Shah has held a series of consultations with Christian leaders and religious organisations.

World.title: CM for use of AI to augment GST revenue
World.content:
Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy has favoured a comprehensive action plan to leverage Artificial Intelligence in augmenting GST revenue of the State.

The Government would soon unveil a programme based on artificial intelligence that will simplify the system and ensure accelerated growth in the State economy. He wanted officials concerned to take steps to ensure that businesses are not adversely affected with the new system.

The Chief Minister held discussions with noted economist and former chief economic advisor Arvind Subramanian on the planned strategy to enhance revenues in view of the rapid growth in the State economy here on Friday.

The meeting focussed on the reforms that should be ushered in the Commercial Taxes department, Excise and GST in particular. Mr. Subramanian explained about the technologies that help in augmenting revenues and simultaneously promote Ease of Doing Business (EoDB).

He wanted the State Government to focus on arresting revenue leakages in the construction and building equipment through effective coordination among Municipal Administration, Panchayat Raj, Energy, Commercial Taxes and RERA through AI. Officials should ensure that tax estimates pertaining to the construction costs of high rises and contract works were recorded at the time receiving applications for permissions.

In addition, an effective connect between Mee Seva, Aarogyasri and Chief Minister’s Relief Fund would go a long way in providing effective administration.

World.title: Walkathon for safety of healthcare workers
World.content:
The Federation of Obstetrics and Gynaecologists Societies of India (FOGSCI) here on Friday (August 7) held a walkathon here to spread awareness on the importance of ensuring the safety of healthcare professionals.

The walkathon was to mark Abhaya Day, which was instituted after the murder of a doctor at R.G. Kar Medical College Hospital in Kolkata in 2024.

The walkathon saw doctors and nurses carrying placards with slogans against gendered violence and the need for the protection of medical staff.

The Kolkata incident galvanised the medical staff across the country, who demanded a legislation for the protection of the medical fraternity in hospitals that were witnessing violence against health care workers.

World.title: Centre-State government jointly working to provide relief to flood-affected people in Assam: PM
World.content:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday (July 28, 2026) said the Central Government is working closely with the Assam government in providing relief to the flood-affected people of the State.

PM Modi made this statement after meeting with Union Ministers and BJP MPs from Assam in New Delhi at the Parliament House complex. So far this year, 68 people have lost their lives due to the deluge.

"Met MPs from Assam and discussed the prevailing flood situation in various parts of the State. The Centre is working closely with the Assam government in assisting those affected. I pray for everyone's safety and well-being," the Prime Minister said in a post on X.

Met MPs from Assam and discussed the prevailing flood situation in various parts of the state.



The Centre is working closely with the Assam Government in assisting those affected. I pray for everyone's safety and well-being. pic.twitter.com/wFlxc198f8 — Narendra Modi (@narendramodi) July 28, 2026

Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways Sarbananda Sonowal and Minister of State for External Affairs Pabitra Margherita attended the meeting.

According to the Assam State Disaster Management Authority (ASDMA), 4,45,495 people have been impacted in six districts — Sivasagar, Golaghat, Charaideo, Jorhat, Nagaon and Kamrup (Metropolitan) — in the floods.

Altogether 90 relief camps are operational, sheltering 28,695 people due to the floods. Additionally, 94 relief distribution centres were also functional.

Multiple agencies, including the NDRF, SDRF and civil defence personnel, are carrying out the rescue and relief operations, with 67 boats deployed in the affected areas, the bulletin said.

A crop area of 37,139.52 hectares was still submerged and 26,679 animals have been washed away, ASDMA said.

Damage to houses, roads and other infrastructure was reported from various parts of the affected districts, it added.

The flood situation improved on Tuesday (July 28), with no fresh fatalities reported and water levels receding in several districts, officials said.

A Central team visited Sivasagar, one of the worst-hit districts in the current wave of floods, and reviewed the situation in the eastern parts of the State, they said.

World.title: Waterlogging, traffic jams hit Delhi as heavy rain lashes city; red alert issued
World.content:
N

Waterlogged roads, knee-deep flooding in busy markets and bumper-to-bumper traffic marked a rain-soaked Tuesday (July 28, 2026) morning in Delhi as heavy showers battered the city, prompting the weather office to issue a red alert for thunderstorms, lightning and rain over the next few hours.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) forecast a generally cloudy sky with heavy rain for the rest of the day, warning of thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and intense spells of rain across the national capital.

Relentless rain through the morning inundated several parts of the city, with waterlogging reported from Connaught Place, Janpath, several roads in Lutyens’ Delhi, Bharat Mandapam Road, Barakhamba Road, Mathura Road near ITO, Kalindi Kunj and other low-lying areas.

Amid reports of waterlogging from several parts of the city, PWD Minister Parvesh Sahib Singh shared a video on X showing traffic moving smoothly on Minto Bridge.

“Rain is pouring relentlessly, but life on Minto Bridge is moving along at the same pace. The very effort is to ensure that the monsoon remains just a season, not a trouble,” he said.

Large pools of water accumulated at several intersections, slowing traffic and forcing motorists to navigate submerged stretches with caution.

Aam Aadmi Party leader Saurabh Bharadwaj posted a video on X from Sadar Bazar, one of Delhi’s busiest wholesale markets, where rainwater had risen to waist level, forcing schoolchildren, office-goers and shoppers to wade through flooded streets.

“School kids crossing Sadar Bazar ie one of the largest wholesale market in Delhi with rain waterlogged till their waistline.” the opposition leader said on the social media platform.

Dark, overcast skies blanketed the city for most of the morning, with spells of steady rain accompanied by gusty winds. Pedestrians huddled beneath umbrellas and bus shelters while vehicles moved slowly with headlights on as poor visibility.

According to posts shared by social media users, heavy traffic was reported from Greater Kailash-II to Savitri Cinema to Chirag Dilli, Hauz Khas and RK Puram, and from Sangam Vihar to Khanpur via MB Road on both carriageways.

Traffic congestion due to waterlogging was also reported on NH-8 near Shankar Vihar, Zakir Hussain Road, the Delhi Cantt-Naraina Flyover-Mayapuri stretch, ITO, Old Rohtak Road, the Madhuban Chowk-Netaji Subhash Place stretch, Peeragarhi, NH-48 near AIIMS, the Delhi-Noida Road, Kalindi Kunj and Vikas Marg, among other arterial roads.

Between 11:30 a.m. and 2:30 p.m., Pusa recorded the highest rainfall at 80 mm, followed by Janakpuri at 72 mm, Lodi Road at 63.4 mm, Chhatarpur at 57.5 mm, Safdarjung at 51 mm, Ayanagar at 50.1 mm, Narayana at 44 mm, Ridge at 37.3 mm, Mayur Vihar at 33.5 mm and Palam at 26 mm. Jafarpur recorded 8 mm of rainfall, while Najafgarh received no rain during the three-hour period.

The minimum temperature at Safdarjung settled at 25.5 degrees Celsius, 1.8 notches below normal.

Palam recorded 25 degrees Celsius, 2.1 notches below normal, while Lodi Road recorded 25.8 degrees Celsius, 0.2 notch below normal. The Ridge station recorded a minimum of 23.2 degrees Celsius, 2.3 notches below normal, while Ayanagar recorded 27.1 degrees Celsius, 1.1 notches above normal.

World.title: Women’s outfits hold protest in Delhi seeking unconditional implementation of 33% quota
World.content:
Various women’s organisations under the banner of ‘National Coalition for Women’s Reservation’ on Friday (August 7, 2026) staged a demonstration in the national capital demanding the unconditional implementation of the Women’s Reservation Bill during the current Monsoon session of Parliament.

Women from various parts of Delhi and neighbouring States gathered in large numbers for the protest, demanding that the Women’s Reservation Bill be implemented without conditions attached to it.

The Constitution (106th Amendment) Bill, popularly known as the Women’s Reservation Bill or the ‘Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam’, was passed in September 2023. The law stipulates that 33% reservation for women will come into effect only after the first census conducted following the commencement of the Act and the subsequent delimitation exercise, with implementation from the election held after that process is completed. The NDA government is currently holding talks with various Opposition parties for a consensus on the passage of the Delimitation Bill.

Addressing the protest, All India Progressive Women’s Association (AIPWA) national secretary Shweta Raj highlighted a stark contradiction as on one hand, a large number of women have had their names removed from the electoral rolls, while on the other, the BJP-led government is stalling the path for granting 33% reservation to women.

“The BJP government aims to foster communal polarisation across the country by linking the Women’s Reservation Bill to delimitation; the elections in Assam and Jammu & Kashmir are recent examples of this,” she said according to a statement.

At this juncture, there is a need for the entire country to unite and demand the unconditional implementation of the Women’s Reservation Bill, and for it to be enacted during this Monsoon session of Parliament itself, the statement added.

World.title: Mehbooba Mufti calls for J&K-wide protest on August 5; says ‘meaningful engagement only way forward’
World.content:
Jammu & Kashmir Opposition Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) president Mehbooba Mufti, while speaking on the party’s 27th Foundation Day in Srinagar on Tuesday (July 28, 2026), said meaningful democratic engagement among all stakeholders is the only sustainable path towards lasting peace and stability in the region.

Ms. Mufti also called for Jammu & Kashmir-wide protests on August 5, the anniversary of the Centre’s move to end Jammu & Kashmir’s autonomous status, to press for the demand of the restoration of Article 370.

“PDP’s core philosophy is ‘Peace with Dignity’. Dialogue, reconciliation, confidence-building and meaningful democratic engagement among all stakeholders is the only sustainable path towards lasting peace and stability in the region,” said Ms. Mufti.

The PDP unanimously adopted a political resolution on the occasion and pledged to follow the ideals of its founder Mufti Mohammad Sayeed. It called for “continued democratic struggle for the restoration of Article 370, Article 35A and the constitutional guarantees, which protected the unique identity and special status of Jammu & Kashmir”.

The resolution also demanded the immediate release of political prisoners and detainees, “an end to the misuse of preventive detention laws, and the restoration of democratic rights, civil liberties and the rule of law”.

“At a time when J&K is passing through one of the most difficult phases in its contemporary history, the party renewed its resolve to pursue peaceful, democratic and constitutional means to safeguard the rights, identity, dignity and aspirations of its people,” said the resolution.

The party said it will also work towards “reopening historic roads, Cross-LoC routes, and traditional trade and travel links with the objective of transforming J&K into a bridge connecting South and Central Asia”.

The PDP also called for the dignified return, rehabilitation and secure resettlement of Kashmiri Pandits and all other displaced communities. It also pledged to work towards greater administrative justice for the Pir Panjal and Chenab regions, and enhanced political representation and empowerment of women.

SC upholds abrogation of Article 370, says move was part of 70-year-old exercise to integrate J&K to the Union

Meanwhile, Ms. Mufti clarified the recent remarks, which sparked protests from the ruling National Conference and other parties in Jammu & Kashmir. “I said there is militancy and intended to say ‘Bahana Banta Hain’, but I could not utter the word ‘Bahana’. I apologise to the people of J&K if my misconstrued statement hurt their sentiments,” said Ms. Mufti.

She accused the NC leaders of “always complaining to Delhi about my statements, which forces them to take a position on serious issues in Kashmir”.

Meanwhile, NC leader and legislator Tanvir Sadiq said, “There is no ‘if’ or ‘but’ here. People across J&K were appalled by your statement. The only appropriate response is a clear and unconditional apology to every Kashmiri who was hurt, especially the victims of pellet injuries. Everything else said today was simply an attempt to divert attention from the real issue: your original remarks,” said Mr. Sadiq.

World.title: Nurses stage protest in Krishnagiri against redeployment order
World.content:
Nursing staff of the Government Medical College Hospital here staged protests inside the hospital, demanding that the government revoke an order for the redeployment of nursing staff from new medical college hospitals to other institutions.

G.O. 204 ordered the redeployment of 20 staff nurses from Krishnagiri Government Medical College Hospital to Government Mohan Kumaramangalam Medical College Hospital, Salem.

Similarly, a bunch of nursing staff are being redeployed from smaller new medical college hospitals to large medical college hospitals.

The protesters, who wore black badges, also demanded dismantling of contractual jobs and regularise all nursing staff currently under contractual employment.

The protesters also demanded that the term staff nurse be replaced with Nursing Officer and a G.O. be released describing the job description.

World.title: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Turkiye sign tripartite defence agreement in Makkah
World.content:
Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye on Friday signed a joint defence pact in Makkah that empowers member states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.

The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, which seeks to strengthen the collective security of the three states, was signed by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Saudi Crown Prince and PM Mohammad bin Salman, and Türkiye’s President Recep Tayyip Erdogan at the “Makkah Al-Mukarramah Summit for Joint Defence” held at Al-Safa Palace.

The three countries announced the signing of the agreement in a joint statement published by the Foreign Office (FO) and Saudi Arabia’s official SPA press agency.

The statement said the pact reflected the three countries’ “shared commitment to further strengthening their collective security and to promoting peace, security, and stability in the region and beyond, in pursuit of a secure and prosperous future”.

“The agreement is intended to strengthen collective deterrence against any act of aggression, and stipulates that any armed attack against any one of the three states shall be regarded as an attack against them all.”

It also “provides for the enhancement of all aspects of defence cooperation” among the three countries, the statement added.

The agreement is “guided by the longstanding historical ties among the three states, based on the enduring bonds of brotherhood and Islamic solidarity that unite them, and building upon their shared strategic interests and longstanding defence cooperation”.

During the Makkah Al-Mukarramah Summit for Joint Defence, the “distinguished relations” between the three countries were reviewed, “along with a number of issues of mutual interest”, the statement noted.

Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, Deputy PM and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, and Defence Minister Khawaja Asif were also present at the signing ceremony.

The defence and foreign ministers of Saudi Arabia and Turkiye were in attendance as well, pictures showed.

Sealing the agreement in Makkah, the holiest site in Islam, adds symbolic heft to a pact that builds on longstanding bilateral military ties among the three countries.

The agreement ties together Pakistan, the only nuclear-armed Muslim country; Saudi Arabia, the home to Islam’s holiest sites and one of the world’s top oil exporters; and Turkiye, Nato’s second-largest military.

‘Historic day for Pakistan’

Information Minister Attaullah Tarar, while talking to a private TV channel, described the signing of the joint defence agreement between the three states as a “historic day” for Pakistan, saying the pact reflected growing recognition of the country’s defence capabilities and strengthened ties among the three nations.

Speaking about the agreement, Tarar said the defence cooperation framework would take relations between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye to a new level. He credited Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Field Marshal Asim Munir with bringing the three countries together, saying they had an “ideal working relationship” and that their teamwork had contributed to recent successes.

Tarar said the agreement was aimed at strengthening defence cooperation and served as a form of deterrence rather than aggression. The minister further said Pakistan’s capabilities had been demonstrated during last year’s conflict with India and claimed that the country had since played a role in promoting regional peace.

Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan said that the signing of the joint defence agreement by the crown prince, the president of Türkiye and the prime minister of Pakistan underscored the depth of the fraternal and strategic relations between the three countries.

He said the agreement marked an important milestone in their defence cooperation and reflected their shared desire to coordinate efforts to address challenges and threats affecting regional security and stability. He added that the pact embodied the three countries’ shared political will to safeguard security, support a more secure regional environment and pave the way for greater development and prosperity.

Saudi Arabia’s Deputy Minister for Public Diplomacy Rayed Krimly said the agreement “does not represent an effort to establish a military axis or a sectarian bloc”.

“Nor is it linked to any nuclear ambitions or arms race; rather, it is focused on building sustainable capabilities,” he wrote on X.

He noted that the deal “does not constitute a threat to the security of any country in the region, nor does it represent an escalation of tensions between any two states”.

The Saudi official further said the agreement “does not supersede or replace any existing bilateral or multilateral agreements between these countries”.

Mansoor Ahmed, of the Australian National University’s Strategic and Defence Studies Centre, said Islamabad and Ankara bring strong defence industries to the table, while Riyadh could contribute with technological spending.

While the pact comes in the backdrop of the US-Israel war on Iran, Bloomberg had reported in January — before the conflict began — that Ankara was seeking to join a separate mutual defence pact between Islamabad and Riyadh.

Pakistan and Saudi Arabia had already signed the “ Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement ” in Riyadh last September, pledging that any attack on either nation would be treated as an act of aggression against both.

In January, Reuters quoted Defence Production Minister Raza Hayat Harraj as saying that a draft had been prepared after 10 months of talks. Turkish FM Hakan Fidan had said Ankara favoured an “inclusive platform that creates wider, bigger cooperation and stability”.

Pakistan has also sought to mediate efforts to end the US-Iran war, while Turkiye has played a diplomatic role in negotiations aimed at ending the war in Gaza.

The three countries, along with Egypt, have been closely involved in efforts to promote regional stability and contain the regional upheaval sparked by the US-Iran war.

The regional conflagration has rained missile fire onto Gulf oil exporters, with Iran targeting Gulf countries in retaliation for attacks carried out against it using US military bases in the region.

The deal also comes as a 2022 truce between Riyadh and the Houthi rebels in Yemen has broken down.

After the two sides traded fire for the first time in years last month, Houthis declared a maritime blockade against the kingdom, threatening access to its ports, and has claimed to have attacked Saudi tankers in the Red Sea.

Pakistan had condemned the Houthis’ threats to Saudi Arabia and to trading with the kingdom via the Red Sea. It also warned that it had the right to self-defence if its “maritime interests” were targeted in “any hostile act”.

As the conflict expanded onto new fronts, Saudi Arabia last week unveiled plans for a multinational maritime defence coalition to protect shipping and energy supply routes in the Red Sea. Fourteen countries, including Pakistan, have voiced support for the coalition.

Saudi crown prince meets PM Shehbaz, Erdogan

Crown Prince Salman held separate meetings with PM Shehbaz and President Erdogan at the Al-Safa Palace earlier in the day.

DPM Dar, CDF Munir and Asif were also present in the meeting with PM Shehbaz, the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said.

Meanwhile, Erdogan’s office confirmed on X that he also held a meeting with Crown Prince Salman.

PM Shehbaz arrived in Saudi Arabia on a three-day visit on Thursday, while the Turkish president undertook a one-day visit today, Anadolu Agency reported.

Erdogan landed at King Abdulaziz International Airport in Jeddah, from where he departed for Makkah by road, the Turkish news outlet reported.

PM Shehbaz had landed in Jeddah on Thursday. CDF Munir later joined the Pakistani delegation, which also included Information Minister Attaullah Tarar and Special Assistant to PM Tariq Fatemi.

On Friday morning, the delegation visited the Holy Kaaba and performed Umrah, the PMO said. PM Shehbaz is also expected to visit Masjid-i-Nabvi (PBUH) in Madina.

According to an earlier statement by the FO, discussions between the two sides were to “focus on consolidating the Pakistan-Saudi bilateral relations as well as exchange of views on regional and international developments of mutual interests”.

The FO had noted that although the visit was taking place amid heightened tensions in the Gulf, it carries “significance beyond the immediate crises and short-term considerations”.

It said the visit will “further strengthen bilateral relations, deepen strategic cooperation, enhance coordination on regional and international issues of mutual interest, and reinforce multilateral cooperation”.

“The visit marks Pakistan’s long-standing partnership with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia anchored in decades of mutual trust, cooperation and brotherhood,” the FO had emphasised.

Pakistan has provided training and technical assistance to Saudi forces for decades, while Turkiye and Pakistan have exchanged warships and training aircraft.

In 2023, Riyadh agreed to buy Turkish drones in what Ankara called its largest defence export contract. In April this year, Saudi Arabia said it received a military force and fighter jets from Pakistan to boost the kingdom’s security.

Additional input from AFP and Reuters

World.title: Bilawal claims 'certain elements' within PML-N are sowing division among allies, undermining PM Shehbaz
World.content:
PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari claimed on Friday that certain elements within the ruling PML-N were undermining Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and sowing discord between him and his political allies.

The PPP and the PML-N have been engaged in a war of words since the latter emerged in the lead in Mirpur polls on July 27. The PML-N has also won the majority of the seats in the second phase , with the PPP accusing it of rigging and other violent tactics in both phases.

The PPP chief was addressing an election rally in Azad Jammu and Kashmir’s Poonch district, where the third phase of elections in the region is slated to be held.

“High-profile people are saying that the government has collapsed. I’m not saying that, nor am I casting doubt on the prime minister’s intentions. He’s a good man with good intentions. But what can he do when the people around him have bad intentions?” Bilawal asked.

In reference to remarks he made earlier this week, the party chief highlighted that the PPP did not start the “countdown” to the government’s collapse, but rather these elements within the ruling party.

“The PML-N’s fight is not with the PPP — it happens in elections, as it has before. The real fight is entirely different, because the PM, with his good intentions and actions, is undermined by a large part of the PML-N,” Bilawal alleged.

“A big part of the PML-N wants the PM to fight not only the opposition, but also his own allies.”

He then asked the audience: “Have there ever been elections held in six phases in Kashmir’s history? If Kashmir is one, then the election should have been held on a single day.”

Bilawal said the elections were being held in phases “so that there is calm and the elections are peaceful, free and fair”, before asking: “But in which phase were the elections free, fair or peaceful?”

“In truth, elections were carried out in phases so they could rig them. They knew that 10 seats were in their pocket from the start,” he alleged.

“With the 10 seats in their pocket, they robbed Mirpur, they robbed Muzaffarabad, and they’re looking at you, in Poonch. They are looking at Bagh. On August 10, they will find out that those in Poonch and Bagh hunt tigers.”

Elections are being held across AJK in three phases . Polls in Mirpur and Muzaffarabad divisions were held on July 27 and August 2, respectively.

The first phase of polling in Mirpur saw the PML-N secure nine of the 13 seats while the PPP won the remaining four.

In the second phase in Muzaffarabad, the PML-N bagged 15 more seats, while the PPP managed to add just six more to its tally.

The third phase in Poonch division was set for August 10. Poonch Division comprises 11 constituencies — three in Bagh, one in Haveli, five in Poonch and two in Sudhnoti district.

However, earlier today, the AJK Election Commission revised the schedule for the third phase of elections in the region, saying polling would only be held in Poonch Division’s Bagh and Haveli districts on August 10 amid concerns over the law and order situation.

The electoral process in the constituencies of Poonch district and Sudhnoti’s Pallandri would not be held on August 10, the Election Commission said, adding that it reviewed the “current situation” regarding the scheduled elections in Poonch.

It noted that according to a report it received from the AJK home secretary, there were “concerns over the law and order situation in some areas of Poonch district and Pallandri district”.

The commission’s decision comes in the wake of clashes that took place between protesters and law enforcement personnel in Poonch district’s Rawalakot on July 27, which reportedly resulted in several casualties.

Rawalakot has been gripped by unrest since early June , with the proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) staging sit-ins periodically.

The JAAC, which has been demanding the abolishment of 12 seats in the local legislature reserved for refugees from Indian-held Kashmir, has been holding protests in the region for several weeks now.

World.title: SCBA backs call for new provinces, calls it 'step forward' for better governance
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) — a premier lawyers’ body — on Friday voiced support for the controversial proposal recently put forward by Interior Minister Syed Mohsin Naqvi regarding the creation of new provinces in the country.

Recently, while addressing the Pakistan Economic Summit 2026, the interior minister had urged all political parties to resolve various national issues, including the question of creating new provinces. He termed this the only solution to improving the country’s overall condition, which he said had “collapsed”.

Speaking at the Full Court Reference held at the Supreme Court (SC) in honour of Justice Musarrat Hilali on the occasion of her laying down her judicial robes, SCBA President Haroonur Rashid said the association endorsed and supported the suggestion to create new provinces.

Headed by Chief Justice of Pakistan (CJP) Yahya Afridi, the reference was attended by SC judges both in person and via video link.

The reference was also attended by Additional Attorney General (AAG) Chaudhry Aamir Rehman, representatives of the SCBA and the Pakistan Bar Council (PBC), senior members of the legal fraternity, court officers, media representatives and others.

“The association believes that any constitutional measure for the creation of more provinces would be a step forward towards an enhanced governance system through devolved and equitable administration at the grassroots level, the creation of equal opportunities for parallel economic development, and stronger political stability in the country,” the SCBA president said.

He added that the creation of more provinces would also improve the standard of living by addressing the economic challenges faced by the people of the country.

Meanwhile, in its 250th meeting held in Islamabad on Friday, the PBC — the apex body of the legal fraternity — said it firmly believed that all constitutional matters must be addressed strictly within the framework of the Constitution.

The PBC deliberated upon the issue of the creation of new administrative units and provinces in the country. It reaffirmed through a resolution that the legal fraternity was committed to upholding the Constitution, and that members were of the unanimous view that the question of creating new provinces should be considered in accordance with the constitutional principles and procedures.

The resolution emphasised that all political parties, irrespective of their political differences, should act in the “larger national interest” and initiate a “comprehensive and meaningful dialogue” for the betterment of the country and its people.

The PBC resolved that, if the establishment of new provinces was deemed necessary, it must be carried out strictly in accordance with the Constitution through due parliamentary process and national consensus.

The PBC also authorised its Vice Chairman Pir Muhammad Masood Chishti and the chairman of its Executive Committee to organise a national seminar by inviting leaders of all political parties represented in Parliament, as well as representatives of provincial bar councils, for meaningful dialogue and to develop a broad-based national consensus. The seminar would aim to strengthen the federation, promote good governance, ensure equitable administrative and economic development, and improve the welfare of the common man.

On the other hand, the SCBA president said the association would continue supporting the 26th and 27th Constitutional Amendments.

He said the association believed that the amendments were an “important step towards ensuring parliamentary sovereignty, enhancing the separation of powers, and realising the concept that the judiciary should focus more on its fundamental constitutional responsibility of prompt dispensation of justice”.

He also requested President Asif Ali Zardari to immediately give his assent to the recent appointment and confirmation of the high court judges recommended by the Judicial Commission of Pakistan (JCP) during its meeting on July 20 and 21.

“SCBA believes that the appointment procedure adopted through the recent amendments were more balanced, comprehensive and transparent, since both the members of the judiciary and the Parliament were part of such a judicial process,” he said.

Rashid also expressed his trust and confidence in the performance of the JCP, saying that its recent decisions regarding the appointment of judges to the high courts were based on merit, as “competent individuals” had been recommended for the highest judicial offices.

Therefore, pendency in the grant of assent by the president may result in harming the Constitution as well as the interests of the country, he said.

During the reference, the AAG, SCBA president and PBC vice chairman paid rich tributes to Justice Hilali’s professional integrity, judicial acumen and unwavering commitment to the administration of justice. They acknowledged the respect and admiration she earned across the bench and the bar through her principled conduct, independence and distinguished service, and conveyed their heartfelt best wishes for the next chapter of her life.

In his address, CJP Afridi paid tribute to Justice Hilali, describing her judicial journey as one defined by “courage, perseverance and an unwavering commitment to justice”.

He observed that her career was remarkable not only for the high judicial offices she held, but also for the barriers she broke and the enduring example she set for generations of lawyers, particularly women aspiring to leadership roles within the legal profession.

“Justice Hilali’s career stands as a beacon of the growing participation and leadership of women in Pakistan’s justice sector,” Afridi said.

Her professional journey, he noted, demonstrated that integrity, dedication and professional excellence remained the “true hallmarks of judicial leadership” and could inspire future generations of women to pursue careers of distinction in law and justice.

The CJP also acknowledged Justice Hilali’s valuable contributions to strengthening the principles of judicial responsibility, institutional integrity, and public service throughout her tenure.

PBC condemns NCCIA’s detaining of Islamabad-based journalists

The PBC, in its Friday meeting, also strongly condemned the actions of the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) in issuing notices to and detaining Islamabad-based journalists under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca).

The council demanded that the government should immediately withdraw all such illegal notices and refrain from any actions that undermine the constitutional guarantees of freedom of expression and freedom of the press.

“The legal fraternity has always stood in support of an independent and free media as a fundamental pillar of democracy and the rule of law, and will continue to oppose any attempt to intimidate, harass, or curtail the independence of the media,” it said.

World.title: Power consumers to pay 75 paisa per unit FCA in August bills
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (Nepra) on Friday notified an additional burden of Rs9.8 billion on electricity consumers for the August billing period due to a fuel cost adjustment (FCA) of 75 paisa per unit.

The net average fuel cost in August would be around 41 paisa per unit higher than in July, when the FCA stood at Rs0.34 per unit.

In its notification, Nepra said it had decided that the positive FCA for June 2026, amounting to Rs0.7503 per kWh, would apply to all consumer categories that opted for prepaid tariffs, except lifeline consumers, electric vehicle charging stations and prepaid electricity consumers.

The adjustment applies to K-Electric (KE) as well as power distribution companies (Discos) that originated from Wapda.

The regulator said the adjustment would also apply to consumers under the incremental consumption package. Discos and KE are required to reflect the fuel charges adjustment for June 2026 in the billing month of August 2026.

The FCA is reviewed every month as per the tariff regime applicable across the country and is usually applicable to the consumer’s bills for one month only.

The Central Power Purchasing Agency (CPPA) had reported that the actual average fuel charges component for June 2026 was Rs8.9138/kWh, compared with the reference fuel charges component of Rs7.7138/kWh approved in the applicable notified consumer-end tariff.

Accordingly, it had demanded Rs1.20 per unit additional FCA for June 2026.

After certain adjustments, Nepra worked out the actual fuel component of the tariff at Rs8.4641, thereby allowing a lower FCA of Rs0.75 per unit in August instead of Rs1.20.

The power division and its entities had reported a 5.6 per cent decline in overall generation in June compared to the projected level.

Nepra expressed concern over partial loading charges amounting to Rs4.9 billion.

CPPA, however, argued that these charges were not due to operational inefficiencies but resulted from reduced daytime demand caused by rooftop solar generation.

Power plants were operated at partial load during solar hours and ramped up later to meet the evening increase in grid demand.

The power division warned that renewable power sources, such as wind and solar, may need to be curtailed in the future if daytime demand declines significantly in the coming years.

Under the tariff mechanism, changes in fuel cost are passed on to consumers only on a monthly basis through the automatic mechanism.

On the other hand, quarterly tariff adjustments — based on variation in power purchase price, capacity charges, variable operation and maintenance costs, use of system charges and impact of transmission and distribution losses — are built in the base tariff by the federal government.

Last week, the government indicated that it was working on another power tariff package as it sought about Rs1.20 per unit additional fuel cost from consumers to collect Rs15.7 billion in August for electricity consumed in June.

World.title: JI protests cause traffic disruptions across Karachi
World.content:
Several major thoroughfares in Karachi were blocked or affected by traffic disruptions on Friday as Jamaat-i-Islami held protest sit-ins in the city as part of a nationwide demonstration against the petroleum levy.

A day earlier, the party announced that it would stage sit-ins at 510 locations across the country by blocking major roads.

In a traffic advisory issued, the Karachi traffic police warned that traffic flow could be affected due to the protests and sit-ins, with slow-moving traffic, temporary diversions and partial road closures expected on several major thoroughfares.

The affected areas included Mazar-i-Quaid, Numaish Chowrangi, Saddar, Sharea Faisal, Sharae Pakistan, UP Mor, Power House Chowrangi, Defence Housing Authority, Sea View, Shahrah-i-Orangi, Hub River Road, Super Highway and National Highway.

The traffic police advised citizens to avoid travelling to the affected areas unless necessary, and urged them to select alternative routes and allow extra travel time before setting out.

Meanwhile, according to the latest updates shared on JI Karachi’s official X account, party workers had begun staging sit-ins at the announced locations.

According to the updates, workers had blocked the road leading to Natha Khan from Sharea Faisal. The Super Highway and Hub River Road were also blocked. Moreover, the road leading from Sharea Faisal Nursery Bus Stop to Airport had also been blocked.

‘Fuel for political point-scoring’

Responding to the protest, Sindh government spokesperson Sadia Javed said the petroleum levy was a federal matter and questioned why Karachi’s citizens were being “punished” through road closures.

“Jamaat-i-Islami is using the protest to score political points instead of serving the public,” she alleged, adding that the party should focus on the performance of its local government representatives to improve conditions for Karachi’s residents.

She said it was unacceptable for a few hundred protesters to hold a city of millions hostage by disrupting traffic and daily life, adding that such politics should come to an end.

“Blocking roads does not serve the public; instead, it adds to their difficulties,” Javed said, questioning how ambulances and patients could reach hospitals when major roads were closed.

“If Jamaat-i-Islami is sincere in its concerns, it should raise the matter at the relevant forums and in Parliament rather than resorting to protests that disrupt public life,” she said.

Javed also warned that the party should not use Karachi’s residents as “fuel for political point-scoring” and stressed that authorities would not allow anyone to take the law into their own hands, block roads or damage public property under the guise of protest.

Other parts of country

Meanwhile, JI workers also gathered at the designated sit-in locations in other provincial capitals, including Lahore, Quetta, Peshawar and Islamabad.

According to reports, Srinagar Highway had been blocked as protesters gathered at Golra Mor to march towards Chungi 26.

In Sindh, protesters also staged sit-ins in Thatta, Matiari, Tando Allahyar, Shikarpur and other districts.

World.title: US to vet social media of foreign journalists applying for visas, report says
World.content:
The US State Department will ​vet the social media accounts of foreign journalists applying for visas to work in the United ‌States, according to a media report on Thursday.

The report in the conservative news outlet The Daily Signal cited an internal memo that said an initiative by President Donald Trump’s administration that requires applicants for many visa types to make their social media accounts public ​for screening was being expanded to include foreign media representatives.

Applicants for another type of visa for ​workers from Canada and Mexico also will now be included in the screening, it said.

The ⁠White House and the State Department’s official accounts on X shared a link to the article, but the ​State Department declined to confirm the specifics of the report, citing a policy of not commenting on “purported internal documents”.

A ​State Department spokesperson said that what the department calls “online presence vetting” is used to ensure that applicants are eligible for a visa under US law.

“The Department of State is screening and vetting to the maximum extent possible every foreign national seeking admission to ​the United States to ensure they will respect US law including the terms of their admission and do ​not pose a threat to US security, public safety or national interests,” the spokesperson said.

“Officers use a variety of methods to ‌make ⁠informed decisions that protect national security, prevent fraud and ensure a thorough review of applicants,” the spokesperson added.

It was unclear when the reported new policy would take effect.

The Department of Homeland Security tightened rules last month around how long foreign journalists working in the United States, as well as other visa holders including foreign students, could remain in ​the country.

It also builds ​on a series of ⁠steps that Trump’s administration has taken since he began his second term in taking office in January 2025 to make online speech a factor in immigration and visa decisions. ​These steps have raised concerns among civil liberties advocates about freedom of speech.

US Citizenship ​and Immigration Services ⁠has said it will screen the social media posts of immigrants and visa applicants, including for what it deems antisemitic content and “anti-Americanism”. The administration has canceled the visas of foreign students in the US who engaged in pro-Palestinian activism, ⁠in some cases attempting to ​deport those students.

The State Department said in October 2025 that it ​revoked the visas of six foreign nationals over comments about the assassination of conservative activist Charlie Kirk, and said it would continue identifying visa ​holders it believed had celebrated the killing.

World.title: Domestic, foreign investors show interest in Fesco privatisation: privatisation commission
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Privatisation Commission (PC) on Friday said it had received a strong response from domestic and international investors for the privatisation of Faisalabad Electric Supply Company (Fesco).

The commission said it had received 12 expressions of interest (EOIs) from prospective investors seeking to acquire a 51pc to 100pc stake in Fesco along with management control.

The EOIs were submitted by three Turkish investors, one Chinese investor and eight local investors.

The three from Turkiye include Aktor Elektrik Enerji Yatırımları San. ve Tic. A.Ş., Genvera Enerji A.Ş. (Celik Group) and ⁠Cengiz Enerji Sanayii ve Ticaret A.Ş.

The EOI from China came from Jiang Xi Electric Power Construction.

The remaining eight Pakistani groups include Engro Energy Limited, Sapphire Fibers Limited, Hub Power Holdings, Lucky Cement, Shirazi Investments (Pvt) Limited (Atlas Group), Maple Leaf Cement and Kohinoor Textile, Nishat Mills Limited and Pak Elektron Ltd, and Artistic Milliners (Private) Limited and K-Electric Limited.

The Privatisation Commission welcomed the interest shown by leading business groups in entering the power distribution sector and appreciated the investor community’s extensive engagement during domestic and international roadshows over the past six months.

“This is an important milestone in the privatisation of Discos,” said Muhammad Ali, PC chairman and adviser to the prime minister on privatisation.

“The strong response to Fesco reflects investor confidence in the potential of Pakistan’s electricity distribution sector and in the government’s commitment to a transparent, competitive and professionally managed process.”

He further added that the commission “looks forward to engaging constructively with the prequalified investors through the due diligence process and discussing the contours of the post-privatisation regime”.

The privatisation of Discos would “improve operational efficiency, modernise distribution infrastructure, strengthen customer service, reduce losses and support a more financially sustainable power sector”, the PC chairman said.

“Over time, these measures will help create the conditions for more competitive electricity distribution and affordable, reliable power for consumers,” he added.

In the next stage of the process, the EOIs and Statements of Qualification (SOQs) submitted by interested parties will undergo a comprehensive evaluation against the approved prequalification criteria.

Applicants meeting the prescribed requirements will be invited to the next stage of the transaction, where they will be granted access to the Virtual Data Room (VDR) to conduct detailed buy-side due diligence.

Fesco is among the three electricity distribution companies in Disco Batch-I privatisation, alongside Gujranwala Electric Power Company (GEPCO) and Islamabad Electric Supply Company (IESCO).

The three are considered the most viable Discos among the 11 electricity distribution companies originally carved out of the Water and Power Development Authority (Wapda) in 1998.

The deadlines for submission of EOIs for Gepco and Iesco are August 21 and September 7, 2026, respectively.

PC said it would ensure an open, transparent and competitive privatisation process, undertaken in the public interest and in support of the federal government’s wider power-sector reform agenda.

World.title: Schedule for 3rd phase of AJK polls revised over law and order concerns
World.content:
The Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) Election Commission on Friday revised the schedule for the third phase of elections in the region, saying polling would only be held in Poonch Division’s Bagh and Haveli districts on August 10 amid concerns over the law and order situation.

Elections are being held across AJK in three phases amid tensions between protesters and the authorities. Polls in Mirpur and Muzaffarabad divisions were held on July 27 and August 2, respectively.

The third phase in Poonch division was set for August 10. Poonch Division comprises 11 constituencies — three in Bagh, one in Haveli, five in Poonch and two in Sudhnoti district.

However, the Election Commission said in a press release on Friday that the electoral process will go ahead as planned on August 10 in only the division’s Bagh and Haveli districts.

In its press release, the AJK Election Commission said polling will be held in the three constituencies of Bagh and one of Haveli on August 10 as per the previous schedule.

However, the electoral process in the constituencies of Poonch district and Sudhnoti’s Pallandri will not be held on August 10, it said. The Election Commission said it reviewed the “current situation” regarding the scheduled elections in Poonch.

It noted that according to a report it received from the AJK home secretary, there were “concerns over the law and order situation in some areas of Poonch district and Pallandri district”.

“Moreover, the Election Commission received requests from some political personalities and candidates hailing from these districts, in which it has been requested to postpone the elections in Poonch district and Pallandri district considering the current situation,” the press release read.

The electoral watchdog said it will announce the new polling dates and a revised election schedule for Poonch and Pallandri after reviewing the situation and “considering all relevant matters”.

The commission clarified that the decision to postpone some of the polls was taken “only in the context of the current law and order situation to ensure that elections are held in a free, fair, transparent and peaceful environment”.

The Election Commission’s decision comes in the wake of clashes that took place between protesters and law enforcement personnel in Poonch district’s Rawalakot on July 27, which reportedly resulted in several casualties.

Rawalakot has been gripped by unrest since early June, with the proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) staging sit-ins periodically.

The JAAC, which has been demanding the abolishment of 12 seats in the local legislature reserved for refugees from Indian-held Kashmir, has been holding protests in the region for several weeks now.

The government has accused militant elements “pursuing a foreign agenda and backed by Indian funding” of fomenting the unrest.

Earlier this week, AJK Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Ghulam Mustafa Mughal noted that the “law and order situation and the demands of the safety of voters play an important role in holding elections”.

Responding to a question, he had said that under the AJK constitution, the current Legislative Assembly ceases to exist after August 4.

“Even if elections cannot be held in two or a few more constituencies, one cannot say that the house is not complete or those who have returned cannot take oath or perform their functions,” he explained.

He said the new assembly would still take oath after the completion of the August 10 polls.

Election Commission addresses malpractice allegations

On Friday, the Election Commission also responded to allegations of electoral malpractices and rigging, noting that a candidate claimed the previous day that Forms-24 had not been provided to polling agents at some polling stations.

The allegation was made by PPP’s Raja Muhammad Shakeel Khan, which the Election Commission denied.

“The Election Commission has not received any complaint regarding any constituency or polling station till now. The relevant presiding officers provided Forms-24 to polling agents at polling stations in line with law and the electoral practice,” its press release said.

The Election Commission further said some candidates had also tried to create an impression that it allotted election symbols at a matter of its prerogative.

“This impression is baseless and contrary to the facts. The symbols are allotted in accordance with the legal process described under AJK Elections Rules, 2020 and Form-42,” it said, adding that the commission allotted symbols without any bias towards or against any candidate.

PML-N has already won: Rana Sana

Meanwhile, PML-N leader and Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah addressed a public gathering in AJK’s Haveli, where he said his party had already won the required number of seats in AJK and was set to form the government.

He said 23 seats were required for a simple majority in the assembly, while the PML-N had already won 24.

Sanaullah told the rally’s participants that the PML-N would focus on development in AJK, which he said had been witnessed in the past every time the party was in the government in the Centre and AJK at the same time.

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”

At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he could bring the girl to him.

However, police officers present immediately stopped him from speaking further.

Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent.

Earlier in the day, Sohel and Swapna were brought to the lock-up of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka.

Later, Judge Masrur Salekin of the tribunal framed charges against the couple in the case over the rape and murder of Ramisa in Dhaka's Pallabi area.

Both accused pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out, said Bench Assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes.

The judge also fixed tomorrow for the start of the trial, with the victim's father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, scheduled to testify first, he added.

On May 24, Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destruction of evidence and providing false information.

Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial.

Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel.

The following day, Ramisa's father filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person.

According to the case statement, Sohel lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime.

On May 20, police produced Sohel and Swapna before a Dhaka court, and court sources said Sohel agreed to give a confessional statement before a magistrate. The third and unidentified accused was on the run. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid recorded Sohel's confessional statement after police brought him to the magistrate’s chamber, said a court staff member.

Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station told The Daily Star that day, the prime accused had already admitted to the crime during primary interrogation.

On May 22, the Dhaka Bar Association decided not to provide legal assistance to the accused following an emergency virtual meeting of its executive committee, citing the gravity of the allegations.

The next day, the government appointed Supreme Court lawyer Musa Kalimullah as a state defence counsel to represent the accused to ensure a fair trial.

This report has been corrected at 4:43pm. In the earlier version, Sohel Rana’s comment was misreported. We regret the error.

World.title: Why Bangladesh must pivot to renewable energy now
World.content:
There are moments in a nation’s history when a crisis does more than create hardship. It reveals the weakness of an old system and opens the door to a better one. Bangladesh is now standing at such a moment.

The country is facing an energy crisis that no longer centres on power cuts. It is affecting factories, farms, schools, offices, exports, foreign currency reserves, and the daily life of ordinary people. What we are seeing today is not just a temporary shortage of gas or fuel. It is a signal that our energy system has become too dependent on imported fossil fuels.

More than 60 percent of Bangladesh’s energy demand is met through imports. LNG, coal, oil, and other fossil fuels have kept the country running for years, but this dependence has become risky and expensive. Global fuel markets are unstable because of geopolitical tension, supply chain disruption, and price volatility. For a country like Bangladesh, this creates double pressure: fuel supply becomes uncertain while fuel costs keep rising.

The government is now spending more than BDT 200 crore per day in energy subsidies. Annual energy import expenditure remains around USD 12 billion, putting serious pressure on foreign currency reserves. Nearly 70 percent of Bangladesh’s LNG imports come from Qatar. If supply is disrupted, Bangladesh can quickly face a severe shortage. In the power sector, daily gas demand exceeds 2,500 mmcfd, but supply sometimes falls to 850–900 mmcfd. This can create a power generation shortfall of 1,500–1,800 MW. Overall, the daily gas shortage exceeds 1,100 mmcfd, and peak-time electricity shortages may reach nearly 2,000 MW.

Bangladesh also has a weak Strategic Petroleum Reserve. The current reserve capacity is sufficient for only about 35–40 days, well below that of countries such as China and Japan. This makes the national energy system even more vulnerable.

Visual: Teeni and Tuni

The impact is already visible. In the readymade garments sector, gas shortages and load shedding are reducing productivity by 25–30 percent in many cases. This threatens export earnings, foreign currency reserves, and economic stability. The crisis has also reached ordinary households. Although Bangladesh declared 100 percent electrification in 2022, many rural areas still experience 10 to 20 hours of load shedding every day during summer. This affects education, small businesses, agriculture, and people’s dignity.

We have also seen long lines at fuel stations, schools moving online, and offices shortening working hours because of fuel shortages. These are not isolated events. They show how deeply energy insecurity can disturb national life.

Over the last 15 years, electricity tariffs in Bangladesh have been increased on many occasions, including more than 10 rounds of increases at both bulk and retail levels. This path is not sustainable. Fossil-fuel-based electricity depends on imported fuel, global prices, the availability of the dollar, subsidies, and repeated tariff adjustments. Solar power offers a different path. With a one-time investment, solar can provide stable energy for 15–20 years. Once installed, its fuel cost is almost zero.

The economic comparison is clear. A 1 MW HFO-based power plant produces electricity per year at a cost of nearly BDT 190 crore, with much of the cost paid in foreign currency. In contrast, a 5 MW solar project requires a one-time investment of around BDT 25 crore, after which fuel costs are practically zero. Each 1 MW of solar power can save around USD 325,000 per year in foreign currency.

This is why renewable energy should not be discussed solely in technical terms like decarbonisation, emissions, and sustainability. For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Despite Bangladesh’s potential, renewable energy contributes less than 5 percent to power generation, far below the global 30 percent target by 2030. Clear, measurable goals and timelines are essential for effective policy planning and investment decisions.

Renewable energy equipment imports face around 50–60 percent in duties and taxes, hindering local manufacturing growth. Policy reforms that reduce import duties and support local industry can accelerate renewable deployment and reduce dependency on imports.

For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Import duty is usually imposed to protect the local industry. But where local production is not yet significant, a high duty only increases project costs, reduces investment returns, and slows renewable energy expansion. Policy reforms can unlock this potential, making stakeholders feel their efforts directly contribute to progress.

India, Pakistan, Vietnam, and China have expanded solar and wind power by offering low or zero import duties, tax exemptions, and low-interest financing. Many countries have also reduced duties on lithium-ion batteries and energy storage systems. Bangladesh should learn from these examples.

The barriers are clear: high duties and VAT, high financing costs of 10–12 percent or more, limited access to easy loans, slow approval processes, net metering delays, high LC margin, weak Merchant Power Policy, lack of clear policies for rooftop solar, utility-scale solar, floating solar, agrivoltaics, solar irrigation, and hybrid solar-storage, weak local manufacturing, and insufficient grid digitalisation. Addressing these collectively can accelerate Bangladesh's renewable journey, uniting stakeholders in a common goal.

One urgent reform is customs assessment. The current weight-based assessment system does not reflect the actual value of solar equipment. It can create artificial overvaluation and raise duties by three to four times. Bangladesh should shift to transaction-value-based assessment using pro forma or commercial invoice values, in line with international practice and WTO customs valuation principles.

The second urgent reform is the elimination of customs duty on renewable energy equipment. This should apply to Solar PV Module, Photovoltaic Cell, Solar Inverter, DC Cable, Data Logger, Aluminium Mounting Structure, Battery Pack, Battery Cell, BMS Circuit Board, PV DG Controller, Hybrid Controller, Solar Plant Safety Aluminium Walkway Mesh, Safety Accessories, and related components.

Current TTI rates are high. Solar PV Module carries 26.90 percent, Photovoltaic Cell 25.75 percent, Solar Inverter 28.73 percent, DC Cable 58.40 percent, Data Logger 37.25 percent, Aluminium Mounting Structure 58.40 percent, Battery Pack and Battery Cell 58.40 percent, BMS Circuit Board 31.50 percent, pack materials 37.25 percent, PV DG Controller or Hybrid Controller 89.08 percent, and Solar Plant Safety Aluminum Walkway Mesh 37.25 percent.
